# 05_decision: every agent's output

16 full investment cases (8 long, 8 short), each attacked by 2 red-teamers, then a 5-judge panel and a synthesis decision memo. 54 agent results.


## [Build] build:S_services_quality

Cumulative revisions $688M / $0.2B per point = 3.44 points of lifetime profitability revised away in 10 quarters = ~1.4 points/year. 3.44% x $85B = $2.92B of lifetime profit destroyed; $0.69B already recognized; $2.23B remains to be absorbed. Over the ~15 years of remaining contract life (29% complete), that is ~$149M/yr of forward EBITDA already contractually gone.

- **dollars_per_share**: STEP 1 — Baseline. FY25 Power segment: revenue $19,767M, services $13,081M, equipment $6,686M, segment EBITDA $2,902M (14.7%). Implied FY25 services EBITDA margin ~21% ($13,081M x 21% = $2,747M) with equipment at ~2% ($6,686M x 2.3% = $155M); 2,747 + 155 = 2,902, ties to the reported segment EBITDA. Source: FY2025 10-K segment table, 2026-01-29.
STEP 2 — Consensus 2027 services line. Power services grows 8%/yr (required for Power to compound toward the Dec-2025 investor-update 2028 ~$56B target with equipment at 20 GW/yr): $13,081M x 1.08^2 = $15,258M. Margin expands 21% to 24% on volume, price and the revision drag reverting to FY25's $151M. Consensus 2027 Power services EBITDA = $15,258M x 24% = $3,662M.
STEP 3 — Short 2027 services line. CSA revenue +1%/yr (three consecutive periods of -1% actual): $5,412M x 1.01^2 = $5,521M. Transactional +8%/yr (honestly, it IS growing): $7,669M x 1.08^2 = $8,945M. Total $14,466M. Margin 21.5% (0.5pt up on volume, less 1.72pt from the revision drag at $400M/yr vs $151M, less ~0.1pt of mix, less ~0.5pt of already-recognized lifetime profit destruction bleeding forward). Short 2027 Power services EBITDA = $14,466M x 21.5% = $3,110M.
STEP 4 — Gap. $3,662M - $3,110M = $552M of 2027 EBITDA. Round to $550M. Bottom-up cross-check: revenue gap $792M x 22% incremental = $174M, plus margin gap 2.5pts x $14,466M = $362M, total $536M — ties to $552M within 3%.
STEP 5 — Enterprise value at the 25x default. $550M x 25 = $13,750M.
STEP 6 — Per share. $13,750M / 266,333,581 shares = $51.63 per share.
STEP 7 — As a percent of price. $51.63 / $940.33 = 5.49%.
STEP 8 — EPS bridge for the target. $550M pre-tax x (1 - 0.22 normalized tax) = $429M / 266,333,581 = $1.61 of 2027 adjusted EPS. Consensus ~$24.50 becomes $22.89.
STEP 9 — The multiple, which is where the real money is. $940.33 / $24.50 consensus = 38.4x 2027. Apply 29x (still a large premium to the S&P's ~22x — I am removing the annuity premium, not the equipment-franchise growth premium): $22.89 x 29 = $664.
STEP 10 — Decomposition of the $276 of downside. EPS cut at the current 38.4x = $1.61 x 38.4 = $62 (22% of the move). De-rating 38.4x to 29x on $22.89 = 9.4 x $22.89 = $215 (78% of the move). Stated plainly: 78% of this short is multiple compression, 22% is earnings.
- **implied_target**: $664 base case (-29.4% from $940.33). Range on the multiple at my $22.89 of 2027 EPS: 32x = $732 (-22.1%), 29x = $664 (-29.4%), 26x = $595 (-36.7%). On consensus EPS of $24.00 instead of $24.50 the 29x case is $649 (-31.0%); on $25.00 it is $678 (-27.9%). For reference my base sits between the sell-side average target of ~$1,236 and GLJ Research's Sell at $470 (Sep 14 2026); I am materially less aggressive than GLJ because GLJ's case is equipment margin on the 2024-priced order vintage, which is a different and additive argument to mine.
- **key_assumption**: The multiple compresses from ~38.4x 2027 EPS to 29x. This assumption does 78% of the work — far more than any operating number in the case. It requires the market to stop capitalizing $88.5B of services RPO as a proven 20-year annuity and start treating it as a slow-growing, margin-eroding aftermarket book attached to a cyclical equipment business. Secondary assumption, doing most of the remaining work: the CSA profitability revision drag runs ~$400M in 2027 rather than reverting to FY25's $151M.
- **sensitivity**: On the multiple (the assumption that matters). Halve the compression — 38.4x to 33.7x — and the target is $771, only -18.0%; at that point the short barely clears financing and borrow cost over 3-12 months. Double it — 38.4x to 19.6x, i.e. a discount to the S&P — and the target is $449, -52.3%. The entire trade lives in this band, which is an honest admission that this is a sentiment/narrative short dressed in accounting evidence.
On the revision run-rate (the operating assumption). Halve it to $200M/yr: the revision gap versus consensus falls from $249M to $49M, the total 2027 EBITDA gap falls to $350M, which is $32.85/share (3.49% of $940.33), 2027 EPS becomes $23.48, and at 29x the target is $681 (-27.6%). Double it to $800M/yr: the gap rises to $950M, $89.17/share (9.48%), 2027 EPS $21.72, and at 29x the target is $630 (-33.0%). Note how little the target moves — from $681 to $630 across a 4x swing in the operating assumption. That is the tell: the earnings case is real but small, and it is doing almost none of the lifting.
On CSA growth. If CSA revenue reaccelerates to +6%/yr instead of +1%, the revenue gap closes from $792M to $234M and the total EBITDA gap falls to roughly $430M — $40.37/share, 4.29%.
- **dated_test**: October 28, 2026 — GEV Q3'26 earnings and the Q3'26 10-Q, Note 9. Three numbers publish simultaneously and all three are on the record before anyone can argue about them. (1) Nine-month 2026 net unfavorable changes in estimated profitability: my case needs at least $290M cumulative, i.e. Q3'26 of at least $72M, at least 5% of Q3 CSA revenue. (2) Nine-month 2026 CSA billings: my case needs $3,700M or less, versus 9M'25 of $3,781M — a third consecutive quarter of year-over-year decline in the physical cash meter. (3) Services RPO at Sep-30-26 and its one-year bucket: my case needs $90.5B or less with the one-year bucket at 16%, i.e. forward-twelve-month contracted services of roughly $14.5B, up 5% or less on the $13.8B implied at Sep-30-25.
An earlier and cheaper partial test exists: GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, and adjusted EPS is driven by equipment volume and Electrification, not by Note 9. So the Oct 28 print can go against the position on day one even if all three of my numbers confirm. Size for that.
CRITICAL SCHEDULING PROBLEM FOR THE TEAM: Oct 28 is after the Oct 22-24 finals. This case has no dated test that resolves inside the competition window. If the judges ask "what proves you right and when," the honest answer is "five weeks after this presentation." Weigh that against the LONG when choosing sides on Sep 26.
- **kill_condition**: Kill the short if the Q3'26 10-Q (Oct 28 2026) shows BOTH of the following: nine-month 2026 net unfavorable changes in estimated profitability of $240M or less (implying Q3'26 of $22M or less, a return to the FY25 run-rate of 2.8% or less of CSA revenue), AND nine-month 2026 CSA billings of $3,900M or more (+3.1% year over year, the first growth in two years). Together those two would establish that H1'26 was a discrete true-up rather than a trend and that the cash meter has reinflected — both legs of the case die at once.
Second, independent kill: services RPO at Sep-30-26 above $95B with the one-year bucket disclosed at 17% or higher. That implies forward-twelve-month contracted services of $16.2B or more, up 17%+ on the $13.8B implied a year earlier, which would mean the annuity is inflecting with the equipment book and the premium multiple is earned. Cover immediately.
Third, thesis-invalidating disclosure: if GEV discloses on the Oct 28 call or in the Q3'26 10-Q that CSAs attached to the 53 GW firm backlog are excluded from services RPO until commissioning and quantifies that excluded book at more than roughly $30B, pillar 3 collapses and the case should be reduced to pillars 1, 2 and 4 alone — which is $250M of EBITDA, $23.47/share, 2.5%. Not a short.
- **weakest_link**: Four places, ranked by how much they hurt.
1. Seventy-eight percent of the downside is multiple compression, and a 38x multiple in a power-shortage bull market does not compress because of a footnote in Note 9. The stock fell ~20% from its late-June $1,196 peak on the lowest volume in 14 months — that is drift, not repricing. There is no forcing mechanism in the horizon that makes a generalist read the CSA rollforward. I can be entirely right about the services book and lose money for four quarters while the equipment cycle prints.
2. Services RPO excludes contracts that are not yet active — GEV's own FY2025 10-K says services RPO includes life-of-contract sales from long-term service agreements "excluding contracts that are not yet active." If GEV signs CSAs at equipment order but books them into RPO only at commissioning, then flat services RPO through a doubling equipment book is a disclosure artifact and my pillar 3 is worth nothing. I could not resolve this from any public filing, and the H1'26 $126.7M/GW figure would be meaningless if the exclusion is large. This is the single question a judge will ask that I cannot answer.
3. Q4 seasonality. Q4'24 ($184M) and Q4'25 ($115M) were the two largest revision quarters, which suggests GEV trues up estimates in the fourth quarter. A bull will argue H1'26's $218M is simply an earlier true-up and FY26 lands near $250-300M — not the $436M my run-rate implies. My counter is that Q1'26 at 6.95% and Q2'26 at 9.16% broke the seasonal pattern, but two quarters is two quarters.
4. Scale. The entire operating case is $550M of EBITDA against a ~$250B market cap — 0.2% of market value on the EBITDA math, 2.3% capitalized at 25x. It is a margin story inside a volume story, and the volume story is enormous and going the other way: H1'26 gas orders of 20.1 GW versus 12.2 GW, equipment RPO up 143% year over year, Electrification EBITDA margin up from 13.0% to 18.2%. A short whose thesis is 5.5% of the share price needs the multiple to do the rest, which returns to weakness 1.
- **strength**: 3
- **data_gaps**:
  - Consensus 2027 Power segment services revenue and margin — I benchmarked consensus at 8% services growth and 24% services EBITDA margin by inference from the Dec-2025 investor update 2028 ~$56B revenue target and the 17-19% Power margin guide. The entire gap calculation is a difference against that inferred benchmark. If the sell-side actually models Power services at 4-5% growth, the revenue gap collapses from $792M to roughly $200M and the case loses about 40% of its operating content. This is the highest-priority number to firm up from the overnight consensus run.
  - Whether CSAs attached to the 53 GW firm equipment backlog are excluded from services RPO until commissioning, and if so how large that excluded book is. The FY2025 10-K says services RPO excludes contracts not yet active but never sizes it. This determines whether pillar 3 is real economics or a disclosure artifact — it is the load-bearing unknown in the case.
  - The split of Power services revenue between Gas Power and Nuclear/Hydro. The 10-Q gives Power services in total ($6,598M H1'26) and business-unit revenue (Gas Power $8,493M, Nuclear $1,575M, Hydro $382M) but not the equipment/services split by business unit. Nuclear services grew 26% year over year and is flattering the Power services line; the Gas-only services growth rate is almost certainly lower than the 5.8% I used, which would strengthen the case but I could not prove it.
  - The Jan-1-2026 business-unit realignment moved a component of Electrification Software into Gas Power and broke Steam Power into Nuclear/Hydro/Gas. GEV restated history, but I could not size how much of reported 2026 Gas Power services growth is reclassification rather than organic.
  - Services EBITDA margin by type — contractual versus transactional. I assumed transactional parts carries roughly 4 points less EBITDA margin than CSA work, which produced only 0.1 points of the 2.5-point margin gap. If transactional actually carries a HIGHER margin than CSA (plausible — spot parts pricing is strong right now), the mix-shift argument in pillar 2 inverts and becomes a bull point.
  - Whether CSA billing uses actual or factored fired hours. The FY2025 10-K says only 'per hour of usage for example.' This does not affect my case (I deliberately built it without any duty-cycle story) but it would flip the sign on the competing AI-duty-cycle argument if anyone raises it.
  - GEV's normalized adjusted effective tax rate. GAAP ETR was -72.5% in 2025 and 37.6% in 2024, both distorted. I used 22% for the EPS bridge; a 27% rate would cut the EPS impact from $1.61 to $1.49 and the 29x target from $664 to $667 — immaterial, but the base EPS level itself is not.
  - What the '~35x forward P/E' in the team's prior work refers to. $940.33 divided by a 2027 consensus of $24.50 is 38.4x, not 35x. If 35x is the correct forward multiple then the consensus EPS base is ~$26.87, my EPS becomes $25.26, and at 29x the target is $733 (-22%) rather than $664. The team needs the exact consensus EPS and the year it applies to before this model goes into a memo.

## [Build] build:S_multiple_compression

- **side**: SHORT
- **thesis_sentence**: The market believes GEV's 116 GW order book and $12B of free cash flow justify 38x forward earnings; it is wrong because that cash is customer deposits rather than earnings and management's own 2028 plan implies it falls ~65%, and because the identical franchise (GE Power Systems) carried an identical 37.7x multiple at the identical point in the 2001 gas cycle and then lost 57% of its multiple while its segment profit still ROSE 148% — so GEV de-rates from 38x toward 25x on unchanged consensus EPS, taking the stock to ~$615.
- **pillars**:
  - - **claim**: The last time this exact franchise stood at this exact multiple at a gas-order peak, the MULTIPLE collapsed 57% while segment PROFIT rose 148%. The de-rate did not wait for the earnings decline — it preceded it by two years. GE's P/E went 37.7x (YE2000) to 16.1x (YE2002); over that same window GE Power Systems segment profit went $2,523M to $6,255M. GEV today is 38.3x. Earnings visibility is not multiple protection.
    - **evidence**:

- **dollars_per_share**: PRIMARY CHAIN — the de-rate on unchanged consensus earnings.
Step 1. Current multiple: $940.33 / 2027E adj EPS $24.55 = 38.30x. (Reproduced independently: GuruFocus forward P/E 38.13x and FinanceCharts 37.59x, both Sep 20 2026.)
Step 2. Target multiple 25x. Justification: GE's own post-de-rate multiple in this franchise was 16.1x (YE2002) and 20.0x (YE2003); Siemens Energy trades at 16.7x EV/EBITDA today; the S&P 500 is ~22x. 25x is deliberately generous — it still leaves GEV at a 14% premium to the market and a 55% premium to GE's 2003 recovery multiple.
Step 3. $/share impact = (38.30 - 25.00) x $24.55 = 13.30 x $24.55 = $326.58 per share.
Step 4. As % of $940.33 = 34.7%. Target = $940.33 - $326.58 = $613.75.
Bear leg, 22x (S&P parity): (38.30 - 22.00) x $24.55 = $400.23/share = 42.6% of $940.33 -> $540.10.
Mild leg, 30x: (38.30 - 30.00) x $24.55 = $203.83/share = 21.7% -> $736.50.

SECOND CHAIN — the EBITDA line, which is the fuse rather than the bomb.
Named line: Power services net unfavorable revisions to estimated contract profitability, plus Wind segment EBITDA.
(a) Services: H1'26 revisions -$218M = 8.11% of contract revenue vs FY25 2.79%. Annualizing the H1'26 rate on ~$5.4B of CSA revenue gives -$438M/yr vs FY25's -$151M -> incremental drag -$287M/yr.
(b) Wind: H1'26 EBITDA -$657M against an FY guide of ~-$400M, which requires H2 to swing to +$257M versus a best-ever quarter of +$19M. A realistic H2 of -$100M gives FY -$757M, a $357M miss.
Combined EBITDA shortfall vs plan = $287M + $357M = $644M, call it $0.65B/yr.
At the current 38.30x: $0.65B x 38.30 = $24.90B of value / 266,333,581 shares = $93.49/share = 9.9% of $940.33.
At a de-rated 25x: $0.65B x 25 = $16.25B / 266,333,581 = $61.01/share = 6.5% of $940.33.
Read this honestly: the operating misses are small. They are worth $61-93/share, not $327. Their function is to break the "flawless execution" narrative that supports 38x. The multiple is the trade; the misses are the trigger.

THIRD CHAIN — cash-flow cross-check, derived independently and used to corroborate the target.
Sustainable FCF from management's own cumulative plan: (>=$24B for 2025-2028) - $3.7B (2025 actual) - $12.0B (2026 guide) = $8.3B for two years = $4.2B/yr. Taking $6.0B as a fairer normalized figure (assuming they beat their floor):
$6.0B x 20x FCF (a 5% yield, generous for a cyclical) = $120.0B + net cash $10.3B = $130.3B equity = $489/share.
$6.0B x 25x FCF = $150.0B + $10.3B = $160.3B = $602/share.
Range $489-$602 brackets the $613.75 produced by the wholly independent P/E route. Two methods, one answer: roughly $500-$615.
- **implied_target**: $615 base case (25x 2027E adj EPS of $24.55), -34.6% from $940.33. Bear leg $540 (22x, S&P parity), -42.6%. Mild leg $737 (30x), -21.7%. The independent FCF route lands at $489-$602, and GLJ Research's Sep 14 2026 Sell initiation at $470 (~19x) sits just below my bear leg. Note the asymmetry the team should price: the sell-side average target is ~$1,236, 31% ABOVE spot, so this is a short against near-unanimous positioning.
- **key_assumption**: That GEV's forward multiple compresses toward 25x within 3-12 months WITHOUT requiring an earnings collapse — i.e. that the market re-rates on the QUALITY of the cash and the credibility of the 2028 margin path rather than waiting for reported EPS to fall. Everything rests on this: the de-rate is 100% of the $326.58, while the operating misses contribute only $61-93. This is exactly what happened to GE between 2000 and 2002 (multiple -57%, Power Systems profit +148%), which is why that parallel is load-bearing rather than decorative. The second-order assumption inside it is that 2027 consensus EPS of ~$24.55 is the right denominator.
- **sensitivity**: HALVE the assumption (multiple compresses only to ~31.6x, half the 38.30->25 move): $/share = (38.30 - 31.65) x $24.55 = $163.29 = 17.4% of $940.33 -> $777. Still a profitable short, but 17% over up to twelve months is thin compensation for carrying a 53.8%-vol, 1.78-beta name against a $1,236 street target. At this outcome the trade is not worth doing as a standalone short — it becomes a pair (short GEV / long ETN or the S&P) rather than an outright.
DOUBLE the assumption (compression to ~11.7x, double the move): that is below GE's 2002 trough multiple of 16.1x and implies a full bust, not a de-rate. Target ~$287, -69%. I do not underwrite this inside a 3-12 month horizon: GEV's 53 GW of firm equipment backlog and $40B of nonrefundable deposits genuinely do prevent a 2002-style earnings collapse THIS fast. The 2002 analogue took two years from the orders peak to the profit trough, and GEV's orders have not even peaked yet.
SENSITIVITY TO THE DENOMINATOR: every $1.00 of 2027 EPS is worth $25 of target at a 25x exit. If consensus is $26.50 rather than $24.55, the 25x target rises to $662.50 and the decline narrows from 34.7% to 29.5%. If consensus is $22.50, the target falls to $562.50 and the decline widens to 40.2%. The thesis survives the whole plausible $22-27 range — the de-rate dominates the estimate uncertainty, which is the main structural strength of a multiple-driven short.
SENSITIVITY TO WACC IN THE REVERSE DCF: at 8% WACC the required 10-year FCF CAGR off a $6.0B base is 12.3%; at 9% it is 14.8%; at GEV's beta-consistent 12.9% it is 23.1%. Even the most bull-friendly rate demands low-teens compounding for a decade from a company whose physical gas output has not grown in ten quarters.
- **dated_test**: Q3'26 earnings, CONFIRMED for Oct 28 2026 — inside the horizon and after the Oct 22-24 competition finals, so the team must state the test in the memo rather than wait for it. Three numbers, in priority order:
(1) GAS GW SHIPPED. Management claims a 20 GW/yr output run-rate FROM Q3'26, which requires 5.0 GW in this quarter. Actuals for the last five quarters were 5, 4, 3, 4, 3, and no quarter in ten has exceeded 5.2 GW. A print of 4.0 GW or below means the 2028 ramp to $56B revenue is arithmetically out of reach on schedule, and the 20% margin target with it.
(2) SEQUENTIAL CONTRACT-LIABILITY BUILD. Q1'26 added ~$6.2B and Q2'26 added ~$8.1B. A Q3 build below +$3.0B is the first visible deceleration of the deposit engine that is producing 100% of reported FCF, and it lands one quarter before management must guide 2027 cash.
(3) SERVICES REVISIONS. The net unfavorable revision line has printed -89 and -129 ($M) in the last two quarters, running at 8.11% of contract revenue versus 2.79% in FY25. A third consecutive quarter worse than -$100M establishes a trend that cannot be dismissed as lumpiness.
SECOND DATED TEST: a December 2026 investor update (no date announced; the Dec 9 2025 edition produced +15.6% on 3.75x volume and fully reversed within five sessions). If management guides 2027 FCF, the >=$24B cumulative arithmetic becomes explicit and unavoidable. Note this event is a two-sided risk, not a one-sided catalyst.
- **kill_condition**: Cover on ANY of the following, each numeric:
(1) Q3'26 (Oct 28) gas shipments >=5.5 GW AND sequential contract-liability build >=$6.0B. That combination means the factory ramp is real and the deposit engine is still accelerating, which is the growth case the 38x multiple is actually paying for. My central claim — that physical output has stalled while the order book inflates — would be falsified.
(2) Management guides 2027 free cash flow >=$10.0B (at Q3 earnings or the December update). This kills Pillar 2 outright: it would mean the >=$24B cumulative figure was a floor set so low as to be uninformative, and that FCF is not cliff-shaped.
(3) 2027 consensus adjusted EPS revises UP through $27.00. At $27.00 the current multiple is 34.8x rather than 38.3x, and a de-rate to 25x yields only -28.2%; more importantly, shorting into an active upgrade cycle in a 1.78-beta name is a losing structure regardless of the valuation argument.
(4) Stop at $1,080, +14.9%. This is above the Sep 12 Jefferies-note high and roughly 90% of the June 30 peak of $1,174.86; a move there means the AI-power multiple is re-expanding and the de-rate has not begun.
(5) FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin tracking above 14% (the top of guidance) at Q3. My $6.0B EBITDA base, and therefore the 40.0x EV/EBITDA that anchors Pillar 3, would be too low.
- **weakest_link**: Four places, ranked, and the first is serious.
(1) THE DE-RATE HAS NO TIMETABLE, AND I AM SHORT INTO TWO EVENTS THAT HAVE RECENTLY GONE THE OTHER WAY. Multiple compression is the entire trade ($327 of the $327) but nothing schedules it. GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, and the Dec 2025 investor update produced +15.6% on 3.75x volume. Both event types recur inside my horizon. A valuation short with no catalyst in a name with 37 analysts, mostly Buy, and an average target of $1,236 — 31% above spot — is a trade where I can be entirely right about the analysis and still lose money for twelve months. If the team takes this side, it should be a pair against ETN or the S&P, not an outright, and the memo should say so.
(2) THE $12B OF FCF IS REAL CASH, NOT FAKE CASH. The CFO stated on the Oct 22 2025 call that down payments on both orders and reservations are nonrefundable. My argument is that the flow is non-recurring, not that it is illusory — a subtler and weaker claim. If gas orders keep compounding (and Q2'26 orders were +88% organically), the deposit build can persist well past my horizon, and a 4.8% FCF yield will keep looking cheap to anyone who does not decompose it. Note too that "at least $24 billion" is floor language; management may simply be sandbagging, in which case my most striking number — the 65% FCF cliff — is an artifact of conservatism rather than a forecast.
(3) THE GE 2000-2002 DE-RATE WAS NOT PURELY A GAS CALL. GE was a conglomerate; the 37.7x-to-16.1x compression also reflects GE Capital, the post-dot-com market, Enron-era distrust of complex financials, and the Welch-to-Immelt succession. I cannot attribute the multiple move to Power Systems from public sources, and I did not try to fake a decomposition. What survives that objection is narrower but still holds: the same franchise carried the same multiple at the same point in the same cycle, and the earnings visibility everyone cited did not protect the stock.
(4) A DATA CORRECTION THE TEAM NEEDS. The brief describes GEV's ~20% drawdown as GEV-specific versus the AI-power peer basket. The corpus price table does not support that: from the late-June peaks to Sep 18, VRT fell 30.3%, PWR 14.0%, GEV 20.0%, ETN 2.5%, and SPY rose 0.3%. The de-rate is a sector event already in progress, not a GEV idiosyncrasy. This helps my direction but it also means a meaningful part of the move I am forecasting may already have happened, and it makes GEV a beta expression of an AI-capex view rather than a clean single-name short.

- **dated_test**: Q3'26 10-Q, CONFIRMED for Oct 28 2026. The RPO timing footnote reprints in Note 9 with a Sep-30-2026 measurement date. Three numbers decide it, all available within minutes of the filing and all in a single paragraph:
(1) Equipment RPO dollars and the 1-year percentage -> multiply to get the 1-year dollar bucket. My case needs >= $31,616M (the Jun-30-26 figure). The series has risen every single quarter for seven quarters: 18,941 / 20,465 / 20,879 / 22,178 / 23,771 / 28,851 / 31,616.
(2) The beyond-5-year residual (100% minus the 5-year percentage, times equipment RPO). My case needs it to stay near $2,635M; it has fallen 12.6% in dollars since Dec-2024 despite the book doubling.
(3) The implied 2-year bucket (p2 minus p1, times equipment RPO) -> my case needs >= $25,468M, since half of it is my H2'27 revenue.
SECONDARY, SAME DAY: Q3'26 equipment gross margin (Sales of equipment less Cost of equipment). My case needs >= 11.0%; Q2'26 printed 13.10%.
IMPORTANT TIMING CAVEAT FOR THE TEAM: Oct 28 falls AFTER the Oct 22-24 finals. Nothing in this case gets confirmed or refuted before the competition ends. The test is valid for the 3-12 month investment horizon, not for the pitch window — the team must be willing to defend the thesis on the Jun-30-26 footnote alone.
- **kill_condition**: Kill the LONG if ANY of the following prints on Oct 28 2026:
(1) The 1-year equipment RPO in DOLLARS at Sep-30-2026 comes in below $31,616M. This is a dollar test, not a percentage test — the percentage may keep falling (I expect it to, toward 33-34%) and the case survives, because a falling share on a fast-growing denominator is the signature of a book being added to faster than it can be worked off. A falling DOLLAR amount means the near-term book is genuinely draining. At a plausible Sep-30-26 equipment RPO of $95B, the 1-year percentage would have to drop below 33.3% to breach this.
(2) The beyond-5-year equipment bucket rises above $4,000M (from $2,635M). That is the book lengthening for real rather than the share shifting between years 1 and 2-5, and it directly falsifies Pillar 3.
(3) Q3'26 equipment gross margin falls below 9.0% (vs 13.10% in Q2'26 and 10.39% for FY25). Two consecutive quarters below 9.0% would mean the 2025-vintage repricing is not reaching the P&L and the 10.5 pt key assumption is wrong, which takes 75% of the case with it.
(4) Any restatement or downward revision of the prior-period RPO timing percentages. The whole case is built on management's own estimate of when costs will be incurred; if that estimate proves unreliable, the instrument is unreliable.
ADDITIONALLY: exit on a cumulative net unfavorable services contract-profitability revision above $200M in Q3'26 alone (H1'26 was $218M across two quarters, already 8.11% of contract revenue). That does not touch the equipment argument, but it would signal the services annuity is impaired enough to offset the equipment win.
- **weakest_link**: Pillar 2 — $176.6 of the $235.8/share, 75% of the case — is measured against GLJ Research's bear case, NOT against consensus. That is a real problem and the team must not paper over it. With ~37 analysts mostly at Buy and an average target of $1,236, consensus almost certainly already embeds roughly 10-point equipment margins. So $176.6/share is "downside that does not happen", not "upside the Street has missed". If the market already agrees with me, there is no edge in Pillar 2 and the genuine vs-consensus upside is only Pillar 1's $59.2/share (+6.3%) plus the unpriced SRA optionality — which is a thin case for a 25% move. The honest version of this thesis is a RE-RATING argument (the stock fell 20% from $1,196 on a Sell note and low volume; the RPO footnote says that de-rating was unjustified) rather than an EARNINGS-BEAT argument, and re-rating arguments are much harder to defend in a pitch than numbers the Street has not seen.

Three further vulnerabilities, stated plainly:
(a) The even-spread-within-bucket assumption is doing real work and is unverifiable. GEV does not disclose quarterly RPO phasing. If revenue is front-loaded within the 1-year bucket — plausible, since Q2'26 equipment revenue was $6,459M against Q1'26's $5,254M — then less of it falls into H1'27 and my $28,542M is too high. Route B's $20,558M is the defensible floor if a judge presses on this, and it is 30% lower.
(b) 35% of the headline TTM-to-CY2027 equipment step is Prolec annualization, not organic growth. Anyone who checks will find this, and quoting the +34% step without the caveat would be a serious credibility loss in a Q&A.
(c) The 110.3% realization ratio has n=3, and all three vintages sit in a single period of accelerating orders. It is not a through-cycle relationship and I would not defend it as one.
Finally, the catalyst lands Oct 28, four days after the finals. The team cannot point to a confirming event inside the competition window.

The whole 'vs consensus' framing needs a real sell-side 2027 revenue number and, ideally, one analyst's explicit 2027 equipment gross-margin assumption. - **dated_test**: Q3'26 earnings, CONFIRMED Oct 28 2026 (note: this is AFTER the Oct 22-24 HFAC finals, so the pitch must be made on the setup, not the result). The 3Q Form 10-Q Power segment table prints one line, "Gas Turbine Gigawatts," for the three months ended Sep 30 2026. Management committed on Jul 22 2026 to "20 GW of annual gas turbine output in the third quarter of 2026" and reaffirmed on Sep 16-18 2026 a "5-gigawatt quarterly production run rate in both the third and fourth quarters." - **dollars_per_share**: LINE: GE Vernova Power segment -- Gas Power equipment revenue, and Power segment EBITDA.

STEP 1 -- the volume gap. Management's own stated 2027 path (Strazik, Sep 16-18 2026): 5 GW/qtr in Q3'26 and Q4'26, stepping to 6 GW/qtr "in the second half of 2027." That is Q1 5 + Q2 5 + Q3 6 + Q4 6 = 22.0 GW for 2027. My short case: the step-ups slip roughly two quarters, 2027 runs ~4.5/4.5/4.75/4.75 = 18.5 GW. GAP = 22.0 - 18.5 = 3.5 GW.
Reasonableness check on 18.5: TTM through Q2'26 is 14.6 GW actual. 18.5 GW still requires +27% growth off the actual run rate. This is not a doomsday number.

STEP 2 -- revenue per GW. Power segment equipment revenue FY25 = $1,422 + $1,459 + $1,668 + $1,871 = $6,420M on 15.3 GW = $420M/GW. TTM through Q2'26 = $1,668 + $1,871 + $1,877 + $1,957 = $7,373M on 14.6 GW = $505M/GW. The rate is rising on price/mix. Cross-check from backlog: Power equipment RPO $39,261M at Jun-30-26 / 53 GW firm backlog = $741M/GW (newer, higher-priced vintage; this is an upper bound because RPO includes Nuclear/Steam/Hydro). I use $550M/GW for 2027 deliveries -- above today's realized $505, well below the $741 backlog rate.
REVENUE EFFECT = 3.5 GW x $550M/GW = $1,925M = $1.93B.

STEP 3 -- flow to EBITDA. Decremental margin 30%. Justification: the capacity cost is already sunk and committed -- 305 machines installed in gas factories over ~5 quarters with 100 more by YE26, Power segment capex $380M (FY24) -> $573M (FY25) -> $357M in H1'26 alone. Volume that does not arrive drops through at well above the 17-19% segment margin because the fixed base is already carried. 30% is the midpoint of a 25-40% band.
EBITDA EFFECT = $1,925M x 0.30 = $578M.

STEP 4 -- multiple. 25x (the default; I do not adjust it).
$578M x 25 = $14.44B of enterprise value.

STEP 5 -- per share. $14,440M / 266,333,581 shares = $54.21 per share.

STEP 6 -- as a share of price. $54.21 / $940.33 = 5.8%.

=== SECOND ROUTE (EPS, and where the real money is) ===
$578M EBITDA x (1 - 25% tax) = $433M of net income / 266,333,581 = $1.63 of 2027 EPS.
Consensus 2027 adjusted EPS ~$24.50 -> $22.87, a 6.6% cut.
Current multiple: $940.33 / $24.50 = 38.4x 2027E.
De-rate to 28x (still a 27% premium to the S&P's 22x and above the AI-power peers): $22.87 x 28 = $640. That is -$300/share, -32.0%.

DECOMPOSITION OF THE $300 -- state this plainly to the team:
  Earnings piece: $1.63 EPS x 38.4x = $62/share = 21% of the move.
  Multiple piece: $22.87 EPS x (38.4 - 28.0) = $237/share = 79% of the move.
Four fifths of this short is multiple compression, not an earnings miss. The volume slip is the trigger, not the payload.

- **key_assumption**: That the 2027 gas output gap is 3.5 GW (22.0 GW guided path vs 18.5 GW delivered) AND that a miss on that line compresses the multiple from 38.4x to 28x. The volume assumption alone is worth $54/share; the multiple assumption is worth $237/share. The single most load-bearing input is therefore NOT the GW number -- it is the belief that GEV's 38.4x is paid for the ramp narrative specifically, so that a visible ramp miss de-rates the whole stock rather than just trimming one segment's EBITDA.

Bloomberg-type commentary already made this point explicitly: Q2'26 HA deliveries fell to 3 units "yet Power equipment revenue still grew 30%." My rebuttal -- that costs incurred are bounded by the same physical throughput, so the divergence cannot widen forever -- is logically sound but has been wrong for ten quarters. METHOD 1 — capitalize the CONTRACTED data-center book.
Step 1. Data-center GW under contract = 116 GW x 20% = 23.2 GW.
Step 2. Equipment revenue per GW, derived two ways. Step 3. Equipment revenue at risk = 23.2 GW x $500/kW = $11.6B, delivered over ~5 years (2029-2033) = $2.32B/yr.
Step 4. Power equipment EBITDA margin 12% (vs 17.6% blended segment margin H1'26 = $1,842M/$10,448M; 12% respects GLJ's 10-11 pts on the 2025 vintage) => $2.32B x 12% = $278M/yr.
Step 5. Attached services = 23.2 GW x $25M/GW-yr (management's own ~$500M per GW over 20 years, Laguna Sep 16 2026) = $580M/yr revenue x 25% EBITDA margin = $145M/yr.
Step 6. Mature annual EBITDA from the entire contracted data-center book = $278M + $145M = $423M/yr.
Step 7. x 25x multiple = $10.59B.
Step 8. / 266,333,581 shares = $39.74/share = 4.23% of $940.33.

METHOD 2 (reproduction, top-down) — data centers as a permanent share of the gas franchise.
Step 1. Market cap = $940.33 x 266,333,581 = $250.4B; less ~$8B net cash => EV ~$242B.
Step 2. Power share of segment EBITDA H1'26 = $1,842M / ($1,842M + $1,199M - $657M) = 77.3% (FY25 check: $2,902M / $3,737M = 77.7%) => Power ~$187B.
Step 3. Gas Power share of Power revenue H1'26 = $8,493M / $10,448M = 81.3% => gas franchise ~$152B.
Step 4. Data centers at 20% of GW => $30.5B = $114/share = 12.2% of price. Weighting data centers to 25% for richer HA mix and services => $38.1B = $143/share = 15.2%.

THE TWO METHODS BRACKET THE ANSWER: $40/share (contracted book only) to $143/share (data centers as a permanent quarter of the gas franchise, destroyed in perpetuity).

WHAT THE MARKET HAS ALREADY TAKEN: peak close $1,174.86 (Jun 30 2026) to $940.33 = -$234.53/share, -19.96%, -$62.5B of market cap. That is 1.6x the MOST generous estimate of the entire data-center franchise being destroyed forever, and 5.9x the contracted-book estimate.

THE IN-HORIZON DRIVER THAT ACTUALLY MOVES A LINE — SRA conversion.

Step 2. x 12% EBITDA margin = $1.20B of EBITDA.
Step 3. x 25x = $30.0B at full credit.
Step 4. The market already gives SRAs partial credit; the uplift is the collapse of that discount. If SRAs are credited at 75%: $7.5B = $28.16/share = 3.0% of price. At 50%: $15.0B = $56.32/share = 6.0%. At 25%: $22.5B = $84.48/share = 9.0%.

- **key_assumption**: That the ~92.8 GW of "traditional" (non-data-center) gigawatts under contract would still be built if hyperscaler capex fell sharply — i.e. that the utility, IPP and international demand in the book is driven by load growth, coal replacement, reserve-margin shortfalls and international build that exists independently of AI, and not merely by AI load wearing a utility's name on the contract.
- **sensitivity**: HALVED (only 46.4 GW, half the traditional book, is genuinely AI-independent; the rest evaporates with hyperscaler capex): total durable book = 46.4 GW = 2.32 years of production at 20 GW/yr. The in-horizon conclusion is UNCHANGED — shipments for the next twelve months still come entirely out of the 53 GW firm backlog, and the $45.8B of RPO due within twelve months still covers FY26 guidance in full. What breaks is the 2029-2031 slot fill and the pricing power that depends on scarcity; the stock would deserve a materially lower multiple but not a lower FY26/FY27 P&L. Roughly: losing half the traditional book plus all data centers = ~70 GW of the 116 GW, which on Method 2 arithmetic ($152B gas franchise x 60%) is ~$91B = $342/share. That is far more than the $234.53 already taken, so this scenario is NOT priced and it is the real bear case.

DOUBLED (the traditional book is even more AI-independent than claimed, and data centers are actually below 20%): the entire drawdown is a sentiment event. Non-DC coverage rises above 4.64 years, the >=125 GW target is met comfortably, and the peer-relative gap ($88.51/share) closes entirely, plus full SRA-conversion credit (up to $84.48/share) — $1,113 or better.

The asymmetry is the point: the downside case requires the traditional 80% to be fake, and the four primary utility filings (Southern, FPL, Entergy, NRG) say the AI load inside it is contractually insulated, not fake.
- **dated_test**: OCTOBER 28, 2026 — Q3'26 earnings (confirmed date; note this falls AFTER the Oct 22-24 competition finals, so the team must state the test in advance rather than rely on the result). Four numbers, in priority order:
1. GW converted from SRA to firm orders. Base case >=8 GW (Q2'26 was 10 GW, Q1'26 6 GW). Below 5 GW breaks the conversion engine.
2. Total GW under contract. Base case >=122 GW, on track to the stated ">=125 GW by end of the year". Management also guided to backlog GW exceeding SRA GW in H2'26 — watch whether firm backlog moves 53 -> ~63+ while SRAs stay flat or fall.
3. Whether the traditional/data-center split is restated. Base case still ~80/20. Any move below 70/30 damages pillar 1 directly.
4. Contract liabilities. Base case >$42B, continuing the $17.6B (Dec-24) -> $25.8B (Dec-25) -> $31.8B (Mar-26) -> $40.0B (Jun-26) build. These are nonrefundable customer deposits and are the hardest available evidence that customers are actually committing cash, not just signing paper.

Secondary, earlier and free: GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, so the Oct 28 print is directionally high-information rather than noise.

Interim test before the memo deadline: any Q3 pre-announcement, investor-conference remark, or customer 10-Q (Southern, Entergy, Duke, Dominion file Q3 in late Oct/early Nov) that restates large-load contracted GW. Southern's 11 GW PSC-reviewed + ~5 GW pending is the single most trackable proxy.
- **kill_condition**: Any ONE of these kills the LONG:
1. Q3'26 (Oct 28) shows SRA conversions below 5 GW AND total GW under contract below 120 GW — the >=125 GW year-end target then fails and the conversion engine, which is the entire in-horizon value driver, has stalled.
2. Firm equipment backlog falls sequentially by more than shipments — i.e. net NEGATIVE cancellations appear in the 53 GW firm book for the first time. Backlog after Q3 below 53 GW + converted GW - ~5 GW shipped.
3. Management restates the traditional/data-center mix below 70/30, or withdraws the disclosure entirely (the NRG precedent — its GEV reservation disclosure paragraph simply vanished from its 2026 10-Qs — shows this happens).
4. Contract liabilities decline sequentially below $38B, indicating deposits are being returned or liquidated faster than new ones are posted.
5. Two or more of Southern / Entergy / Dominion / AEP disclose cancelled or materially reduced large-load contracts totalling more than 3 GW in their Q3 filings.
6. FY26 revenue guidance is cut below $45.5B, which would falsify the claim that the $45.8B of RPO due within twelve months locks the in-horizon P&L.
- **weakest_link**: "Traditional customer" is a COUNTERPARTY label, not a LOAD label — and this is the hinge of the whole case. Southern Company's own 10-Q describes its large-load book as contracts "with new data centers and other large load customers" covering ~11 GW. Southern is, in GEV's taxonomy, a traditional customer. So GEV's 80/20 almost certainly understates how much of the book is ultimately AI-driven load; the honest reading is that the counterparty is diversified while the underlying demand driver may not be. GEV has never disclosed the END-USE split of the traditional 80%, and that single undisclosed number would settle the argument either way. My pillar 4 (take-or-pay floors, termination payments, collateral, Meta parent guaranty) blunts this but does not eliminate it: those provisions make the UTILITY whole if a hyperscaler walks; they do not oblige the utility to proceed with a new turbine ORDER if its own load forecast collapses. If AI capex fell hard enough to reset utility IRPs, the traditional 80% would not be independent of it.

Second weakness: I cannot determine how the 23.2 GW of data-center capacity splits between the 53 GW firm backlog and the 63 GW of SRAs. I assumed 20% of each. If data centers are concentrated in FIRM backlog rather than reservations, near-term cancellation exposure is higher than I model — though the nonrefundable-deposit structure and the over-time revenue recognition still blunt it.

Third, and the team should be honest about this in the room: my case argues DEMAND durability and says nothing about MARGINS. GLJ's Sell thesis — that 2027 ships 2024-priced orders at ~3 points versus 10-11 on the 2025 vintage — is orthogonal to everything above and could hit 2027 EBITDA even if every gigawatt in the book ships on time. A LONG built on this case is exposed to a margin-vintage miss on Oct 28 that has nothing to do with data centers. That is why my implied target is $1,050 and not the $1,236 street average.

Fourth: two premises handed to me were wrong and the team must not repeat them (see data gaps) — including the claim that GEV's drawdown was GEV-specific versus the AI-power peer basket. Vertiv fell MORE. The idiosyncratic component is ~7.5 points, not 20.

- **dollars_per_share**: LINE: GE Vernova Electrification segment EBITDA.

STEP 1 — Where it is. FY24 $679M on $7,550M (9.0%); FY25 $1,433M on $9,642M (14.9%) [gev_segments.csv, xbrl IncomeLossFromContinuingOperations...;OperatingSegments;ElectrificationSegment]. H1'26 $1,200M on $6,597M (18.2%), or 19.8% excluding the $106M Prolec inventory step-up sitting in cost of equipment.

STEP 2 — FY26E. Guide (raised 2026-07-22): revenue $14.5-15.0B including ~$3.1B Prolec, margin 18-20%. Use $14.75B x 19.7% = $2.90B. (19.7% not the 19.0% midpoint, because H1 is already 19.8% ex-step-up and H2 is the seasonally larger half: Q4'25 was Electrification's biggest quarter.)

STEP 3 — 2028E revenue build.
  organic FY26E = $14.75B − $3.1B Prolec = $11.65B
  organic at 14%/yr (BELOW the +29% organic in Q2'26 and below the Dec-2025 plan's own 16-18%) = $11.65 x 1.14^2 = $15.14B
  Prolec, GEV's own Oct-2025 deck 2028E = $4.20B
  Prolec revenue synergy: $800M of orders booked in ~5 months = ~$1.9B/yr order rate; halve it and convert over ~24 months = $1.00B
  2028E revenue = 15.14 + 4.20 + 1.00 = $20.34B

STEP 4 — 2028E margin 22%. This is MANAGEMENT'S OWN assumption embedded in the $56B revenue / 20% adjusted-EBITDA 2028 target (third-party decomposition: "This target already assumes margins for Power and Electrification reaching 22% each, alongside Wind turning around ... to a 6% margin"). $20.34B x 22% = $4.47B, plus $90M mid-point cost synergies = $4.56B. Round to $4.50B.
  CHECK (second method, top-down): the $11.2B 2028 target only closes if Electrification delivers ~$5.0B — Power $29B x 22% = $6.4B, Electrification, Wind $7.5B x 6% = +$0.45B, corporate −$0.6B. 6.4 + 4.95 + 0.45 − 0.6 = $11.2B. So $4.5B is BELOW what the company's own plan arithmetically requires.

STEP 5 — Skeptical baseline (what a disbeliever marks). FY26 guide MIDPOINT $2.80B growing at 8%/yr, the US industrial average: $2.80 x 1.08^2 = $3.27B.

STEP 6 — DELTA = $4.50B − $3.27B = +$1.23B of 2028 EBITDA.

STEP 7 — MULTIPLE: 20x, not the 25x default. Justification: it is below the 23.8x median EV/FY2025-EBITDA of the four listed grid-equipment comps as of 2026-09-18 (HUBB 17.4x, ROK 23.5x, AME 24.1x, ETN 39.1x; VRT 45.0x excluded as a data-center pure-play) [corpus table comps_inputs]; below GEV's own consolidated 21.4x EV/2028E-EBITDA; and above the 9.4x 2028E adjusted EBITDA GEV itself paid for Prolec. Using a multiple below the comps is the conservative choice and I take it deliberately.

STEP 8 — $1.23B x 20 = $24.6B of enterprise value.
STEP 9 — $24.6B / 266,333,581 shares = $92.37 per share.
STEP 10 — $92.37 / $940.33 = 9.8% of the current price.
  At the 25x default instead: $1.23B x 25 = $30.75B / 266,333,581 = $115.46/share = 12.3%.

STEP 11 — SECOND LEG, the re-rating. EV today = $250.44B market cap ($940.33 x 266,333,581) + $2.79B debt − $13.1B cash at Jun-30-26 = $240.1B. Against the company's own 2028 target of $11.2B adjusted EBITDA that is 21.4x — BELOW the 23.8x grid-comp median, on a number two years forward. (Reproduces a third-party calc in the corpus: "At the current price of ~$920, the stock trades at approximately 21x EV/EBITDA based on the company's 2028 targets.") If Electrification's delivery pulls the 2028 multiple to the 23.8x comp median: EV $266.6B, +$26.5B, / 266,333,581 = +$99.35/share = +10.6%.

TOTAL: $92.37 + $99.35 = $191.72/share = 20.4% of $940.33.

WHAT YOU OWN (gross, not differential): Electrification EBITDA rises $2.90B → $4.50B between FY26E and 2028E. $1.60B x 20x = $32.0B / 266,333,581 = $120.15/share of EV creation from one segment, 12.8% of today's price, with $9.1B of the cash already collected.
- **implied_target**: $1,132 (= $940.33 + $92.37 earnings differential + $99.35 re-rating), +20.4%. Round to a $1,100-1,150 range. This sits BELOW the ~$1,236 average of 37 analysts and far below the $1,450 Street high, and above the $895 200-day moving average that the corpus cites as the technical downside. Horizon 3-12 months, with the path running through the Oct 28 2026 Q3 print and any December 2026 investor update (the Dec 2025 update produced +15.6% the next day on 3.75x volume, fully reversed within 5 sessions — so treat a December pop as noise, not the catalyst).
- **key_assumption**: Electrification reaches a 22% segment EBITDA margin by 2028. Everything else in the model is either contracted (the $40.6B equipment backlog, the $9.1B of prepaid customer cash) or conservative (14%/yr organic revenue vs +29% organic in Q2'26). The margin is the number doing the work: it is management's own 2028 plan assumption, it is only 220bps above the 19.8% H1'26 already delivered ex-inventory-step-up, and roughly 150bps of the gap arrives mechanically as the Prolec purchase-accounting drag (~$35-40M/quarter of inventory step-up plus acquisition costs inside segment EBITDA) washes out by end-2026 with zero operating improvement required.
- **sensitivity**: HALVED (margin expands only half as far, to 20% in 2028 instead of 22%): 2028 EBITDA = $20.34B x 20% = $4.07B; delta vs the $3.27B skeptical baseline = $0.80B; x 20x = $16.0B / 266,333,581 = $59.92/share = 6.4% of $940.33. The case survives at about two-thirds strength and the LONG still works.

STALLED ENTIRELY (margin never gets past FY26's 19.7%): 2028 EBITDA = $4.01B; delta $0.74B; $55.5/share = 5.9%. Thin but still positive — because the revenue growth alone carries it.

DOUBLED (margin reaches 24%, i.e. twice the expansion): 2028 EBITDA = $4.88B; delta $1.61B; x 20x = $32.2B = $121.02/share = 12.9%.

Second sensitivity, on organic revenue growth: at 10%/yr instead of 14% (with 22% margin held), 2028 revenue = $19.30B, EBITDA = $4.25B, delta $0.98B, = $73.29/share = 7.8%. The case is materially less sensitive to the revenue assumption than to the margin one, which is why I named margin as the key assumption.

Tariff sensitivity: charging the entire guided FY26 company-wide net tariff high end of $350M to Electrification costs −$26.28/share (−2.8%); doubling it to $700M costs −$52.57/share (−5.6%). Neither reverses the sign.
- **dated_test**: Q3 2026 earnings, CONFIRMED for October 28 2026 — five weeks from tonight, inside the horizon and after the Oct 22-24 finals. Four numbers, all published in the segment table of the 8-K press release that morning:
(1) Electrification revenue >= $3.8B. The guide bridge forces it: FY $14.5-15.0B less H1 $6,597M leaves $7.9-8.4B for H2; a normal Q3/Q4 split puts Q3 near $3.87B, +49% against the restated Q3'25 of $2,601M.
(2) Electrification segment EBITDA margin >= 19.0%, up from 18.4% in Q2 and 18.2% in H1, with the inventory step-up ($35M in Q2, $106M cumulative) now substantially exhausted. This is the single cleanest read on the key assumption.
(3) Electrification orders >= $4.4B, i.e. book-to-bill >= 1.15x, EVEN THOUGH Strazik pre-warned on Sep 16 that data-center orders fall from ~40% of Electrification orders in H1 to closer to 20% in H2. Clearing 1.15x on a pre-announced-weak mix is the real test of breadth.
(4) Electrification equipment backlog >= $43B (from $40.6B at Jun-30).
Secondary, Q4: the ~$1.5B India HVDC award Strazik said GEV won publicly but expects to book in the fourth quarter. If it slips out of 2026, orders momentum is weaker than management implied.
- **kill_condition**: Any ONE of these on the October 28 2026 print kills the case and the team should flip or stand down:
(a) Electrification segment EBITDA margin below 17.5% — below Q2'25 + 300bps, below the low end of the 18-20% FY guide, and with no inventory step-up left to blame. The margin-compounding pillar is then simply wrong.
(b) Electrification orders below $3.8B, i.e. book-to-bill below 1.0x, for Q3 — or below 1.0x in Q3 AND Q4. Backlog stops growing and the 2028 revenue build loses its foundation.
(c) FY26 Electrification revenue guidance cut below $14.5B (the current low end), or the 18-20% margin guide cut.
(d) Electrification equipment backlog flat or down sequentially from $40.6B.
Numeric threshold on the model itself: if 2028 Electrification EBITDA has to be marked below $3.6B, the delta versus the skeptical baseline falls under $0.35B, worth under $26/share (2.8%) — below the noise band of a stock that has moved 20% in three months, and the pitch no longer justifies a position.
- **weakest_link**: The sum-of-the-parts does NOT show Electrification is free, and I will not pretend otherwise. Back the segment out of the $240.1B enterprise value at even a generous 23.8x FY26E EBITDA ($69.0B) and the residual for Power plus corporate is $171.1B against FY26E Power EBITDA of $4.19B — 40.8x. At a 20x Electrification multiple the residual is 43.5x. GE Vernova is expensive on its largest segment on any cut. This is a growth-and-credibility case, not a valuation-support case: if the gas thesis cracks the way GLJ argues (2027 shipping 2024-priced orders at ~3pts of margin, slot reservations that hold a slot but not a price), Electrification will not rescue the stock. It is 43% of FY26E segment EBITDA and ~40% in 2028 — large enough to matter, nowhere near large enough to offset a Power de-rating.

Four more places I am exposed, in order of severity:
1. The shortage that supports the margin is forecast to ease exactly when I need the margin. A Sep 16 2026 corpus source has Morgan Stanley Infrastructure-style analysis expecting the equipment bottleneck to become "more manageable beginning in 2028" as capacity is added, and Hitachi Energy is putting $9B into ramping global transformer capacity. My 22% 2028 margin assumes pricing power survives the relief year.
2. The Section 232 cliff lands in my target year. Grid equipment's capped 15% derivative rate expires Dec 31 2027 and reverts to 25% on Jan 1 2028. I cannot size it because GEV does not disclose its imported dollar base.
3. The $800M revenue synergy is a CEO remark at a conference, not a filed figure. No contract, no price, no delivery schedule, and no way to confirm it is incremental to Prolec's pre-existing frame agreements rather than a reallocation within them. It is 2.9% of the case on its own.
4. My "skeptical baseline" of $3.27B (guide midpoint grown 8%/yr) is my own construction, not a Street segment estimate. The entire $92/share differential is measured against a number I made up. If consensus already carries Electrification at $4.0B+ for 2028, the differential collapses to roughly $37/share and the case is mostly the re-rating leg, which is far softer.
5. GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, and Electrification is 32% of revenue. Even if every Electrification number lands, a Wind writedown or a gas miss sets the October 28 tape.
- **strength**: 3
- **data_gaps**:
  - MOST IMPORTANT: Street segment-level estimates for Electrification 2027 and 2028 EBITDA. The entire $92/share differential is measured against a skeptical baseline I constructed (FY26 guide midpoint grown 8%/yr = $3.27B). If the overnight consensus run comes back with Electrification 2028 EBITDA already at $4.0B+, the differential falls to roughly $0.5B = ~$37/share and the case is mostly re-rating. Get this before the team commits.
  - Electrification's share of the $176.3B RPO and of the $87.8B equipment RPO. GEV discloses RPO only at the company level and breaks out Electrification only as a management-defined 'equipment backlog' ($40.6B), which is not the same measure. Without the split I cannot state how much of 2027-28 Electrification revenue is contractually locked versus management-asserted.
  - Prolec's clean post-close P&L. The 10-Q gives revenue ($859M in Q2'26, $1,344M Feb 2-Jun 30) and pre-tax loss (−$57M, −$166M) but no EBITDA. My ~$147M GAAP segment EBITDA and ~21.6% clean margin rest on a $179M/quarter intangible amortization figure I computed from the acquired-intangibles table, not a disclosed number. If the actual amortization schedule is front- or back-loaded rather than straight-line, the organic/Prolec split moves.
  - GEV's dollar value of imports subject to Section 232 derivative duties. Without it the January 1 2028 step from 15% to 25% on grid equipment cannot be sized, and that is the one dated risk that lands inside my target year.
  - Whether the $800M of newly enabled North American transformer orders is incremental volume or a reallocation within Prolec's existing frame agreements (which the Oct 2025 deck said are 'not in backlog'). Also unknown: the price and delivery schedule, so the 24-month conversion assumption is unverified.
  - Electrification's 2028 revenue and margin targets as published by GE Vernova segment-by-segment. The 22% figure comes from a third-party decomposition of the $56B / 20% company target, which I reproduced arithmetically (6.4 + 4.95 + 0.45 - 0.6 = 11.2) but did not source to a GEV slide. Worth pulling the Dec 2025 investor update deck directly.
  - Hitachi Energy and Schneider Electric trading multiples. comps_inputs covers ETN, HUBB, ROK, AME, EMR, PWR, VRT but neither Hitachi Energy (not separately listed ex-India) nor Schneider. The 23.8x comp median rests on four names, one of which (ETN at 39.1x) is an outlier pulling it up.
  - Q3'26 Electrification order composition. Strazik pre-warned data centers drop from ~40% to ~20% of Electrification orders in H2. Nobody has published what the non-data-center pipeline looks like, so the (3) test threshold of 1.15x book-to-bill is my judgment, not a modeled number.

- **dollars_per_share**: START: $940.33 (GEV close 18 Sep 2026). Shares 266,333,581. Market cap = 266,333,581 x $940.33 = $250.44B. Cash 6/30/26 $13.120B, debt ~$1.5B, net cash ~$11.6B, EV ~$238.8B.

STEP 0 — ANCHOR ON MANAGEMENT'S OWN PLAN, NO THESIS REQUIRED. 2028 outlook (Dec-2025 investor update, restated 28 Jan 2026): revenue $56.0B, adjusted EBITDA margin 20% => $11.20B adjusted EBITDA. At the 25x default: EV = 25 x $11.20B = $280.0B. Equity = $280.0B + $11.6B net cash = $291.6B. Per share = $291.6B / 266,333,581 = $1,094.87 in 2028. Discounted 2 years at 10%: $1,094.87 / 1.21 = $904.85. Versus $940.33 that is -$35.48/share, -3.8%. Today's price already embeds ~96% of a perfectly delivered 2028 plan at a 25x terminal multiple.

STEP 1 — MULTIPLE: 25x -> 22x (pillar 2, the failed-inversion credibility hit). Delta EV = 3 x $11.20B = $33.6B. Per share in 2028 = $33.6B / 266,333,581 = $126.16. Discounted: $126.16 / 1.21 = $104.27. Running price: $904.85 - $104.27 = $800.58. (-11.1% of $940.33.) Justification for 22x rather than 25x: GEV trades at 30.5x trailing gross profit versus Siemens Energy 15.1x and Mitsubishi Heavy 12.1x (corpus chunk 217437); 22x EBITDA is still a large premium and above where GEV's own peer basket clears.

STEP 2 — EBITDA: 2028 revenue $56.0B -> $50.0B and margin 20% -> 18% (pillar 1, the conversion machine cannot build the firm order book required for a 24 GW shipment year). EBITDA $11.20B -> $9.00B, delta -$2.20B. At 22x: delta EV = -$48.4B. Per share in 2028 = $48.4B / 266,333,581 = $181.73. Discounted: $181.73 / 1.21 = $150.19. Running price: $800.58 - $150.19 = $650.39. (-16.0% of $940.33.)

TARGET $650. TOTAL DOLLARS PER SHARE = $940.33 - $650.39 = -$289.94/share = -30.8% of $940.33.

CROSS-CHECK A (independent route, FY26 instead of 2028): FY26 adjusted EBITDA = revenue $46.0B midpoint x 13.5% (mid of the 12-14% guide) = $6.21B. At the 25x default: $155.3B equity / 266,333,581 = $582.92/share, -38.0%. Today GEV trades at $250.44B / $6.21B = 40.3x market cap to EBITDA, 38.5x EV/EBITDA.

CROSS-CHECK B (independent route, FCF): FY26 FCF guide midpoint $12.0B => 20.9x market cap / FCF. The 22 Jul raise of +$5.0B (from the 22 Apr guide of $6.5-7.5B) was attributed by management 'primarily' to SRA down payments. Same 20.9x on the pre-raise $7.0B = $146.1B equity = $548.71/share, -41.7%.

Three independent routes land at $549, $583, $650. I take $650 as the target because it is the only one built on 2028 rather than on a single trough year, and it is the least aggressive of the three. Range: $583 (25x FY26 EBITDA) on the low side, $731 (full $56B/20% plan at 20x, discounted) on the high side.

BOUNDING CHECK (pillar 4): if instead you simply wrote off the reservation pool's fundamental value, 63 GW x $300M/GW x 18% / 3 years + 63 GW x $25M/GW-yr x 30% = $1.61B/yr run-rate EBITDA x 25x = $40.2B = $151/share, 16.0% of price. A 40% failure rate costs only $60/share (6.4%). This is why the case is a multiple case, not an asset-writeoff case, and I am explicit about that.
- **implied_target**: $650 (-30.8% from $940.33). Range $583-$731. For reference: GLJ Research initiated Sell at $470 on 14 Sep 2026 (the low of the ~37-analyst range); average target ~$1,236.
- **key_assumption**: That GEV's slot-reservation conversion rate stays near its observed level — 20.3% of the opening pool per quarter naive, 22.0% on the vintage-adjusted (2-quarter-seasoned) basis in H1'26 — rather than jumping to the 30-46% that management's H2'26 inversion promise and the 2028 24 GW shipment plan both require. Everything else in the model (2028 revenue $50B vs $56B, margin 18% vs 20%, multiple 22x vs 25x) is downstream of that one number.
- **sensitivity**: HALVED (c = 10.2%/qtr, ~10-quarter dwell): the steady-state reservation pool S* = N/c = 18/0.102 = 176 GW. Reservations become 3x firm backlog, the inversion promise fails by a mile, the '125 GW under contract' headline becomes visibly a queue rather than a book, and the 2028 firm order base supports well under 20 GW/yr of shipments. Target moves to the FY26-anchored $583 or below, toward GLJ's $470. Downside roughly -38% to -50%.

DOUBLED (c = 40.6%/qtr, essentially Siemens Energy's 46.2%): S* = 18/0.406 = 44 GW. Conversions run ~25 GW/qtr, firm backlog crosses above reservations inside one or two quarters, management is vindicated on 28 Oct, the 24 GW 2028 ramp is fully underwritten, and the pool's residual value plus the credibility restoration argue for 25x or higher on a plan that is now believable. The thesis is dead and GEV re-rates upward; a short loses 15-25% from here.

The asymmetry is genuine and it cuts against me: the sensitivity is roughly symmetric in magnitude, so this is not a free option. It is a one-number bet resolving on a known date.

SECOND-ORDER SENSITIVITY (the multiple): every 1 turn of 2028 EV/EBITDA on the $9.00B short-case EBITDA = $9.00B / 266,333,581 = $33.79/share in 2028 = $27.93/share discounted = 3.0% of the price. So the 25x-to-22x cut is worth 8.9%, and if the market instead holds 25x on my lower EBITDA the target rises from $650 to $734.
- **dated_test**: Q3'26 earnings, CONFIRMED 28 Oct 2026 (inside the 3-12 month horizon; six days after the 22-24 Oct finals). Three numbers to read off the release in order:

1. THE PINCER. Firm gas equipment backlog B and slot reservations S at 30 Sep 2026, and the quarter's conversions C. My model says: with new reservations N at the recent 18-19 GW pace and shipments ~5 GW, B_end ~= 53 + 2 + C - 5 and S_end ~= 63 + 18 - C. Firm backlog only reaches reservations if C >= 13 GW in the quarter. CONFIRMS THESIS: C <= 9 GW and S_end - B_end >= 10 GW (gap has not narrowed). Also confirms if total under contract comes in below ~120 GW, which would mean they bought the inversion by starving the top of the funnel.

2. THE CASH. Q3 free cash flow and the 'contract liabilities and current deferred income' line in the cash-flow statement. Management's own FY26 guide implies H2 FCF of $1.6-2.6B, i.e. $0.8-1.3B per quarter versus Q2'26's $5,107M. CONFIRMS THESIS: Q3 FCF <= $1.5B with a contract-liability inflow under $2.0B, which demonstrates that the float, not earnings, was the engine. Watch also whether they reaffirm $11.5-12.5B — reaffirming it while posting a small Q3 loads all the risk into Q4.

3. THE PRICE. GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, and the stock fell 8.69% on 22 Jul 2026 ($1,078.81 -> $985.03) on a day it raised both revenue and FCF guidance. The tape already penalises float-funded beats.

SECONDARY, EARLIER: any 8-K or press release between now and 28 Oct announcing a large gas order conversion (a named customer moving a reservation to a firm order) is a real-time reading on C. Watch NRG, VST, CEG and the Texas/PJM IPP filings in the corpus 'projects' table for GEV-linked projects reaching FID.
- **kill_condition**: COVER IMMEDIATELY if the Q3'26 print (28 Oct 2026) shows EITHER of:
(a) Firm gas equipment backlog >= slot reservations at 30 Sep 2026 (the inversion actually happened), OR conversions >= 13 GW in the single quarter — either proves the conversion rate has stepped up to the Siemens-like 30-46% band and the entire pillar-1 and pillar-2 chain is wrong. 13 GW is 1.30x the all-time record; 30 Sep firm >= reservations is management's own stated bar.
(b) Q3'26 contract-liability / deferred-income inflow >= $6.0B AND FY26 FCF guidance raised above $12.5B — the float is still accelerating, meaning the deposit engine has more runway than I credit and the H2 cash cliff I am shorting does not exist.

ALSO COVER (position management, not thesis): if GEV closes above $1,060 (the 22 Jul post-print level, ~+13% from $940.33) at any point before 28 Oct without a Q3 print, the market has re-embraced the narrative ahead of the catalyst and the risk/reward into the event is no longer worth carrying.

TRIM if the vintage-adjusted conversion rate computed off the Q3 print rises above 30% even without the inversion — the direction of the key assumption has reversed and only the multiple leg survives.
- **weakest_link**: Three places, in order of how much they hurt.

1. THE DEPOSITS ARE REAL AND A LAPSED SLOT MAY BE A GAIN, NOT A LOSS. CFO Ken Parks on the record (22 Apr 2026, corpus chunk 468326): on both slot reservations and orders "there's a measurable amount of cash funding upfront and down payments. And in both cases, they're nonrefundable." A customer who has posted roughly $100-290M per GW is powerfully motivated to convert. Worse for me: GEV is oversubscribed roughly five years out and H1'26 orders priced 10-20 percentage points higher on a $/kW basis than Q4'25 orders (corpus chunk 217480). If a reservation lapses, GEV keeps a non-refundable deposit AND resells the slot at a higher price. In a genuinely sold-out market, low conversion may be a pricing option, not a quality problem. I cannot defeat this with public data. The best I can do is point out that (i) the Maxim Power filing shows price is set later in the definitive agreement, so the reservation holder is not locked to a price either, and (ii) a lapse-and-resell cycle still delays revenue recognition and breaks the 2028 shipment ramp, which is what my model actually cuts. But this is the argument that beats me and the team should expect it.

2. A LOT OF THE DE-RATE IS ALREADY DONE, AND IT IS NOT CLEANLY GEV-SPECIFIC. GEV is -20.0% from its 30 Jun 2026 high of $1,174.86 to $940.33. Over the identical window VRT fell -25.5% and PWR -11.6% while SPY rose +2.0%. So the AI-power complex de-rated and GEV sits in the middle of it — this is not proof the market has singled out GEV's reservation quality. More damaging: the market ALREADY sold the float. GEV fell 8.69% on 22 Jul, the day it raised FY26 FCF guidance by $5.0B. If the deposit-funded-FCF point is already in the price, my pillar 3 buys me less than the model implies, and the remaining downside is smaller than 31%.

3. n = 5, AND THE CONVERSION SERIES IS LUMPY. The naive rates are 14.3%, 28.0%, 27.6%, 14.0%, 17.9%. With five observations I cannot statistically separate a structural slowdown from noise, and the two weak quarters (Q2'25, Q1'26) each follow a quarter in which the pool jumped. I built the vintage-adjusted series specifically to test this, and the deterioration survives (32.7% -> 22.0%), but that is four observations, not forty. If Q3'26 converts 11-12 GW the whole trend is inside the noise band and pillar 1 is a coincidence I dressed up as a mechanism.

Minor but worth flagging to the team: my $/share bridge runs through a 2028 EBITDA estimate two years out, and the horizon is 3-12 months. The catalyst (28 Oct) is real and dated, but the valuation gap only closes if the market revises its 2028 view on one quarter's data — which it may not do in one print.
- **strength**: 3
- **data_gaps**:
  - THE BIG ONE: the split of the H1'26 $13.7B contract-liability inflow between slot-reservation deposits and milestone billings on firm orders. GEV does not disclose it. My two estimation routes disagree badly — the stock method (43.3% vs a 36.0% baseline prepayment ratio on Product RPO) gives ~$102M/GW of SRA deposit, the flow method (residual after attributing 36% to the $23.6B of incremental Product RPO) gives ~$261-290M/GW. The flow number is implausibly high against $300M/GW of content, which means I am over-attributing to SRAs and the firm-order prepayment rate at signing must be well above 36%. Until this is nailed, the claim 'the FCF is reservation deposits' rests on management's own attribution language rather than on my arithmetic. Fix: read the Q3'26 10-Q contract-liability rollforward note on 28 Oct, and check whether GEV discloses SRA deposits inside ContractWithCustomerLiability at all or parks them in other liabilities (an SRA may not be an ASC 606 contract).
  - Consensus 2027 adjusted EPS. I assumed the ~$24-25 the brief supplied and did not build the case on EPS at all, using EBITDA and FCF instead. But the multiple leg would be far more persuasive with a firm consensus number: at $940.33 and 35x forward the implied 2027 EPS is $26.87, which does not match $24-25, implying the forward P/E is closer to 38x. The overnight consensus run should settle this; if 2027 consensus EPS is really $24.50 then GEV trades at 38.4x and my multiple argument gets stronger, not weaker.
  - Q1'25 gas GW shipped and converted. My series is anchored at Q1'25 ending B=29 / S=21 from a secondary source (X post, corpus chunk 217497) cross-checked against Strazik's '50 gigawatts under contract' on the 23 Apr 2025 call. The flow model closes perfectly from Q2'25 forward, but I have no Q1'25 or FY24 conversion observations, so my conversion series is five quarters, not nine. The Q1'25 and Q4'24 numbers would let me test whether the seasoned conversion rate was ever above 40%.
  - GEV's exact 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance as of 22 Jul. The mgmt_guidance row for 'ADJUSTED EBITDA MARGIN*' stated_on 2026-07-22 is garbled (value '2026', prior_value '96%'). I used the 22 Apr guide of 12-14%. If July raised it to, say, 13-15%, FY26 EBITDA is $6.44B not $6.21B and the FY26 cross-check target moves from $583 to $604 — small, but it should be read off the actual press release.
  - Whether the SRA deposit is credited against price or is a separate fee, and what GEV's stated remedy is if a reservation lapses. The Maxim Power Q1'26 filing establishes a non-refundable deposit credited to price with price set later in the definitive agreement — one data point, one small customer, one 7HA.02. I need two or three more customer-side descriptions (NRG, VST, CEG, and the hyperscalers) to know whether lapse-and-resell is economically good or bad for GEV. NRG's disclosure of its 1.2 -> 2.4 -> 3.6 GW reservation vanished from its 2026 10-Qs, which is suggestive but is an absence, not evidence.
  - Siemens Energy's FQ4 (quarter ending 30 Sep 2026) conversion figures, which report in mid-November — after our deadline. If Siemens' 46.2% was a one-quarter spike rather than a run rate, the peer comparison that carries pillar 1 weakens considerably. I have Siemens' own 6-12 month stated target as support, but only one quarter of observed conversion data against GEV's five.
  - Options positioning, short interest and ownership — being gathered by the separate overnight run. Relevant here because a 31% downside target on a heavily-owned, high-momentum name with a dated binary catalyst six days after the finals is a crowded-trade question as much as a fundamental one.

## [Build] build:L_derating_mispricing

- **data_gaps**:

The overnight consensus run must confirm 2027 adj EPS near $24-25 and, more importantly, whether the sell side already models the full 20% 2028 margin. If consensus already sits at 20%, my 'market discounts only 85.8% of the plan' framing is measuring analyst optimism, not a mispricing.
  - Peer FORWARD EV/EBITDA. I only have trailing operating income for VRT/ETN/PWR (no D&A in comps_inputs), so my relative-value claim rests on EV/Sales (GEV 6.3x corrected vs VRT 9.4x, ETN 6.7x) and EV/RPO (GEV 1.36x vs ETN 12.2x, PWR 2.90x). Trailing EV/EBIT flatters nobody: GEV 173x vs ETN 49x, VRT 53x. A proper forward comp table could weaken the 25x default materially.

GEV held $13.120B cash at 2026-06-30 (xbrl_facts, tag CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents). Correct EV is $240.115B. Every EV-based number anyone on the team pulls from that table is 5.5% too high. This needs fixing before the model is built.

  - The Dec 2026 investor update date is unannounced. The Dec 2025 event produced +15.6% the next day on 3.75x volume and fully reversed within 5 sessions. If a 2026 update is scheduled inside the horizon it is a second catalyst; the reversal history says do not underwrite it.
  - Whether GEV bills LTSA on actual or factored fired hours. Unresolved across three prior runs. It does not change my four pillars but it sets the sign on the services annuity, which is the largest single component of the 2030s value the Jefferies note is capitalizing.
  - Short interest, options positioning and the identity of the seller. August average daily volume of 2.03M was the lowest month in 14 months while price fell, which is consistent with supply exhaustion, but I cannot distinguish that from passive drift without positioning data.
- **dated_test**: Oct 28 2026, Q3'26 earnings (confirmed; note this lands AFTER the Oct 22-24 finals, so it tests the trade, not the pitch). Four numbers decide it. (1) Gas equipment backlog + slot reservations: must print >=120 GW to stay on the >=125 GW year-end path raised on Jul 22 (Q2'26 was 116 GW; run-rate has been +9 to +16 GW/quarter since Q2'25, per gev_operational.csv). (2) Power segment EBITDA margin: must be >=17.0%, the floor of guidance. H1'26 ran 17.67% ($1,842M / $10,427M, from gev_segments.csv IncomeLossFromContinuingOperations and the two Power revenue rows). (3) Total adjusted EBITDA margin: H1'26 was ~10.3%; FY guide of 12-14% requires H2 at ~15.1%. Q3 must print >=12.5% or the FY guide is arithmetically unreachable. (4) FY26 FCF guidance must be maintained at $11.5-12.5B. An earlier and cheaper read: GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, and Jul 22 2026 (-8.69%) was itself a negative surprise despite the raise, so the Oct 28 reaction is a clean test of whether the market has stopped punishing good prints.
- **dollars_per_share**: CHAIN A -- the de-rating, which is the entry point and the largest single number.

Shares 266,333,581. Price $940.33. Market cap = 940.33 x 266,333,581 = $250.441B.
Balance sheet 2026-06-30 (xbrl_facts): cash $13.120B, debt $2.794B, so net cash = $10.326B = $38.77/share.
EV = 250.441 + 2.794 - 13.120 = $240.115B.
(The corpus comps_inputs table reports EV $253.235B because it deducts no cash. That is a 5.5% error and it must be corrected before anyone models this.)

2028 adjusted EBITDA anchor = $56.0B revenue x 20% margin = $11.20B. Both figures are management's own, from the Dec 2025 investor update and repeated verbatim in the 2026-04-03 DEF 14A.
EV / 2028E EBITDA today = 240.115 / 11.20 = 21.44x.
At the Jun 30 2026 peak of $1,174.86: mcap = $312.90B, EV = 312.90 + 2.794 - 13.120 = $302.58B, so 302.58 / 11.20 = 27.02x.

De-rating = 27.02 - 21.44 = 5.58 turns.
5.58 turns x $11.20B = $62.50B of enterprise value.
$62.50B / 266,333,581 = $234.63 per share.
$234.63 / $940.33 = 24.9% of the current price.

That $234.63 is the whole move, and across the same window the 2028 target was unchanged while the FY26 revenue guide, the FY26 FCF guide and the Power organic-growth guide were all RAISED (Jul 22 2026 8-K).

CHAIN B -- what the market is paying for. At the 25x default, $240.115B EV implies perpetual adjusted EBITDA of 240.115 / 25 = $9.605B. That is 9.605 / 11.20 = 85.8% of the 2028 target, capitalised with zero growth after 2028. The stock is priced for GEV to reach 86% of its own plan and then stop forever.

CHAIN C -- the operating pillars, each at 25x / 266,333,581 shares.
Power margin already delivered: H1'26 Power segment EBITDA $1,842M vs H1'25 $1,302M = +$540M; annualised +$1,080M. x25 = $27.00B / 266,333,581 = $101.38/share = 10.8% of $940.33.
Wind to breakeven from the FY26 guide of -$400M: +$400M x 25 = $10.00B / 266,333,581 = $37.55/share = 4.0%.
FY26 FCF guidance raise of $5.0B at the midpoint ($7.0B to $12.0B): valued at 1x, NOT 25x, because it is mostly working capital and non-refundable deposits rather than earnings: $5.0B / 266,333,581 = $18.77/share = 2.0%.

TARGET. 25x x $11.20B = $280.0B EV, + $10.326B net cash = $290.33B equity, / 266,333,581 = $1,090.08, or +15.9% from $940.33.

CROSS-CHECK by EPS, reproduced independently. 2028E adjusted EBITDA $11.20B, less D&A ~$2.0B (H1'26 ran $759M, rising with Prolec), plus ~$0.5B net interest income on the $13.1B cash and $40.0B deposit float = $9.70B pre-tax; x 0.76 after a 24% rate = $7.37B; add back intangible amortisation of ~$0.95B x 0.76 = $0.72B; adjusted net income $8.09B. On ~255M shares after two more years of buyback, 2028E adjusted EPS = $31.74. Today's $940.33 is 29.6x that. The $1,090 target is 34.3x 2028E adjusted EPS -- the same ~35x forward multiple GEV carries today, simply rolled one year forward. The EBITDA route and the EPS route agree.
- **implied_target**: $1,090 base (+15.9%), = 25x 2028E adjusted EBITDA of $11.20B plus $10.326B net cash, cross-checked at 34.3x 2028E adjusted EPS of $31.74. Bull $1,174 (+24.9%), the Jun 30 multiple of 27.0x restored. Bear $796 (-15.4%) at 18x. Risk/reward from $940.33 is +$150 against -$144, roughly 1:1 -- which is honestly poor for a pitch, and the team should know that before choosing this side. The bull case is not a new high; it is merely June's multiple on an unchanged plan.
- **key_assumption**: That GEV reaches its own 2028 framework of $56B revenue at a 20% adjusted EBITDA margin, i.e. $11.20B of adjusted EBITDA, up from ~$5.98B in FY26E -- a 36.9% two-year CAGR driven almost entirely by margin, since revenue only needs to compound 10.3%/yr. The margin expansion from 13% to 20% is doing the work; roughly two-thirds of my target value rests on it. Supporting it: H1'26 Power is already at 17.67% against a 17-19% guide and Electrification at 18.2% against 18-20%, so the segment-level margins are being delivered now rather than promised. Against it: the consolidated FY26 guide of 12-14% needs H2'26 at ~15.1% versus 10.3% in H1'26, which is a real stretch and depends on a revenue ramp from $20.4B to ~$25.6B dropping through at high incremental margin.
- **kill_condition**: Kill the long on any ONE of these at the Oct 28 2026 Q3 print. (1) Power segment EBITDA margin below 17.0% for the quarter -- that is the guidance floor and the margin-convergence pillar is the case. (2) Gas equipment backlog + slot reservations below 120 GW, which makes the >=125 GW year-end target unreachable at the observed +9 to +16 GW/quarter run-rate. (3) FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance cut below 12%, or FY26 FCF guidance cut below $11.5B. (4) A second consecutive quarter of Power equipment revenue growth below 15% year over year -- Q2'26 was +34.1% ($1,957M vs $1,459M), and it is the line that proves cost-to-cost percentage-of-completion is overriding the shipment slowdown; if it converges toward the -40% shipment trend, my third pillar was wrong. Price-based backstop: a close below $795 (18x 2028E EBITDA plus net cash) means the market has rejected the 2028 plan outright rather than merely de-rated it, and the thesis is no longer a multiple argument. Additionally, if the Q3 10-Q shows GEV did NOT repurchase materially through the drawdown (say under $1.0B in Q3 against $2,393M in Q2'26), the strongest non-price confirmation is gone and I would cut the position size rather than exit.
