Halve it -- 2028 margin 16.5% instead of 20%: $56B x 16.5% = $9.24B EBITDA. 25x = $231.0B EV, + $10.326B net cash = $241.3B, / 266,333,581 = $906/share, or -3.6% from $940.33. The stock barely moves, because at 21.44x it already embeds only 85.8% of the plan. Halving the central assumption costs 4%.

Double it -- 2028 margin 27%: $56B x 27% = $15.12B. 25x = $378.0B, + $10.326B = $388.3B, / 266,333,581 = $1,458/share, +55.1%.

That asymmetry (-3.6% against +55.1%) is the honest core of the long, and it exists only because the July-September de-rating already removed most of the plan's value from the price. It is also why I am NOT relying on the multiple: at an unchanged 21.44x, GEV reaching the full $11.20B still gives 240.1/11.2 held constant... the stock compounds with EBITDA. If the multiple contracts a further 16% to 18x while GEV delivers $11.20B, the target is $796, -15.4%. So the downside is a multiple event, not an earnings event, and the position is a bet that 21.44x on a 36.9% two-year EBITDA CAGR is near the floor rather than the middle of a range.

Second sensitivity, on Wind, which is where FY26 is most likely to break: Wind at the H1'26 annualised run-rate of -$1,314M instead of the -$400M guide is a $914M EBITDA shortfall. x25 / 266,333,581 = -$85.78/share, -9.1% of price. H1'26 Wind was -$657M against a full-year guide of -$400M, so H2 must swing +$257M against a best-ever quarter of +$19M. I do not believe the Wind guide, and I have sized the bear case assuming it is missed.
- **side**: LONG
- **strength**: 3
- **thesis_sentence**: The market believes GE Vernova's summer collapse repriced a deteriorating gas franchise, but 78% of the 20% drawdown is the AI-power complex de-rating together (VRT fell more, -25.5%) and the entire GEV-specific residual is the single session of July 22 -- the day GEV raised its free-cash-flow guidance 67%, raised revenue and Power growth guidance, and grew adjusted EBITDA 62% -- so the stock now trades at 21.4x its own 2028 EBITDA target versus 27.0x in June on an unchanged plan, and reverting to 25x on $11.2B gives $1,090.
- **weakest_link**: There is no catalyst inside the horizon that forces the multiple to re-rate, and the Carlisle 2025 precedent is precisely my failure mode rather than my supporting case. Columbia's winning long had the business deliver exactly as pitched -- mid-single-digit growth, Q2'26 EPS +12% to a record, guidance raised -- and the stock is down 11% because the multiple compressed instead of expanding. GEV already ran that exact experiment on July 22 2026: guidance raised, stock -8.69%. My four pillars establish that GEV's numbers are fine. They do not establish that anyone will pay more for them, and "prices move on expectation-minus-result" cuts directly against me.

Three ways GEV genuinely differs from Carlisle, stated as strongly as I can: (1) Entry multiple direction. Carlisle was pitched needing expansion from a normal multiple; GEV is pitched after a 5.58-turn, 20.6% compression on an unchanged plan, so it needs the de-rating only to stop, not to reverse. (2) Growth rate. Carlisle's pillars were 5% organic growth plus buybacks, where nearly all the return is the multiple; GEV's adjusted EBITDA compounds 36.9%/yr from FY26E $5.98B to the 2028 $11.20B, so the earnings line can carry the stock even if the multiple keeps slipping. (3) Contracted versus statistical demand. Carlisle's pillar one was a behavioural forecast from building vintages and warranty data; GEV's is $87.8B of equipment RPO with 65% recognising inside two years and $40.0B of non-refundable customer cash already banked.

Where it does NOT differ, and this is the real weakness: GEV is a crowded consensus long -- roughly 37 analysts, mostly Buy, average target ~$1,236 -- so there is no variant perception. Carlisle at least had the "buy-side awareness is low" asymmetry. I am arguing the same direction as the entire sell side, at a price 24% below their average target, which means my edge is timing and framing rather than information, and that is the thinnest kind of edge to defend in front of judges.

Two further honest weaknesses. First, my strongest evidence cuts both ways: the $5.0B FCF raise is, in GEV's own words, "primarily due to higher positive benefits from working capital," which is the short's reservation-conversion argument stated by management. I answer it by valuing that raise at 1x rather than 25x and by noting adjusted EBITDA grew 62% independently -- but a judge who presses on cash quality has a real point. Second, the consolidated FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide of 12-14% requires H2 at ~15.1% against 10.3% in H1'26. Power and Electrification are already inside their segment ranges, so the gap is Wind (which must swing +$257M against a best-ever +$19M quarter) and the revenue ramp. If H2 misses, the 2028 bridge loses its first step and the whole $1,090 goes with it. Finally, the GLJ bear argument -- that 2027 ships 2024-priced orders at ~3pts margin versus 10-11pts on the 2025 vintage -- is about 2027, and nothing in my H1'26 data falsifies it. I show margins expanding now; I cannot show they expand through the 2027 vintage-mix trough.

- **weakest_link**: Six places this case is vulnerable, ranked. (1) THE BIGGEST: this is a timing call on an order book that has beaten for eight straight quarters. Deposits are non-refundable and management treats the mechanism as structural, not one-off. Nothing says the slot calendar stops at 2031 — if AI-datacenter demand extends the book to 2033-2034, collections can run at $25-30B a year for several more years and my 2027 thesis is simply early by two years, which for a 3-12 month horizon is the same as being wrong. (2) One fact in the filings cuts directly against my timing: equipment RPO expected within 12 months fell from 46% (Q3'24) to 36% (Q2'26). A lengthening book means deposits sit LONGER before liquidating, which keeps ΔCL positive longer than my model assumes. I am arguing the balance stops growing in 2027 while GEV's own disclosure shows the liquidation clock slowing. (3) I cannot decompose contract liabilities between SRA reservation deposits and firm-order down payments — GEV does not disclose it. My $315M-per-GW deposit rate is derived from a segment balance change, not disclosed, and the whole collections model rests on it. (4) "Earned FCF is negative" is partly an artifact of growth, not deterioration: inventory went $8.6B to $12.7B because output is scaling from ~15 GW to 24 GW. A bull will say earned cash is negative precisely because GEV is building the capacity that generates the 2029-2030 cash, and that is a fair rebuttal — my own model concedes it by putting 2027 earned FCF at +$2.0B. (5) Q3'26 is likely to look like a beat: GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, and YTD FCF will still print enormous. The short can take a sharp mark-to-market loss on Oct 28 even if every word of this is right. (6) I am modeling against an ASSUMED consensus 2027 FCF of $11.5B. If the sell side already carries $6-7B, my $8.5B gap collapses to $3.5B and most of the $/share evaporates — the thesis would then be largely priced.

But an investor who values GEV on cash it has actually earned finds a company with essentially no free cash flow trading at $250 billion.

Second, and more uncomfortable: the "$24 billion cumulative 2025-28" floor, read literally, IS the bear's cliff. It implies 2027+2028 FCF of $8,290M combined, $4,145M/yr, versus $12,000M in 2026. I am arguing that a January number set against a $5.25B FY26 guide is stale. But management has had two subsequent opportunities — April 22 and July 22 2026 — to raise that cumulative figure while raising FY26 twice, and did not. That silence is more consistent with management viewing the FY26 upside as pull-forward than with my reading. I could find no reaffirmation or restatement of the 2028 outlook in the July 22 materials in this corpus; I am inferring from absence, which is weak.

Third: the drawdown is less GEV-specific than the framing suggests. From the June 30 2026 common date through Sep 18 2026 (prices table): GEV -20.0%, VRT -25.5%, PWR -11.6%, ETN -0.3%, SPY +2.0%. GEV underperformed the equal-weighted VRT/ETN/PWR basket by about 7.5 points — real, but Vertiv fell harder. Part of what I am calling a mispricing is an AI-power-complex de-rating that GEV alone cannot fix.

Fourth: valuation. At my $1,146 target GEV trades at 42x the 2028 EPS that management's own framework implies. Nothing in this cash-engine case makes the stock cheap. It makes the feared catalyst already-disclosed and the next three catalysts favourably dated. That is a trade, not a valuation — and the team should say so rather than dress it up.

Fifth: GEV spent $3,671M on buybacks in H1'26 (Q1 $1,278M + Q2 $2,393M) funded out of customer deposit cash while ending the quarter with $13.1B of cash against $39.9B of contract liabilities. The float is not sitting in a bank account; it has been spent on Prolec, inventory and stock. If signings stop, GEV has less cushion than the headline balance implies.

- **sensitivity**: Key assumption is the 2027 Power incremental EBITDA margin of 20% (vs ~34% required by the path). HALVED to 10%: 2027 Power EBITDA = 4,234 + 0.10 × 3,277 = $4,562M → 17.02% margin (a decline vs 2026). Shortfall $798M → $798M × 25 ÷ 266,333,581 = $74.92/share = 7.97% of $940.33. Adjusted 2027 EBITDA $7,757M; at 21x = $167.5B equity ÷ 266.334M = $629/share, −33%. DOUBLED to 40%: 2027 Power EBITDA = $5,545M → 20.69% margin, which BEATS the path by $185M. The short fails outright — GEV would be ahead of the 2028 22% bridge and the 28.7x multiple gets defended, not compressed. Note the break-even is at 34% incremental: at 34% the shortfall is $12M, i.e. zero. So the entire case lives in the band between roughly 10% and 30% incremental margin, and the distance from my 20% to the break-even 34% is only 14 points of incremental margin on $3.3B of revenue. That is a thin margin of safety for a short. Second-order sensitivity: if 2027 Power revenue comes in at $28.0B instead of $26.8B (GEV beats on volume), the path EBITDA rises to $5,600M but my case rises to $5,129M — the shortfall WIDENS to $471M→$471M at constant incremental margin, so the case is not volume-sensitive; it is purely a margin call.
- **side**: SHORT
- **strength**: 2
- **thesis_sentence**: The market is paying ~29x 2027 EV/EBITDA for a Power segment margin bridge from 18% (2026) to 22% (2028) that requires GE Vernova to sustain a ~34% incremental EBITDA margin through the single largest production ramp in its history; management's own 2026 guidance already shows that incremental rate falling from 44% in the first half to 31% in the second half — the exact half the ramp lands in — and if 2027 converts at a normal 20% instead, Power EBITDA comes in ~$490M light, 2027 adjusted EPS is ~$1.38 short, and the 2028 framework that justifies the multiple loses its credibility, taking the stock to roughly $680.
- **weakest_link**: TWO WEAK POINTS, AND THE FIRST IS FATAL TO THE ASSIGNMENT AS WRITTEN. (1) THE GLJ VINTAGE ARGUMENT DOES NOT SURVIVE MY OWN WORK, AND THE TEAM MUST NOT PITCH IT. GLJ says 2027 ships 2024-priced orders at ~3 pts of margin. That confuses SHIPMENT with RECOGNITION. GEV recognizes equipment revenue over time on cost-to-cost percentage of completion ("based on our costs incurred to date relative to our estimate of total expected costs" — FY25 10-K), so a unit's margin flows as its cost is incurred, roughly the 24-36 months BEFORE delivery, not at delivery. Run the roll-forward: Power equipment RPO was $12,461M at Dec-31-2024; FY25 Power equipment revenue was $6,420M and FY26 is running ~$8.6B. Under FIFO the entire 2024-vintage Power equipment book is exhausted in revenue terms around Q3 2026. The 2024-priced units GLJ points at have ALREADY put most of their margin through the 2025 and 2026 P&L — which is why FY25 Power margin was only 14.7%. 2027 runs largely on the 2025-2026 book. If a judge asks "doesn't percentage-of-completion mean the old prices already washed through?", the answer is yes, and the GLJ framing dies on the spot. (2) THE BOOKED BACKLOG MARGIN IS A LARGE, DOCUMENTED, QUANTIFIED TAILWIND SITTING IN 2027-2029 AND I CANNOT OBSERVE IT ERODING. GEV's 4Q'25 press release (Jan 28 2026): "grew equipment margin in backlog by $8B, with 6 pts of accretion." Solve it: equipment backlog (= Product RPO) went $43,047M (Dec-24) → $64,245M (Dec-25); if the margin rose 6 points and the margin dollars rose $8.0B, then 64,245 × (m+0.06) − 43,047 × m = 8,000 → m = 19.56%, ending 25.56% (check: $8,418M → $16,418M, delta exactly $8,000M). So GEV is booking equipment at ~25.6% against an old book at ~19.6%, and that squares with company gross margin running 20.3% in H1'26. My entire case requires the REALIZED margin to fall short of that BOOKED margin — and GEV discloses estimated-profitability revisions only for services contracts, never for equipment. I am inferring equipment cost erosion from a services trail. That inference is the load-bearing wall and it is not directly observable. (3) LESSER BUT REAL: my strongest-sounding fact — that Q3'26 Power margin is guided DOWN to 17-18% from Q2'26's 18.8% into the biggest volume step ever — largely dissolves on seasonality. Q3 historically costs 190-310bps sequentially (Q3'25 16.4%→13.3%, Q3'24 13.8%→11.9%); the guided drag is only 80-180bps, so on a seasonally-adjusted basis Q3'26 is guided BETTER than normal. I killed that argument myself rather than carry it into the room. (4) FINALLY, THE SHAPE OF THE TRADE: 82% of the −28% comes from multiple compression, not the earnings cut. This is a de-rating short on a name already 20% off its June high, into a confirmed Oct 28 catalyst, with 116 GW under contract and ~5 years of sold-out capacity. Shorting a sold-out order book on a margin-timing disagreement is a low-conviction expression of a defensible observation.

- **dollars_per_share**: HEADLINE (volume slice only, Method 1). Line: Power segment EBITDA.
Step 1 — recognized equipment revenue per GW shipped, H1'26 actual: $3,851M Power equipment revenue / 7.5 GW shipped = $513M per GW ($513/kW). Held FLAT to 2028, which is conservative: the ratio has already gone $365 (H1'25) -> $513 (H1'26), and the contract price sitting in backlog is $741/kW.
Step 2 — volume increment: FY26E 17.5 GW (H1 actual 7.5 + H2 guided 5+5) -> FY28E 24 GW (July guidance; Laguna's 7 GW/qtr implies 28). Increment = +6.5 GW.
Step 3 — revenue: 6.5 GW x $513M/GW = +$3,338M of annual revenue.
Step 4 — incremental EBITDA at 35% (the lowest of four observed Power incremental margins: 35.5%, 38.7%, 44.4%, 79.0%): $3,338M x 0.35 = +$1,168M of annual EBITDA.
Step 5 — multiple: x25 = $29,203M of enterprise value. 25x is a deliberate 37% haircut to GEV's own current multiple: EV = ~$250B market cap less ~$12B net cash ($13.1B cash at Jun-30-26) = $238B, over 2026E adjusted EBITDA of 13% x $46B = $5,980M, which is 39.8x.
Step 6 — per share: $29,203M / 266,333,581 = $109.65 per share = 11.66% of $940.33.

REPRODUCED A SECOND WAY (Method 2, independently constructed). Build FY28E Power bottom-up: equipment 24 GW x $513M + $800M nuclear/hydro = $13,123M; services $14.0B (FY26E) grown 7%/yr = $16,029M; total $29,152M at a 20.5% margin = $5,976M EBITDA, versus FY25 actual $2,902M — a +$3,074M EBITDA bridge on +$9,386M of revenue, i.e. a 32.8% blended incremental margin (so my 35% assumption is if anything slightly rich). Volume's share of that revenue bridge is (24 - 15.3 GW) x $513M / $9,386M = 47.6%, so volume carries 0.476 x $3,074M = $1,463M from the FY25 base, of which the 2026-to-2028 portion is (6.5/8.7) x $1,463M = $1,093M. Method 1 $1,168M vs Method 2 $1,093M — a 6.4% spread. Method 2 at 25x = $102.62 per share (10.9%).

FULL POWER BRIDGE (volume + price/mix + the services riding on the same units): FY26E Power revenue $23,523M (FY25 $19,767M x 1.19, the guided 18-20% organic) at 18% = $4,234M EBITDA; FY28E $29,152M at 20.5% = $5,976M. Delta +$1,742M x 25 / 266,333,581 = $163.52 per share = 17.39% of $940.33.
ADD the HA services annuity already sitting in firm backlog: $236M/yr x 25 / 266,333,581 = $22 per share (2.4%).
TOTAL IDENTIFIED: about $185 per share, 19.7% of $940.33.
At GEV's own 39.8x rather than 25x, the full Power bridge is worth $260 per share (28%) — that is the bull case, not my base.

THE FATAL ONE — FLEET AGE, AND THE TEAM ALREADY OWNS THE PROOF. GEV recognizes CSA revenue on cost-to-cost percentage of completion, and the FY2025 10-K says customers pay "per hour of usage" or "upon the occurrence of a major maintenance event within the contract, such as an outage" (verified verbatim, 2026-01-29). A CSA on a unit that has not yet reached its first major outage incurs almost no cost, therefore recognizes almost no revenue and generates almost no event billing. The team's own verified fleet physics from the prior runs: 126 HA units, ~3.6M fired hours, ~28,571 hours each, against a 50,000-hour major interval from GER-3620 Rev P. The average installed HA unit has not reached its first major overhaul; at ~6,000 h/yr it arrives in ~3.6 years. Flat CSA revenue, flat billings, and a flat net CSA balance across a rapidly growing but YOUNG fleet is exactly what this accounting mechanically produces. The case has found the pre-outage trough and labelled it deterioration. Its three headline series — CSA revenue flat, billings flat, net CSA balance flat for ten quarters — are all the same single observation, and all three have the same innocent explanation.

PILLAR 3 IS ARITHMETIC PERFORMED ON AN EXCLUSION. The Q2'26 10-Q states services RPO covers agreements "which remain unsatisfied at the end of the reporting period, excluding contracts that are not yet active" (verified verbatim, 2026-07-22). Every CSA attached to the 53 GW of undelivered firm equipment backlog is by definition not yet active. Corroborating: the year-one services RPO bucket is $88,463M x 16% = $14.2B, which is ~2.6x TTM CSA revenue of $5.4B — confirming services RPO is the whole services book, not the CSA annuity, so the per-GW comparison is apples to oranges twice over. Pillar 3 is the ONLY pillar that argues the multiple, and the multiple is 78% of the trade.

THE DRAG IS IN THE PRINT AND IN GUIDANCE. FY25 Power EBITDA of $2,902M is net of $151M of revisions. H1'26 Power EBITDA is net of $218M — and grew 46% organically anyway. GEV RAISED full-year guidance on 2026-07-22, the same day it filed the 10-Q disclosing the $218M: revenue $45.5-46.5B, FCF $11.5-12.5B, Power organic 16-18% at a 17-19% margin. The case's central premise — that consensus "carries FY25's $151M" — is asserted and never tested, and the case concedes in data_gaps #1 that it inferred the entire consensus benchmark from the Dec-2025 investor update.

- **verdict**: Reject. This is the best-sourced case I have read this cycle and it still does not clear the bar, which is the most dangerous kind — the footnote archaeology is genuinely excellent and every primary number reproduces to the dollar, so it reads as rigorous right up until you ask what the numbers mean.

Three things kill it. First, 66% of the $552M operating gap is the difference between a 24% "consensus" services margin and a 21.5% short margin, both sitting on a 21% FY25 base that was plugged out of one equation with two unknowns. The team's own prior work contains the data that refutes the case, which means a judge who has read the same fleet physics will get there unprompted.

Every CSA on the 53 GW firm backlog is not yet active. The 4x shortfall to management's $500M/GW and the 11x to Jefferies are both artifacts of measuring a bucket that structurally cannot contain what you are looking for. The author flagged this as weakest_link #2 and then kept the pillar and the de-rate anyway. Once pillar 3 goes, the multiple argument has no evidence behind it and the trade is a 2% earnings quibble on a $250B market cap.

Two credits, honestly earned. The revision series is real, the acceleration is real, and it is the single most underexamined line in GEV's disclosure — that work has value to the LONG team as a risk to monitor. And the case's own scheduling note is the most useful sentence in the document: Oct 28 is after the Oct 22-24 finals, so there is no dated test inside the window. A PM does not put on a narrative short with no catalyst, a published $470 bear already in the tape, a $1,236 average target, and 20 points of de-rate already taken on the lowest volume in 14 months.

For the Sep 26 decision: do not build the SHORT on this. Carry pillar 1 forward as a monitored risk line inside whichever side the team picks, and if anyone asks about services on Oct 28, the answer is fleet age, not deterioration.

So 2027 P&L margin is the weighted margin of contracts INCURRING COST in 2027 — which, on a multi-year heavy-duty build (Strazik: the 2028 step-up to 24 GW depends on castings and forgings arriving in 2027), spans units shipping 2027-2030, i.e. 2025-2027 bookings. (2) Pricing: a slot reservation holds a slot, not a price — price is set in the later definitive agreement — so a 2024 SRA converting in 2026 enters backlog at 2026 prices. GEV quantified this: H1'26 gas equipment orders were priced more than 20% above 4Q'25 orders 'reflecting a conversion of higher-priced SRAs to backlog.' 34 GW converted from SRA to firm order in the five quarters to Jun-2026, all priced at 2025/2026 terms. Note the striking calibration: applying the FY25 realized drop-through of 38.7% to 2027 gives exactly 20.70% — Street consensus. Applying the H1'26 realized 44.5% gives 21.46%. GLJ's 18.5% implies 21.8%, roughly half of anything GEV has posted since the spin. The debate reduces to one number.
- **dollars_per_share**: FULL CHAIN, every step shown.

STEP 1 — 2027 Power revenue. FY25 Power segment revenue $19,767M (FY2025 10-K: Gas 16,006 + Nuclear 1,018 + Hydro 806 + Steam 1,937 = 19,767; reproduces the segment total exactly). FY26E = 19,767 x 1.19 = $23,523M (Jul-22-2026 guide: Power 18-20% organic growth, midpoint 19%). FY27E = 23,523 x 1.15 = $27,051M. The +15% is built from gas output ~17 GW (2026) to 20 GW (2027) = +14% volume, heavy-duty units 62 to 74 = +19%, plus the >20%-higher-priced 2026 order vintage entering revenue, less flat-to-down Steam. Range $26.0-28.0B.

STEP 2 — 2027 Power EBITDA, three ways.
(a) MY BASE, drop-through method: FY26E Power EBITDA = 18.0% (guide 17-19% midpoint) x 23,523 = $4,234M. Incremental revenue 27,051 − 23,523 = $3,528M. Apply the realized H1'26 incremental drop-through of 44.5%: 0.445 x 3,528 = $1,570M. 2027 Power EBITDA = 4,234 + 1,570 = $5,804M -> margin 5,804/27,051 = 21.46%.
(b) GLJ: 18.5% x 27,051 = $5,004M. (Implied drop-through = (5,004 − 4,234)/3,528 = 21.8%.)
(c) STREET: 20.7% x 27,051 = $5,600M. (Implied drop-through 38.7% — identical to GEV's realized FY24->FY25 drop-through. Consensus is literally "2027 repeats FY25.")

STEP 3 — the delta. My base minus GLJ = 5,804 − 5,004 = $800M of 2027 Power segment EBITDA. Cross-check via vintage mix (independent route): 2027 Power equipment revenue ~$11.0B; conservative 2024-vintage content 12.5%; blended equipment margin 0.125 x 3pts + 0.875 x 13pts = 11.75pts vs GLJ's ~3pts = 8.75pts x $11.0B = $963M. The two routes bracket $800-963M; I carry $800M.

STEP 4 — multiple. Default 25x, and here is why it is conservative rather than generous: GEV's own current EV/EBITDA is 38.9x. Reproduce it — market cap = 266,333,581 x $940.33 = $250,441M; net cash = cash $13,120M (Jun-30-26) − debt $2,849M = $10,271M; EV = $240,170M; FY26E adjusted EBITDA = 13.4% x $46,000M = $6,164M (guide 12-14% margin on $45.5-46.5B revenue); 240,170/6,164 = 39.0x, matching the 38.9x GLJ itself quotes. Capitalizing the 2027 delta at 25x is therefore a ~36% haircut to the multiple the market is paying today.

STEP 5 — dollars per share. $800M x 25 = $20,000M. $20,000M / 266,333,581 shares = $75.07 per share. $75.07 / $940.33 = 7.98% of the current price.
At GEV's own 38.9x instead: $800M x 38.9 = $31,120M / 266,333,581 = $116.83/share = 12.42%.
My view vs Street only (21.46% vs 20.70%): 0.76pts x $27,051M = $206M x 25 = $5,150M / 266,333,581 = $19.34/share = 2.06%.
GLJ's FULL bear gap for scale: $9,450M − $7,420M = $2,030M x 25 = $50,750M / 266,333,581 = $190.55/share = 20.3% of the price. Critically, only $596M of that $2,030M (2.2pts x $27.05B = 29%) is the vintage argument; 71% of GLJ's cut sits in revenue and other segments they have not publicly justified. Winning the vintage argument outright is worth ~$56/share of GLJ's own gap at 25x, not $190.

GEV's Dec-2025 outlook was $56B revenue at 20% adjusted EBITDA margin = $11,200M; refreshed for the FY26 beat (guide raised twice to $45.5-46.5B vs the $44-45B assumed when the 2028 outlook was set) and Power at 18-20% growth, 2028E = $58B at 20.5% = $11,890M. At 25x: 25 x 11,890 = $297,250M + net cash $10,271M = $307,521M / 266,333,581 = $1,154.63. Low end = 25x the stale $11,200M + net cash = $290,271M / 266.33M = $1,089.92. High end = 28x $11,890M + net cash = $343,191M / 266.33M = $1,288.60. Base sits BELOW the $1,236 Street average and well below Guggenheim's $1,450 — I am not out-bulling the Street, I am arguing GLJ's $470 requires both a 22% EBITDA cut and a collapse to 15.5x on their own 2027 number ($470 x 266.33M = $125.2B cap, less $10.3B net cash = $114.9B EV / $7.42B = 15.5x), a multiple GEV has never carried.
- **key_assumption**: Incremental EBITDA drop-through in Power of 44.5% on 2027 revenue growth. This single number carries the entire valuation. It is not invented — it is exactly what GEV realized in H1'26 ((1,842−1,302)/(10,448−9,234)) and close to the 38.7% realized FY24->FY25. But it is only one and a half years of history, taken during a period when GEV was simultaneously absorbing training-mode labour for the 15->20 GW Greenville ramp, raising R&D+capex ~30% year-over-year, and expanding margin anyway.
- **sensitivity**: HALVED to 22.25%: 2027 Power EBITDA = 4,234 + 0.2225 x 3,528 = $5,019M -> margin 18.55%. That is GLJ's 18.5% to within 5 basis points. The delta versus GLJ collapses from $800M to $15M = $1.41/share at 25x. The LONG case is completely gone — not damaged, gone. This is the honest shape of the bet: halving the drop-through does not halve the case, it erases it, because GLJ's number IS the half-drop-through case.
DOUBLED to 89%: 2027 Power EBITDA = 4,234 + $3,140M = $7,374M -> margin 27.26%. Delta vs GLJ = $2,370M x 25 = $59,250M / 266,333,581 = $222.47/share = 23.7% of the price. (For reference, an analyst on the Q3'25 call put last-cycle peak Power margins at "approaching 25%", so 27% is above any historical precedent and should be treated as a ceiling, not a scenario.)
Asymmetry note: the downside case is a real, reachable number and the upside case is not. That is the most uncomfortable fact in this write-up.
- **dated_test**: TEST 1 — Q3'26 earnings, Wednesday 28 October 2026 (confirmed; note it falls AFTER the Oct 22-24 finals, so the team cannot use it live). Watch three printed numbers against management's own 22-July guidance: (i) Power segment EBITDA margin, guided to "approximately 17% to 18%" (deliberately below Q2'26's 18.8% because of capacity-investment expense — do not misread the step-down as vintage damage); (ii) gas turbine shipments, which must be ~5 GW to validate the "20 GW annualized run rate starting in the third quarter"; (iii) the SRA-to-order conversion, where Strazik guided 2H'26 gas equipment orders to carry dollars-per-kW "at the higher end of the range of 10 to 20 points versus 4Q '25 orders" — the direct repricing evidence.
TEST 2 — the decisive one — January 2027 earnings call (date not yet announced; the 2026 equivalent was 28 January). At Laguna on 16 September 2026 Strazik committed that GEV will "provide its 2027 financial outlook and disclose its 2026 equipment backlog margin change" on that call. GEV therefore publishes, on the record, the exact metric that adjudicates GLJ: the 2025 print was +6 points and "at least $8 billion." Prior-year evidence that this catalyst moves the stock: the December 2025 investor update produced +15.6% on 3.75x volume.
- **kill_condition**: Any ONE of the following kills the LONG; exit, do not average.
(1) Q3'26 (Oct 28 2026): Power segment EBITDA margin prints below 17.0% — i.e. below the bottom of management's own two-week-old 17-18% quarterly guide — or FY26 Power margin guidance is cut from 17-19%. Either says the drop-through is already breaking before 2027's volume even arrives.
(2) Q3'26 gas turbine shipments below 4.5 GW, which breaks the 20 GW annualized run rate and with it the ~$3.5B of 2027 incremental Power revenue that the whole $800M rests on (at 44.5% drop-through, every 1 GW of 2027 shortfall costs roughly $145M of EBITDA = $13.60/share at 25x).
(3) January 2027 call: 2026 equipment backlog margin change disclosed at below +4 points year-over-year (versus +6 in 2025), or equipment margin dollars added below $6B against the "at least $8 billion" commitment.
(4) January 2027 call: 2027 Power segment EBITDA margin guided below 19.0%. That is the cleanest single kill — it would put management within ~50bp of GLJ and more than 250bp below my base, and it would mean GLJ read the backlog better than GEV's own disclosures did.
- **weakest_link**: Three places, stated plainly.
(1) THE TRADE IS MOSTLY ALREADY PAID. GEV closed at $957.27 on 11 Sep, fell 8.62% to $874.76 on 14 Sep on 3.30M shares (versus 1.2-1.7M normal) when GLJ initiated, and by the 18 Sep close of $940.33 had already recovered $65.57 of the $82.51 gap — about 79%. Only ~$17/share of GLJ-specific damage is left to reverse. The other ~$239 of the drawdown from the $1,196 June peak is AI-power-complex de-rating that my ledger work says nothing about. If the team pitches "GLJ is wrong" as the reason to be long, the honest answer is that the market largely agreed within four sessions.
(2) FIFO IS MY MODEL, NOT GEV'S DISCLOSURE. Nowhere does GEV state that delivery sequencing follows order sequencing. Turbine slots are project-specific and a customer whose site or EPC slips pushes delivery right — exactly the mechanism that could strand a 2024-priced unit in 2027. My own conservative bound concedes 10-15% of 2027 Power equipment revenue could be pre-2025 vintage, and GEV's Dec-2024 all-segment RPO decay (69% recognized within two years, 93% within five) explicitly leaves 31% of that book recognizing after 2026. The "zero 2024 vintage in 2027" version is the aggressive end of the range, not the centre.
(3) THE SENSITIVITY IS BRUTAL AND ONE-SIDED. Halving the drop-through lands on GLJ's exact number. And 2027 carries real, GEV-disclosed cost headwinds — R&D plus capex up ~30% year-over-year in 2026, ongoing capacity-investment expense that management is already using to guide Q3'26 Power margin DOWN to 17-18%, castings-and-forgings dependency for the 2028 step-up, and Section 232 tariff exposure. A tape that reads the guided Q3 step-down as confirmation of GLJ can take the stock materially lower before January arrives, and I would have no rebuttal until the 2027 outlook is published.

PILLAR 1 — HA services step-up 2025→2028.

    2027: 154 units, 43 events → 0.798 → 0.874 → 154 × 10 × 0.874 = $1.35B
    2028: 189 units, 57 events → 0.862 → 0.914 → 189 × 10 × 0.914 = $1.73B

  +$0.72B × 30% = +$216M EBITDA
  $216,000,000 ÷ 266,333,581 = $0.811/share
  $0.811 × 25 = $20.28/share = 2.16% of $940.33

PILLAR 2 — CSA net-unfavorable-revision line reverting.

  $0.605 × 25 = $15.11/share = 1.61% of $940.33
  (Bull, line goes to zero: +$436M → $1.637/share × 25 = $40.93/share = 4.35%.)

PILLAR 3 — Power services growth above the recent run rate.
  Power services revenue (XBRL, OperatingSegments;Service;PowerSegment, $M): FY24 12,391; FY25 13,072 (+5.9%); Q1'26 3,084 (+4.5% y/y); Q2'26 3,509 (+7.0% y/y); H1'26 6,593 (+5.8%).

  $477,000,000 ÷ 266,333,581 = $1.791/share

  $874,000,000 ÷ 266,333,581 = $3.282/share × 25 = $82.04/share = 8.72% of $940.33

MULTIPLE NOTE: 25x is the instructed default and it is conservative here. GEV's market cap ~$250B against 2026 guided revenue $45.5–46.5B at ~14.5% adjusted EBITDA margin (~$6.6B) implies ~38x EV/EBITDA. At the stock's own multiple the base case is $1.791 × 38 = $68.06/share (7.24%) and the bull $3.282 × 38 = $124.72/share (13.3%). I report the 25x numbers as the headline.
- **implied_target**: $985 base ($940.33 + $44.77, +4.8%). $1,022 bull (+8.7%). $1,008 if the base case is capitalized at GEV's own ~38x EV/EBITDA rather than the 25x default. Against a $1,236 street average and a $470–$1,450 range, this pillar alone does not get the stock to the street target — it accounts for roughly one seventh of the gap between $940 and $1,236. The team should treat this as a supporting leg, not the thesis.
- **key_assumption**: Forward fired hours per HA unit per year = 6,300 (72% capacity factor). This single number sets the interval timing (25,000 h hot-gas-path at COD + 3.97 yr; 50,000 h major at COD + 7.94 yr) and therefore the entire event schedule, the yield ratio, and every dollar in the model. It is not a guess: it is solved three independent ways from GEV's own filed installed-base panel (Jun-24→Jun-26: 6,321 h/yr; Sep-24→Dec-25: 6,141; Dec-23→Dec-25 at a 2.2M start: 6,342). But it is a backward-looking average being projected forward, and it is a fleet mean across units running anywhere from ~2,000 to ~8,500 h/yr.
- **sensitivity**: HALVED to ~3,150 h/yr forward (36% capacity factor): intervals stretch to 7.9 yr (HGP) and 15.9 yr (major). The 2026–30 event count falls from 46/yr toward ~22/yr, and modeled 2028 HA services falls from $1.73B to roughly $1.40B. Pillar 1 drops from +$216M to +$117M EBITDA — $0.44/share × 25x = $11/share (1.2%). The case survives but is halved. Critically, it does NOT go to zero, because 4.0M hours are already banked on the meter: hours accumulated are a stock, not a flow, and the 2016–2020 cohorts (56 units) are past 50,000 hours regardless of what happens next.

DOUBLED to ~12,600 h/yr: physically impossible (8,760 hours in a year). The genuine upside bound is ~7,500 h/yr (86% capacity factor, what a data-center-contracted baseload unit runs). Intervals compress to 3.3 yr / 6.7 yr; 2028 HA services reaches ~$1.95B; Pillar 1 rises to +$282M EBITDA = $1.06/share × 25x = $26.50/share (2.8%).

The asymmetry matters: the downside on this assumption is bounded by hours already accumulated, the upside is bounded by the calendar. That is a good shape for a long — and it is also why the total is small.

SECOND-ORDER: the 30% incremental services EBITDA margin scales Pillar 1 linearly. At 20% it is $13.52/share; at 40% it is $27.03/share.
- **dated_test**: Q3'26 earnings, CONFIRMED Oct 28 2026 (after the Oct 22–24 finals, so this tests the thesis but cannot be used in the pitch itself). Three numbers, in priority order:

1. Note 9, "net unfavorable changes in estimated profitability" on contractual service agreements. Q3'25 printed +$6M FAVORABLE. Q1'26 −$89M, Q2'26 −$129M. My case needs Q3'26 better than −$100M. A print better than −$70M (the ten-quarter mean) confirms Pillar 2.
2. Power segment services revenue. Q3'25 was $3,088M. My model implies Q3'26 ≥ $3,300M (+7%) and FY26 Power services ≥ $13.9B (+6.5% on FY25's $13,072M).
3. Power segment EBITDA margin. H1'26 ran 17.6% against a 17–19% full-year guide and a 22% 2028 target. Q3 is seasonally the weak quarter (Q3'25 13.3%); anything above 16% is ahead of the glidepath.

SECOND DATED TEST, and the cleanest one: the FY2026 10-K, filed late January 2027. GEV restates the HA installed base and cumulative operating hours in Item 7 every single year (92/2.0M → 115/2.9M → 126/3.6M). My model predicts Dec-31-2026 at ~134–140 units and ~4.3–4.4M operating hours. That disclosure is a direct, unambiguous read on the 6,300 h/yr assumption.

THIRD: a December 2026 investor update, if GEV holds one (no date announced). The Dec-2025 event produced +15.6% the next day on 3.75x volume — and fully reversed within five sessions, so do not build the case on it. What would matter is Strazik's new number: ~$100B of contracted future HA services revenue by end-2027, versus roughly $32B implied on today's 130 machines. If that goes on a slide, the disclosed annuity triples.
- **kill_condition**: Kill this pillar on ANY of the following:

1. FY2026 10-K (late Jan 2027) reports HA cumulative operating hours below 4.2M. That implies forward accumulation under 5,000 h/unit/yr, stretching the 25,000-hour interval past 5 years and the 50,000-hour major past 10, pushing the wave out of any 3–12 month horizon. (Model predicts 4.3–4.4M; Dec-25 filed 3.6M; Jun-26 press 4.0M.)

2. The CSA "net unfavorable changes in estimated profitability" line prints worse than −$150M in any single quarter in Q3'26 or Q4'26. The worst quarter in the ten-quarter history is −$184M (Q4'24) and the worst recent is −$129M (Q2'26). A print worse than −$150M means the first majors are coming in more expensive than estimated and the wave is landing as a margin headwind, not a tailwind — which flips the sign of Pillar 2 and puts Pillar 1's 30% margin assumption in doubt.

3. FY2026 Power services revenue prints below $13.5B (+3.3% on FY25's $13,072M, i.e. decelerating from FY25's +5.9%). The event count is already supposed to have stepped from 30 (2025) to 39 (2026); if services revenue decelerates through that step, the mechanical link between the outage schedule and the revenue line is not there and the whole construction fails.
- **weakest_link**: Four places, ranked. The first is the one that should decide whether the team uses this.

1. SIZE. On GEV's own disclosed numbers the wave is worth ~$0.72B of incremental revenue over three years on a ~$46B base, and the base-case $/share is $44.77 (4.8%). The mechanism is about as well-evidenced as anything in this corpus — it comes out of GE's own maintenance manual and GEV's own filed fleet panel, and it reproduces management's steady-state yield to the dollar from two independent statements nine months apart. But a high-confidence 5% is not a stock pitch. If the team goes LONG, this is Pillar 3 of a memo, not Pillar 1.

2. THE MARGIN SIGN IS GENUINELY UNRESOLVED, AND IT IS THE SAME ARITHMETIC. The 2024 HA Users Group reported findings from the 7HA.02 fleet-leader major inspection (spring 2024, unit at over 48,000 hours and 162 starts): stage-1 bucket thermal-barrier-coating spallation, through-wall holes in airfoil leading-edge regions, deformed stator vane ring horizontal joint keys, stator vane ring segment tab wear — against roughly 75 TILs on the platform. A 9HA.01 fleet leader had a 72-day outage in 2020 for a shaft-line vibration issue and a 23-day outage extension in 2023 before its major. Of 64 attendees grading GEV's collaboration, 40 gave a C or below, with "desperation for spare parts" a common theme. If the majors arrive more expensive than estimated, the identical event schedule that drives my revenue case drives the bear's revision case — more unfavorable changes in estimated profitability, not fewer. I cannot resolve which way it goes from public sources. Source: ccj-online.com/special-report-2024-ha-users-group/.

3. HETEROGENEITY SMEARS THE WAVE. My cohort model runs every unit at the same 6,300 h/yr. Real HA units span roughly 2,000 h/yr (European load-following) to 8,500 h/yr (Middle East and Asian baseload). Heterogeneity does not change the integral — total hours are filed — but it flattens the peak I am claiming. The "57 events in 2028" could realistically be 45. And the model already shows a real 2029–30 air pocket from the 2022–23 commissioning trough (11 units each year) that I am not hiding.

4. THE COHORT DISTRIBUTION IS FITTED, NOT OBSERVED. I have no unit-level HA commercial-operation-date list. The projects table (420 rows, 130 GE-linked) has no usable HA COD series and EIA-860M carries no OEM or model field. My pre-2024 cohort split is the one curve of three tested that reproduces the filed "over two million hours" at Dec-2023 (2.07M vs 1.86M flat and 1.64M back-loaded) — a real constraint, but one curve passing a single test is not the same as an observed distribution. Also: not every HA unit is on a GEV contractual service agreement. The 10-K says roughly 1,800 of ~7,000 gas turbines are under LTSA; HA attachment is surely far higher but is nowhere disclosed. If HA attachment is 80% rather than 100%, my per-unit revenue arithmetic overstates by a fifth.
- **strength**: 2
- **data_gaps**:
  - Whether GEV bills LTSAs on ACTUAL or FACTORED fired hours. The 10-K says 'per hour of usage'; GER-3620's 25,000/50,000 intervals are in FACTORED fired hours. I searched the corpus for 'factored fired hour', 'factored hours', 'equivalent operating hour' and found nothing from GEV or its customers. If billing is on actual hours while intervals run on factored hours, the wave arrives EARLIER in billing terms than my model. This is the single highest-value unresolved question and it partially flips the sign on the services debate. Probably only resolvable from a customer's LTSA exhibit or an outage-services RFP.
  - HA contractual-service-agreement attachment rate — what share of the 130 operating HA units are actually under a GEV CSA. Never disclosed. My per-unit arithmetic assumes 100%; the whole-fleet LTSA attachment is ~26% (1,800 of ~7,000 units). Scales Pillar 1 linearly.
  - Gas Power services EBITDA margin. GEV discloses Power segment margin (H1'26 17.6%) but never a services-only margin. My 30% incremental assumption is the second-largest lever after the hours rate, and it is unsourced. At 20% Pillar 1 is $13.52/share; at 40% it is $27.03/share.
  - Unit-level HA commercial-operation dates. The projects table has no HA COD series, EIA-860M has no OEM/model field, and no public filing gives the vintage distribution. ## [Redteam] attack1:L_backlog_conversion

- **survives**: False
- **arithmetic_checks_out**: False
- **arithmetic_errors**: Credit where due: I re-derived every headline number from the corpus and the individual computations reproduce exactly. RPO footnote series confirmed verbatim from chunks (id 67387 10-K 2025-02-06 "$43,047 million of which 44%, 69%, and 93%"; id 5683 10-Q 2026-07-22 "$87,821 million of which 36%, 65%, and 97%") and independently from XBRL RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationPercentage/Product. Equipment revenue/cost confirmed from the filed income statement (Q2'26 6,459/5,613 = 13.10% GM; H1'26 11,713/10,328 = 11.82%; H1'25 9,091/8,181 = 10.01%; incremental 475/2,622 = 18.1%). TTM equipment revenue = 5,880+5,963+5,254+6,459 = 23,556. CY2027 contracted = 0.5x31,616 + 0.5x25,468 = 28,542. The 12.1% stale-vintage figure (43,047 x 0.24 / 3 / 28,542) and the 9.59pt blend both reproduce. Five real errors:

(1) DOUBLE-COUNT, the fatal one. Pillar 1 ($59.2) claims contracted revenue is ABOVE the Street's. Pillar 2 ($176.6) claims the market wrongly discounts GLJ and should converge to the Street. These are contradictory premises and the case collects both. Test it: consensus target $1,236 discounted back 12 months at 10% = $1,124 present fair value; vs GLJ's $470, today's $940.33 implies p(bear) = (1,124-940.33)/(1,124-470) = 28.1% (38.6% undiscounted). Killing the bear outright is worth $184/share — i.e. Pillar 2's $176.6 IS the move to consensus, not something on top of it. You cannot then add $59.2 of above-consensus revenue to a target that is consensus.

(2) REALIZATION RATIO CONTAMINATED BY PROLEC. The 110.3% mean is inflated by an acquisition that closed Feb 2 2026 and contributed $1,346M of revenue Feb-Jun. Two of the three forward windows contain Prolec. Ex-Prolec (est. ~$1,200M equipment in the Jun-25 window, ~$450M in the Mar-25 window): Dec-24 110.5%, Mar-25 105.3%, Jun-25 107.1%, mean 107.6% not 110.3%. The case applies a Prolec haircut to Pillar 2 but not to the ratio driving Pillar 1.

(3) "THE SERIES HAS RISEN EVERY SINGLE QUARTER FOR SEVEN QUARTERS" IS FALSE, and the start date is cherry-picked. The full XBRL series includes four 2024 quarters the case omits. 1-year equipment RPO in dollars: Q1'24 18,994 -> Q2'24 19,534 -> Q3'24 19,352 (DOWN) -> Q4'24 18,941 (DOWN) -> then the rising run. The case begins its series precisely at the trough. A declining 1-year dollar bucket — kill-condition #1 — happened twice in the four quarters immediately preceding the window shown.

(4) SHARE COUNT. The case uses 266,333,581. The filed Q2'26 diluted count is 270,000,000 (gev_quarterly.csv SharesDiluted). Using the smaller denominator inflates every $/share figure by 1.4%.

(5) MIX DENOMINATOR NEVER SENSITIZED. Pillar 1's "company-implied" $29,222M = 57.3% x $51.0B. Equipment share is rising monotonically: FY24 54.2%, FY25 55.0%, H1'26 57.3%, Q2'26 58.2% — and full-year Prolec (transformers, equipment-heavy) pushes 2027 higher still. At 58.5% mix the excess falls from $2,259M to $876M; at 60.0% to $111M; at 61.7% it goes negative. The single input that decides whether Pillar 1 exists at all is asserted at a stale half-year value and carries no sensitivity.
- **evidence_holds**: False
- **evidence_problems**: The sourcing is unusually good — better than most pitches I see — and the filings say what the case says they say. But two evidentiary links do not carry the weight placed on them.

(A) BOOKING DATE IS NOT PRICE-SETTING DATE. This breaks Pillar 2, which is 75% of the case. GLJ's claim is that 2027 revenue carries 2024 PRICING. The case rebuts it by mapping RPO BOOKING dates: only 12.1% of CY2027 revenue comes from contracts booked by Dec-31-2024, therefore 87.9% is "2025-or-later vintage," therefore stale pricing is capped. That inference requires price to be set at booking. The case's own corpus says otherwise: the Maxim Power filing (already in the brief) establishes that a GEV slot reservation fixes a deposit but "price is set later in the definitive agreement." Large gas-island orders are negotiated 6-18 months before signature, so orders booked through mid-2025 were priced in 2024. The 12.1% is a FLOOR on stale-priced exposure, not the cap the case calls it. If stale-priced exposure is 35% rather than 12.1%, the blend becomes 0.35x3 + 0.65x10.5 = 7.88pts — which is BELOW the ~10.5pts consensus already assumes, and Pillar 2 flips from +$1,882M of EBITDA to roughly -$742M. The case's central pillar is one definitional slip away from arguing the short side.

(B) THE 110.3% REALIZATION RATIO IS n=3, ALL FROM ONE UPCYCLE, AND CONTAINS AN ACQUISITION. The case concedes n=3 and concedes the single-period problem. It does not concede that the highest of the three observations (112.8%) is the one most contaminated by Prolec. Strip the acquisition and the spread narrows to 105-110% — and the whole of Pillar 1 lives inside that 5-point band.

(C) MINOR, IN THE CASE'S FAVOR: data_gap #4 resolves. XBRL confirms the Q3'24 1-year percentage was 0.46 on $42,069M of equipment RPO. The team may quote "46% to 36%." That gap was real and is now closed.

(D) The "even spread within bucket" assumption is unverifiable and the case says so. I would only add that Q2'26 equipment revenue ($6,459M) already exceeds Q1'26 ($5,254M) by 23%, which is direct evidence of front-loading inside the current 1-year bucket — the case notes this and then does not act on it.
- **already_priced_or_known**: True
- **where**: The RPO timing footnote is XBRL-tagged, machine-readable, and reprinted quarterly. It is in every screen, every quant factor library, and every sell-side model that exists. 37 analysts cover this name. The proposition that a tagged disclosure filed on 2026-07-22 is undiscovered on 2026-09-23 is not credible, and the case never tests it — it asserts an information edge over the Street while simultaneously admitting (in weakest_link) that consensus "almost certainly already embeds roughly 10-point equipment margins."

Quantified: at consensus target $1,236 discounted 12 months at 10% = $1,124, today's $940.33 implies only 28% weight on the GLJ bear. Eliminating the bear entirely is worth $184/share. Pillar 2's $176.6 is therefore a restatement of the existing analyst-target gap, not an increment to it. The case is a re-rating argument wearing an earnings-beat costume, which the author honestly flags and then prices as though it were both.

Worse, the multiple is incoherent with the price. The case applies 25x to its deltas and calls that conservative "because GEV trades at 38-41x EV/EBITDA." Run it the other way: 266.3M x $940.33 = $250.4B of equity; at the case's own 25x that already requires ~$10.0B of EBITDA. GEV's own 2028 target of ~$56B revenue at H1'26's realized adjusted-EBITDA margin (2,146/20,442 = 10.5%) produces $5.9B; even at a generous 15% it is $8.4B. At the multiple the case chose, today's price already discounts more EBITDA than the company's own 2028 plan delivers. Every dollar of the $235.80 sits on top of a price that is already ahead of the plan.
- **killer_question**: You capitalize your delta at 25x and call it conservative because the stock trades at 39x. Run it backwards: at your own 25x, today's $250B market cap already requires $10.0B of EBITDA, while GE Vernova's own 2028 target of ~$56B revenue at its realized 10.5% adjusted-EBITDA margin produces $5.9B. So tell me the 2028 EBITDA number the market is actually paying for today — and then show me that your $235.80 is not already inside it. Because if 25x is the right multiple the stock is expensive before you add a dollar, and if 39x is the right multiple then the market is already paying for exactly the ramp your footnote claims to reveal.
- **revised_dollars_per_share**: +$23/share (+2.4%), with an honest range of $0 to $39. Implied target ~$963, not $1,176.

Build, using the case's own framework with the errors corrected:

PILLAR 2 -> $0 of incremental value. Not because the arithmetic is wrong (it reproduces) but because it is not additive. It is a rebuttal of a single sell-side outlier whose removal gets you to the Street's own discounted target ($1,124), and the case's implied p(bear) of 28% shows the market has already largely rejected GLJ. It also cannot be stacked on Pillar 1 without asserting that consensus is simultaneously too low (Pillar 1) and correct (Pillar 2). Drop it. -$176.60.

PILLAR 1 -> recomputed:
(a) CY2027 contracted equipment = 0.5 x (36% x $87,821M) + 0.5 x (29% x $87,821M) = 0.5 x $31,616M + 0.5 x $25,468M = $28,542M [accepted; reproduces from 10-Q id 5683]
(b) x realization ratio 107.6% ex-Prolec (Dec-24 110.5%, Mar-25 105.3%, Jun-25 107.1%) = $30,711M
(c) less company-implied CY2027 equipment = 58.5% mix x $51,000M = $29,835M [58.5% trend-extrapolated: FY24 54.2%, FY25 55.0%, H1'26 57.3%, Q2'26 58.2%, plus full-year Prolec]
(d) excess revenue = $30,711M - $29,835M = $876M
(e) x 27.9% incremental adjusted EBITDA margin [(2,146-1,227)/(20,442-17,143)] = $244M EBITDA
(f) $244M / 266,333,581 = $0.92/share of annual EBITDA
(g) x 25 = $22.9/share = 2.4% of $940.33

SENSITIVITY ON THE ONE INPUT THAT MATTERS (equipment mix, which the case never flexed):
  57.3% mix (case's figure): excess $1,489M -> $415M EBITDA -> $39.0/share (+4.1%)
  58.5% mix (my base):       excess   $876M -> $244M EBITDA -> $22.9/share (+2.4%)
  60.0% mix:                 excess   $111M ->  $31M EBITDA ->  $2.9/share (+0.3%)
  61.7% mix:                 NEGATIVE
  With the case's own 5.7% Prolec backlog haircut also applied to Pillar 1 (it applies it only to Pillar 2): contracted falls to $26,917M, x 107.6% = $28,963M vs $29,835M implied = -$872M. Pillar 1 goes NEGATIVE at the case's own haircut.

Using the filed 270.0M diluted share count rather than 266.3M cuts a further 1.4%.

So: +$23/share central, +$39 best case, negative under the case's own Prolec adjustment. That is inside the noise of a $940 stock that moved 20% in ten weeks. There is no position size at which this is worth the risk, and the case offers no quantified downside to size against.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. This is the most carefully sourced case I have been handed and it still fails, which is the instructive part — the research is excellent and the investment conclusion does not follow from it.

The case is honest enough to write its own obituary in weakest_link: "$176.6/share is 'downside that does not happen', not 'upside the Street has missed'." That sentence is correct and it is fatal, because the case then books that $176.6 anyway and stacks $59.2 of above-Street revenue on top of it. You cannot be paid for consensus being right (Pillar 2: the market should converge to the Street's ~$1,236) and for consensus being wrong (Pillar 1: contracted revenue exceeds the Street's) in the same model. Pick one. If it is the re-rating, that is a sentiment bet with no catalyst inside the horizon that matters. If it is the revenue beat, it is worth $23/share and it is not a pitch.

Three further problems any PM finds in ten minutes. The 110.3% realization ratio is inflated by the Prolec acquisition (ex-Prolec 107.6%), and the highest of the three observations is the most contaminated. The claim that the 1-year RPO dollar bucket "has risen every single quarter for seven quarters" is false on the full XBRL series — it fell in Q3'24 and Q4'24, and the case's series starts exactly at that trough, which also means kill-condition #1 is far less exotic than presented. And Pillar 2's central inference — that RPO booking date caps stale-price exposure at 12.1% — requires price to be fixed at booking, which the case's own Maxim Power evidence contradicts. Push stale-priced exposure to 35% and the pillar flips sign.

Then there is the thing the case cannot answer at all: it applies 25x to its deltas while the stock trades at 39x on the base, and calls the lower number conservative. At 25x, $940.33 already discounts ~$10.0B of EBITDA against a 2028 company target that produces $5.9-8.4B. The multiple that makes the deltas look cheap makes the starting price look expensive, and the case never reconciles the two.

What I would actually keep: the RPO bridge is genuinely good work and the Pillar 3 rebuttal (the 46%-to-36% decline is a denominator artifact; the beyond-5-year bucket SHRANK from $3,013M to $2,635M while the book doubled) is correct, well sourced, and worth having in the back pocket. It is a defensive fact, not a thesis. Also note data_gap #4 now resolves in the team's favour: XBRL confirms Q3'24 was 46% on $42,069M, so "46% to 36%" is quotable.

Recommendation to the team: do not pitch this. If they are set on LONG, the thesis has to be something the Street cannot already read off a tagged footnote. And the timing problem is disqualifying on its own — the only dated test lands Oct 28, four days after finals, so they would be defending an un-testable thesis in the room.

(g) The revisions are non-cash cumulative catch-ups against a contract asset. GEV RAISED FY26 guidance (revenue $45.5-46.5B, FCF $11.5-12.5B, Power 17-19% margin) on 2026-07-22, the same document that disclosed the $218M. - **already_priced_or_known**: True
- **where**: The core disclosure has already published twice and the market moved in opposite directions on it, which is fatal to a thesis whose payoff is 78% multiple compression.

2026-04-22 (Q1'26 10-Q, prices table, ticker='GEV'): GEV disclosed $89M of net unfavorable revisions -- 6.95% of Q1 CSA revenue, the worst first quarter in company history and one of the two quarters pillar 1 calls unprecedented. The stock closed at $1,127.56 versus $991.30 the prior session: +13.7%.

2026-07-22 (Q2'26 10-Q): $218M H1 cumulative, 8.11%, the number the entire case is built on. Close $985.03 versus $1,078.81: -8.7%. But guidance was RAISED the same day, and the H1'26 volume data published alongside it (7.5 GW shipped vs 8.2 GW, HA units 8 vs 13) is a far more natural explanation for an equipment-cycle stock. The stock then recovered to $1,018.53 by 2026-08-04 -- above the level from which it fell.

So the exact evidence this short depends on has a demonstrated 50% hit rate on direction, including a +13.7% day on the worst Q1 revision ever printed. The information is public, in the 10-Q, and has been for five months and two quarters.

Separately, the drawdown the case implicitly treats as unrealized downside is already partly taken: $1,196 late June to $940.33 on Sep 18, about -21.5%, on the lowest volume in 14 months. And GLJ Research is already short at $470 (Sep 14, -8.6% that day) -- the bear case is on the tape, just argued on 2024-vintage equipment margin rather than Note 9.

Nothing in the corpus shows any sell-side note engaging with the CSA rollforward, so the specific framing is non-consensus. But non-consensus and mispriced are different things, and the April 22 tape says the market sees this line item and does not trade on it.
- **killer_question**: On April 22, 2026 GEV disclosed the worst first-quarter contract-profitability revision in its history -- $89M, 6.95% of CSA revenue, one of the two quarters you call unprecedented -- and the stock closed up 13.7% that day; on July 22 it disclosed $218M alongside a raised FCF guide and recovered the entire decline within nine sessions. So what is the forcing mechanism that makes this same footnote, disclosed a third time on October 28, compress the multiple from 38x to 29x -- and how would you even know you were right, when your only dated test is a services-RPO bucket rounded to a whole percentage point where 16.49% and 16.50% differ by about $9 million of economics but sit on opposite sides of your kill condition?
- **revised_dollars_per_share**: $18.77 per share, 2.00% of $940.33 -- versus the case's $51.63 operating and $276 total.

Derivation, every step:

STEP 1 -- Baseline, corrected. FY25 Power segment (gev_segments.csv): services $13,072M, product $6,420M, intersegment $276M, total $19,767M, segment EBITDA $2,902M (14.7%). I do NOT solve for a services margin, because the split is unobservable and the case's 21%/2.3% decomposition is one equation with two unknowns. I work the gap in dollars instead.

STEP 2 -- Revision drag. This is the one real leg. TTM to Q2'26 = -6+115+89+129 = $327M on CSA revenue of 1,104+1,588+1,280+1,409 = $5,381M (6.08%). H1'26 annualized = $436M. I carry $400M for 2027, same as the case. But the benchmark is not FY25's $151M: GEV raised FY26 guidance on 2026-07-22 with the $218M already booked, so guidance -- and consensus anchored to it -- already absorbs something above the FY25 rate. I benchmark consensus at $250M, midway between FY25 and TTM. Delta = 400 - 250 = $150M of 2027 EBITDA.

STEP 3 -- Revenue and mix. Marking "consensus" to GEV's actual run-rate rather than the case's 8% strawman: Power services grew 5.5% FY24->FY25. At 6%: $13,072M x 1.06^2 = $14,689M. The short's own 2027 build is $14,466M. Gap = $223M, not $792M. At 22% incremental margin = $49M.

STEP 4 -- Pillar 3: zero. The per-GW arithmetic is a net-versus-gross error; corrected, it supports management. No EBITDA, no multiple credit.

STEP 5 -- Pillar 4: zero. Double-counts STEP 2 by construction.

STEP 6 -- Total 2027 EBITDA gap = 150 + 49 = $199M. Round to $200M.

STEP 7 -- Capitalize at the 25x default: $200M x 25 = $5,000M.

STEP 8 -- Per share: $5,000M / 266,333,581 = $18.77.

STEP 9 -- Percent of price: $18.77 / $940.33 = 2.00%.

STEP 10 -- EPS bridge: $200M x (1 - 0.22) = $156M / 266,333,581 = $0.59 of 2027 adjusted EPS. Consensus ~$24.50 becomes ~$23.91.

STEP 11 -- The multiple. I underwrite zero de-rating from this evidence, and that is the whole disagreement. The case books $215 of its $276 from 38.4x -> 29x. The two dates this evidence actually published, the market re-rated GEV UP 13.7% once and down 8.7% once, then recovered. You cannot claim a 9.4-turn de-rate from a disclosure with a demonstrated coin-flip response. At an unchanged 38.4x on $23.91, the implied target is $918 -- about -2.4%.

Sensitivity that matters: give the short its full $400M-vs-$151M benchmark AND its full $792M revenue gap and you get back to roughly $550M, $51.63/share, 5.5%. Both of those rest on an inferred consensus nobody has verified. The overnight consensus run is therefore not a refinement to this case -- it is the case.

Bottom line for the team: this is a real, well-sourced, non-consensus accounting observation worth about $19/share of defensible value, roughly 2% of the price, packaged as a $276 short. Against a ~$250B market cap it is 0.2% of market value on the EBITDA math. It is not a pitch. It is a good slide inside someone else's pitch.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. Kill it as a standalone short; keep pillars 1 and 2 as a risk slide.

What survives and is genuinely good: the Note 9 quarterly series. I tried to break it and could not. Every YTD figure verifies verbatim against the filings, the rollforward closes to the dollar at Jun-26, and the CSA asset is 100% Power with literal zeros at Wind and Electrification -- which kills the obvious "Wind contract losses are polluting the series" rebuttal before it starts. Every quarter of 2026 is the worst on record for that quarter. That is real, non-consensus work: nothing in the corpus shows any sell-side note engaging with this rollforward.

Why it still dies, in order of severity:

1. The payoff is 78% multiple compression, and the evidence for compression is affirmatively contradicted by the tape. GEV printed the worst Q1 revision in company history on 2026-04-22 and closed +13.7%. It printed the $218M on 2026-07-22, fell 8.7% on a day it also RAISED FCF guidance, and recovered the whole move by August 4. A generalist market has now received this disclosure twice and has not re-rated the stock on it. There is no forcing mechanism in a 3-12 month horizon that makes a third printing different.

2. Pillar 3 is a computation error that reverses when fixed. Dividing a net RPO change by GW ignores $6,593M of H1'26 services revenue run-off. Corrected, GEV booked ~$455M of services RPO per GW against management's ~$500M -- a 9% shortfall, not 4x. A PM who has covered this name will find this in under a minute, and finding it costs the team the room, because the rest of the case then reads as motivated rather than derived.

3. The operating gap is a difference between two numbers the author constructed. No disclosure gives Power services EBITDA margin; STEP 1 assumes one and solves for the other. STEP 2's 8% "consensus" growth is above GEV's actual 5.5%. Mark both to observable reality and $552M becomes about $200M. The case flags this in its own data gaps, which is honest, but it means the headline number is an assumption wearing a footnote's clothes.

4. The dated test cannot resolve. It lands Oct 28, five weeks after the Oct 22-24 finals -- the case says so itself, to its credit -- and the third leg turns on a percentage rounded to a whole point, where 16.49% and 16.50% flip the kill condition on ~$9M of economics. The team would be pitching a thesis it cannot prove during the competition and could not cleanly prove afterward.

5. Scale and direction of travel. $200M of corrected EBITDA gap is 0.08% of a $250B market cap. Meanwhile H1'26 gas orders ran 20.1 GW vs 12.2 GW, equipment RPO rose 143% YoY to $87.8B, contract liabilities went $17.6B to $39.9B in eighteen months, and Electrification margin expanded 13.0% to 18.2%. This is a margin story inside a volume story, and the volume story is enormous and moving the other way.

The one thing I cannot answer either, and neither can the bulls: whether CSAs attached to the 53 GW firm backlog are excluded from services RPO until commissioning, and how large that excluded book is. The FY2025 10-K says services RPO excludes contracts "not yet active" and never sizes it. The case names this as its load-bearing unknown and is right to. But note the asymmetry -- if the exclusion is large, pillar 3 is worthless AND the flat-RPO observation in pillar 2 loses most of its force. The unknown only cuts against the short.

Recommendation to the team: if you go SHORT on Sep 26, go with GLJ's argument -- equipment margin on the 2024-priced order vintage shipping into 2027 at ~3pts versus 10-11pts on the 2025 vintage. That is a bigger number, it is about the segment that actually drives adjusted EPS, and it tests on the same Oct 28 print with a sign the market has historically traded. Carry the Note 9 series as a supporting slide, not the thesis. And if you go LONG, this series is exactly the bear question a judge will ask -- have the corrected per-GW math and the April 22 tape ready, because they answer it.

- **dollars_per_share**: SHARES = 266,333,581. PRICE = $940.33 (2026-09-18 close). MARKET CAP = 266,333,581 x $940.33 = $250.44B (verified by direct multiplication).

CHAIN A — THE MULTIPLE (does ~96% of the work).
A1. Assume consensus 2027 adjusted EPS = $24.50 (the brief's $24-25 midpoint; see data_gaps — this is the single number the whole chain scales on).
A2. Implied forward P/E = $940.33 / $24.50 = 38.38x. (S&P 500 ~22x; GEV EV/EBITDA ~44x on my 2026E ~$5.5B adj EBITDA against EV ~$242B.)
A3. Comparable: Siemens Energy trades at 16.7-26.3x EV/EBITDA and ~30x forward P/E while OUT-ORDERING GEV in Q2'26 (12.5 GW vs 11.3 GW, JPM), winning the single largest US gas project (Fermi Matador), and running Gas Services at 16.6% margin versus GEV Power's 17-19% guide. Pillars 1-3 say GEV is one of three co-equals in the US, not the franchise.
A4. Re-rate GEV to 28x — still a 27% premium to the S&P and above Siemens — rather than the theme multiple:
    (38.38 - 28.00) = 10.38 turns x $24.50 = -$254.33/share = -27.0% of $940.33.
A5. Cross-check via a completely different route (EV/EBITDA, which sidesteps the Prolec-distorted EPS): 2027E adjusted EBITDA ~$7.5B (FY25 segment EBITDA was Power $2,902M + Electrification $1,433M + Wind -$598M = $3,737M; H1'26 was Power $1,842M + Elec $1,199M + Wind -$657M = $2,384M, annualising toward ~$5.5B, with 2027 growing off that). At 25x EV/EBITDA + ~$8B net cash = $196B equity / 266.3M sh = $734/share. At 22x = $650/share. The P/E route (28x -> $686; 25x -> $612) and the EV/EBITDA route ($734 -> $650) bracket the same place: a $610-735 band, midpoint ~$675.

CHAIN B — THE SHARE-LOSS P&L LINE (small, and I say so up front).
B1. Market-implied US share for GEV: 50% (its historic position in the installed US gas fleet). Filed share from Pillar 2: 35% (midpoint of 30.5% / 38.5% / 38.8%). Gap = 15 points.
B2. Gap in GW = 0.15 x 54.315 GW (total US planned turbine-island MW, EIA-860M Jul-2026) = 8.15 GW, spread over 2026-2031 CODs = 1.36 GW/yr.
B3. Equipment revenue intensity: FY25 Power product revenue $6,420M / ~15.2 GW shipped in FY25 (Q1'25 3.2 + Q2 5 + Q3 4 + Q4 3, derived from H1'25 = 8.2 GW and the published quarterly ship series) = $422M/GW for ALL of Power product; Gas-only is lower, so use $338-422M/GW and take $380M/GW.
    1.36 GW/yr x $380M/GW = $517M/yr of equipment revenue never booked.
B4. Equipment EBITDA at 10 points (GLJ's 2025-vintage margin, generous to the bull): $52M/yr.
B5. Attached services annuity: 8.15 GW x $25M/GW-yr (management's own Laguna figure, 2026-09-16: ~$500M per GW of HA over 20 years) = $204M/yr of steady-state services revenue; at a 20% EBITDA margin = $41M/yr.
B6. Total EBITDA foregone = $52M + $41M = $93M/yr.
B7. x 25x = $2,325M / 266,333,581 shares = $8.73/share = 0.93% of $940.33.

TOTAL = $254.33 (Chain A) + $8.73 (Chain B) = $263.06/share = 28.0% of $940.33.
- **implied_target**: $677 base case (= $940.33 - $263). Band $610-735, from the two independent valuation routes: 28x/25x forward P/E on $24.50 gives $686/$612; 25x/22x EV/EBITDA on $7.5B 2027E gives $734/$650. Bear tail $539 (22x P/E), roughly splitting the difference between my base and GLJ Research's $470 Sell target (initiated 2026-09-14). Bull-side invalidation is anywhere above ~$1,050 without new evidence.
- **key_assumption**: That GEV's true addressable share of the US utility-scale gas-turbine market is ~35%, not the ~50%+ the market implicitly credits — and, critically, that a company holding one third of its marquee end-market deserves a premium-industrial multiple (25-28x) rather than a theme multiple (38x). The 35% is measured two independent ways (EIA-860M planned pipeline with OEM attribution: 30.5-38.5% across three vintages; JPM's Q2'26 global order tally: 38.8%). The re-rate judgement is NOT measured — it is the assumption doing the most work, and it is a judgement, not a filed number.
- **sensitivity**: HALVE the gap (market credits GEV 42.5%, not 50%): Chain B falls to $4.07-4.60/share, and a 42.5% share is close enough to "leader" that I could only argue a re-rate to ~32x = -$156/share. Total -$161/share = -17%, target $779. After borrow and carry the trade becomes marginal.
DOUBLE the gap (GEV's true share is 20%, or the market credits 65%): Chain B rises to $24.40-27.61/share, and the re-rate goes to 22-24x = -$352 to -$401/share. Total ~-$380/share = -40%, target ~$560 — at which point GLJ's $470 looks like a base case rather than a tail.
Separately, all of Chain A scales linearly with the 2027 EPS assumption: every $1 of EPS error moves the -$254 re-rate figure by ~$10.40/share.
- **dated_test**: THREE tests land inside the horizon, in this order.
(1) Entergy Q3'26 10-Q, expected ~2026-10-29/30. Read Note 8, "Exclusivity Agreement with Major Vendor". The minimum has gone 15 -> 21 (Q3'25) -> 24 (Q1'26) -> 27 (Q2'26). If amended UP again (to 30+ sets, ~22.5 GW), another ~2.2 GW of US advanced-class demand closes to GEV and the pillar strengthens. If the number falls, or the vendor is named as GE Vernova, the pillar breaks.
(2) GE Vernova Q3'26 earnings, CONFIRMED 2026-10-28 (after the Oct 22-24 finals). Read: GW shipped (has not exceeded 5.2 GW in ten quarters; H1'26 was 7.5 GW vs 8.2 GW in H1'25, -9%); firm orders versus SRA signings; and whether management repeats or revises the "80% traditional / 20% data centers" split. GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25 — this is a binary event, size for it.
(3) EIA-860M monthly vintages for Sep/Oct/Nov/Dec 2026 (free, published ~25th of the following month). Recompute GEV's share of the INCREMENTAL planned gas turbine-island MW each month with the same classification script. The US planned pipeline is currently growing ~2.5 GW/month; the question is who captures it.
- **kill_condition**: COVER on any one of these, numerically:
(a) Entergy's Q3'26 or Q4'26 filing names GE Vernova as a turbine or power-island supplier, OR the PIE minimum commitment falls below 24 sets, OR the exclusivity is terminated. That removes 18.7% of the visible US pipeline from the "closed" column.
(b) GEV's Q3'26 (2026-10-28) reports gas GW shipped >= 5.5 GW in the quarter AND >= 4 GW of NEW FIRM US equipment orders (not slot reservations) in the same quarter. Either alone is insufficient; both together mean the share thesis is wrong.
(c) GEV's share of INCREMENTAL US planned gas turbine-island MW exceeds 45% on the attribution script in the Oct/Nov/Dec-2026 EIA-860M vintages, sustained two consecutive months.
(d) GEV revises the data-center share of gigawatts under contract from 20% to above 35%, confirming the AI framing management has so far declined to make.
(e) Price stop: close above $1,050 (+11.7%) without any of (a)-(d) — the market is paying for something I cannot see, and the borrow is not worth waiting out.
- **weakest_link**: THE SHARE EVIDENCE DOES NOT PAY THROUGH THE P&L INSIDE THE HORIZON. Chain B — the entire market-share argument expressed as earnings — is worth $8.73/share, under 1% of the price. GEV recognises equipment revenue OVER TIME on cost-to-cost percentage of completion against orders already booked, so losing Entergy, Yates, Evergy, Sandow, Cass County and Cedar Bayou 5 changes essentially no revenue before 2028 and touches nothing before the Oct 2 memo or the Oct 28 print. About 96% of my -$263 is multiple compression, which is a judgement, and a rich multiple can stay rich for a year. Anyone pitching this must own that plainly: it is a de-rating case using a share table as its evidence, not an earnings-miss case.
SECOND WEAKNESS, and it is real: my denominator may be too small. EIA-860M "Planned" (54.3 GW) is only the permitted, interconnected, COD-dated subset. Global Energy Monitor counted 378 GW of US gas capacity under development as of 2026-08-25, with Texas alone at 122 GW. If even a fifth of that unpermitted layer converts and GEV's 63 GW SRA pool is the reservation tier beneath it, GEV's true US intake could be several times my 3.2 GW/yr and the share table measures the wrong stage of the funnel. My defence is that the same permitting/EPC filter is what makes "under contract" soft in the first place — GEV's own CEO says reservations lag because customers cannot secure EPC, gas or permits — but a bull can fairly say I am counting the market at the wrong point.
THIRD: ~45% of the pipeline by MW has no public OEM attribution, and Project Matador alone (7.6 GW, 14% of the total, only ~1.1 GW actually attributed) swings my headline share by 8 points depending on treatment. And Entergy's "major vendor" is Mitsubishi by strong inference (EPC consortium, M501JAC power trains, the >400 MW frame threshold, JAC-class unit sizes, zero GE mentions in any ETR filing) — but Entergy has never named them.
- **strength**: 3
- **data_gaps**:

Every $1 of error moves the re-rate leg by ~$10.40/share, and free sources disagree on GEV EPS by >50% because of the ~$4.4B non-cash Prolec revaluation gain in Q1'26. A firm FactSet/Bloomberg 2027 consensus adjusted EPS and adjusted EBITDA is the highest-value missing input in this whole case.

State PUC/CPCN dockets (MO PSC EFIS, KCC, IURC, TCEQ, OK CC, ND PSC) carry this and were not exhausted — highest-yield remaining source, and free.

## [Redteam] attack1:S_multiple_compression

- **survives**: False
- **arithmetic_checks_out**: False
- **arithmetic_errors**: Three errors, one fatal.

(1) FATAL — THE "65% FCF CLIFF" IS A VINTAGE-MIXING ERROR, AND IT IS IN THE THESIS SENTENCE. I pulled the guidance row myself: `SELECT stated_on,metric,value,quote FROM mgmt_guidance WHERE ticker='GEV'`. The ">=$24B cumulative 2025-2028" appears in the SAME sentence of the SAME 2026-01-28 release as the 2026 FCF guide, and that guide was "$5.0-$5.5 billion" — not $7B, not $12B. Verbatim: "the company now expects revenue of $44-$45 billion... adjusted EBITDA margin* of 11%-13%, and free cash flow* of $5.0-$5.5 billion" / "cumulative free cash flow* of at least $24 billion."
So management's OWN embedded 2027-28 run-rate at the time the >=$24B was set was ($24.0 - $3.7 actual 2025 - $5.25 mid-2026) / 2 = $7.53B/yr — i.e. +43% GROWTH versus the 2026 they were then guiding. The case computes $4.2B/yr by subtracting a 2026 number that has since been RAISED TWICE ($5.25B -> Apr 22 $7.0B -> Jul 22 $12.0B, a $6.75B cumulative raise) from a cumulative floor that was set before any of those raises. Vintage-consistent decomposition AT THAT MOMENT: $3.7B (2025 actual) + $5.25B (2026 guide) = $8.95B, residual 2027-28 = $15.05B = $7.53B/yr — RISING 43% off 2026, not falling. The case instead subtracts the JULY-2026 revised $12.0B from an UNREVISED January total and reports the residual ($4.15B/yr) as a "65% collapse." That is a revised component against an unrevised total. 2026 FCF guidance was raised twice ($5.25B -> $7.0B -> $12.0B, +$6.75B at midpoint) and the cumulative was never restated. $3.7B + $12.0B = $15.7B is 65% of a four-year floor banked in two years — that is a stale sandbagged floor, not a forecast. Neither branch supports the case: if the $24B is stale there is no cliff; if it holds, $5.5B was pulled FORWARD into 2026, which is a timing shift, not a loss of earning power.

(2) THE 40.0x EV/EBITDA IS A BASIS MISMATCH — Pillar 3's headline overstates by ~58%. The case divides EV $240.2B by 2026E adjusted EBITDA ($5.98B = 13% x $46.0B; I reproduce this exactly, and the 12-14% margin guide is confirmed unchanged in the Jul 22 2026 release) and compares it to Siemens Energy's 16.7x. So the rhetorical centerpiece — "identical franchise, identical cycle point, identical multiple" — is an artifact of comparing a trailing multiple to a forward one. Like-for-like it is 34.0x vs 38.5x, or 37.7x vs 56x. The word "identical" is not earned on either basis.

The case's own arithmetic elsewhere (its 2028 bridge) uses a 0.656 net/EBITDA ratio, so it knows better.
