DERIVATION — the de-rate that survives scrutiny, on inputs I verified myself.
Denominator: Street 2027E adjusted EPS $24.43 (corpus analyst_calls, 2026-06-22; the case's $24.55 from Erste Group reproduces this — the denominator is the one thing that holds).
Current multiple: $940.33 / $24.43 = 38.5x.
Target multiple: 30-34x, not 25x. Justification: GEV is consensus-forecast to grow EPS 45.7% in 2027 and EBITDA from ~$6.0B (2026E) to $11.2B (2028 management target), a 37% CAGR. At 32x the PEG is 0.70; at 25x it is 0.55 — a growth-adjusted multiple less than a third of the S&P's, which requires the market to conclude the growth is fake. That is the earnings case, not the multiple case.
  34x -> $831 (-11.7%), impact $110/share
  32x -> $782 (-16.9%), impact $159/share
  30x -> $733 (-22.1%), impact $207/share
Add the corrected operating misses from the Second Chain, tax-adjusted: $0.65B EBITDA x 0.75 x 32x = $15.6B / 266,333,581 = $58.59/share (the case's $93.49 applies a P/E to pre-tax EBITDA).

CROSS-CHECK ON A CLEAN BASIS. EV $240.2B (which I reproduce: 266,333,581 x $940.33 = $250.4B, less $13.120B cash, plus $2.849B debt). Against the Street's 2027 EBITDA of $9.45B that is 25.4x, and against management's 2028 $11.2B, 21.4x. Those are rich for an industrial — but they are not the 40.2x the case leads with, and at 25.4x versus Siemens Energy's 16.7x the premium is ~1.5x for a company growing roughly three times as fast, with a 20% margin target against Siemens' mid-teens.

THE HONEST SHAPE OF THE TRADE. Direction is defensible; magnitude is not. Roughly $110-207 of de-rate risk is real and unspent — the multiple can drift from 38.5x to 30-34x on nothing more than the AI-power complex continuing to bleed, and GEV's 1.78 beta guarantees it participates. What is NOT supported is the incremental $120-220 the case gets from 30x down to 25x, because that step needs the 2027 EBITDA cut (Street $9.45B -> GLJ $7.42B) that the case explicitly refuses to underwrite. Against that, the team carries 53.8% annualized vol, a $1,236 street average 31% above spot, a confirmed Oct 28 earnings print whose sign has matched the EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, and an unscheduled December investor update that delivered +15.6% on 3.75x volume last year. A $160 expected move against that carry and that event risk is not an outright short. If the team takes this side at all it is a pair — short GEV against long ETN (-7.7% peak-to-date vs GEV's -20.0%, so the spread has already run) or against the S&P — and the memo has to say so, exactly as the case's own weakest link #1 concedes.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. The direction is defensible; the case as built is not, because four of its five headline numbers are manufactured by mixing measurement bases, and every error runs the same way.

The three that kill it:

1. THE FCF CLIFF IS AN ARTIFACT OF MIXED VINTAGES. The ">=$24B cumulative 2025-2028" and the "$5.0-$5.5B 2026" guide were issued in the same January 28 2026 release. On that vintage, management's own plan implied 2027-28 FCF of $7.53B/yr — RISING 43% off 2026, not collapsing 65%. The case subtracts July's revised $12.0B from January's unrevised total. And $3.7B + $12.0B = $15.7B is 65% of a four-year floor banked in two years, which marks the $24B as stale sandbagging. Pillar 2 goes, and the Third Chain goes with it — because the "independent" $489-602 FCF corroboration is built on the same stale number. The case's claim of "two methods, one answer" is false independence, and that matters more than the arithmetic, because the team would have carried a single error into the memo believing it had been triangulated.

2. THE CASE NEVER ADJUSTS FOR GROWTH. Its thesis sentence compares 38x to the S&P's 22x. Consensus has GEV's EPS at +45.7% in 2027 ($16.77 -> $24.43). That is a 0.84 PEG against the market's 2.2. A valuation short whose entire argument is a raw P/E comparison across a 46%-grower and a 10%-grower, with no growth-adjusted metric anywhere in four pillars and three chains, does not have a valuation argument. It has an anchor.

3. IT IS ALREADY IN THE PRICE, AND THE MARKET ALREADY FADED IT. The multiple fell from 48.1x to 38.5x — 9.6 turns, $235/share — in the eleven weeks before the entry date. GLJ published a harder version of this exact case at a LOWER target ($470) on September 14; the stock closed $874.76 that day and rallied 7.5% to $940.33 within four sessions. The drawdown is sector-wide (VRT -30.3%, PWR -14.0%) and the case's own weakest link concedes the move may already have happened. The team would be shorting the back third of a completed de-rate, 7.5% above where the published bear case pushed it, at 53.8% vol into a confirmed October 28 print.

Two further errors, smaller but revealing of method: the 40.0x EV/EBITDA headline divides EV by a transition-year 2026E number and compares it to a peer's LTM — on the Street's 2027 EBITDA of $9.45B (sourced from GLJ's own note inside the corpus) it is 25.4x, not 40.2x. And the "identical 37.7x" GE parallel is a trailing multiple set against GEV's forward; like-for-like GE was 34.0x. The centerpiece word "identical" is not earned.

WHAT THE CASE GETS RIGHT, and the team should keep: the denominator ($24.55 reproduces the Street's $24.43, closing its own biggest data gap); the share count, EV and ex-deposit FCF arithmetic, all of which I reproduced exactly; the price-basket correction to the brief; and the intellectual honesty of weakest link #1, which correctly identifies that a catalyst-free valuation short in a 1.78-beta name against a $1,236 street target is a trade you can be right about and still lose on. That paragraph is the most valuable thing in the document — and it argues against the document.

The deeper problem is one of construction rather than any single number. This is a conclusion reached first and evidenced backwards: the 25x target is set in Pillar 1, and the FCF route is then built to "bracket and corroborate" a number it was never independent of. Three pillars pointing at $500-615 is not confirmation when two of them share an input.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE TEAM: if you want to be short GEV, be short it on the services revisions and the Q3 shipment number — the two things here that are fresh, falsifiable on October 28, and not in anyone's published note. Those are worth ~$59/share corrected, which is an honest small short or a pair leg. They are not worth $327. And if you want $615, you must underwrite the 22% EBITDA cut that GLJ already published and the market already declined to pay for — which is a different memo, and a crowded one.

4) Kill condition (2) is set below a level the series already crossed without consequence: the beyond-5-year bucket was $4,093M at Mar-25 and $3,977M at Jun-25. A trigger breached fifteen months ago with no adverse outcome is not a test. At ~$950M per point of p5, the entire $2,635M bucket sits within three rounding increments — the kill condition is inside the measurement noise.
5) The percentages are visibly soft: p5 jumped 92% -> 97% in one quarter (Jun-25 -> Sep-25) unexplained. Kill condition (4) says a restatement of the timing percentages would make the instrument unreliable. A 5-point one-quarter swing is that in substance, and it already happened.

The case cannot use "unpriced until conversion" to protect Pillar 4 and "booking date = price vintage" to power Pillar 2.
7) Pillar 4's headline divergence is a category error plus an acquisition. It compares CONSOLIDATED equipment revenue (Power + Wind + Electrification) against GAS GW shipped. Electrification equipment — including newly consolidated Prolec and >$5B of H1'26 data-center orders — is most of the growth. Ex-Prolec, equipment revenue rose 14.1%, not 28.8%, against gas GW -8.5%: a 23-point gap, not 37, and most of the residual is a different segment.
8) Percentage-of-completion is double-edged and the case shows one edge. Under cost-to-cost you recognize revenue in proportion to COSTS INCURRED. Rising equipment revenue on falling shipments is equally consistent with cost inflation on in-process fixed-price contracts — lifting revenue while destroying margin — as with healthy progress. That is precisely GLJ's reading, and the case never addresses it.
9) The $700-850/kW SRA band is self-declared as un-sourced, yet "$44-54B" still appears in a pillar headline.

- **where**: The RPO timing footnote has printed seven consecutive times — 2025-02-06, 2025-04-23, 2025-07-23, 2025-10-22, 2026-01-29, 2026-04-22, 2026-07-22 — in the same paragraph of the same note, and the case itself confirms every figure is XBRL-tagged (RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationPercentage / Product). XBRL-tagged means machine-ingested by every quant screen, data vendor and sell-side model the morning of filing. This is the most systematically distributed number GEV produces; there is no asymmetry to harvest.

The market-based refutation is decisive: the case's own contracted-CY-next metric rose fastest in exactly the quarters the stock fell hardest — $22,165M (Dec-25) -> $26,194M (Mar-26, +18.2%) -> $28,542M (Jun-26, +9.0%), while GEV went from $1,196 in late June to $940 by Sep 18. The footnote improved and the multiple compressed. That is the market saying it has read the footnote and is discounting something else: services revisions at 8.11% of contract revenue in H1'26, a Wind segment that must swing +$257M in H2 against a best-ever +$19M quarter, and 63 GW of unpriced reservations.

The case admits this in its own weakest_link and then keeps the $176.6 in the headline anyway.

That two-year percentage just fell from 69% to 65% in two quarters, taking $1.76B out of your CY2027 revenue line in the most recent print, and it is a rounded integer on an $88B base where one point is $878M. So why are your primary kill condition, your entire third pillar and your headline dated test all written on the one-year bucket — the one variable that does not enter your model at all — and where in this case do you sensitise the only number that does?

Pillar 3: $0 — refuted. On its own stated effect it is -$113/share, which I do not take because Pillar 1 is already rebuilt from the p2 series.
Pillar 4: $0 — the divergence is 51% Prolec and cross-segment.

REVISED UPSIDE = $26 + $40 = $66/share, +7.0%, implied ~$1,006.

THE DOWNSIDE THE CASE NEVER PRICES: apply the case's own declared 25x default consistently to FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $5.52-6.44B (12-14% margin guidance on $45.5-46.5B revenue, Q2'26 press release) plus ~$5-6B net cash against $13,120M cash at Jun-30-26 = $537-627/share, call it $580. That is -$360/share, -38%. The case's multiple and the case's target are mutually exclusive, and the case applied the multiple only where it flatters.

NET: +$66 of provisional, half-sentiment upside against -$360 of downside on the case's own stated valuation basis. Even at only a 20% probability on the 25x scenario: 0.8 x (+$66) + 0.2 x (-$360) = -$19/share. I would not carry this long.
- **verdict**: The case does not survive. It is well-constructed, honestly disclosed at the edges, and structurally broken at the center. Three findings kill it.

First, the model is algebraically one number — CY2027 = 0.5 x equipment RPO x the two-year cumulative percentage; the one-year percentage cancels exactly. The case does not know this. It therefore spends Pillar 3, its primary dated test and its lead kill condition defending and monitoring a variable that has no effect on its answer, while the one variable that does — p2 — fell from 69% to 65% in the two most recent quarters and is never sensitised. A case that cannot identify its own load-bearing input cannot be defended in Q&A.

Second, the central epistemic claim is falsified by the case's own instrument. Run the identical method at the identical 18-month lead one year earlier: at Jun-30-2025 it said CY2026 equipment revenue was "contracted" at $17,399M, against a CY2026 tracking $25-26B. Visibility was ~66-70%, not 97.7%. The contracted-CY-next series (14,851 / 16,145 / 17,399 / 19,203 / 22,165 / 26,194 / 28,542) grows 10-18% every quarter because new orders land in it. It is a running total, not a floor. "Already contracted regardless of what happens to new orders" is exactly backwards: roughly a third of CY2027 equipment revenue must still come from orders not yet booked, which reinstates the entire order-and-conversion risk the thesis claims to have eliminated.

Third, the valuation is incoherent in a way that inverts the trade. $176.6 of the $235.8 is the distance between the case and GLJ's Sell note, stacked onto a $940 price that plainly does not embed GLJ. And the 25x multiple the case calls conservative, applied to the whole company rather than only to the increments, gives $537-627/share — the case's own default multiple implies a 38% short.

Secondary but material: the 110.3% realization ratio, the +28.8% equipment growth, the 57.3% equipment mix and the 27.9% incremental margin are all lifted by the Prolec consolidation; ex-Prolec they are 107.3%, +14.1%, 54.3% and ~20%. Pillar 3's tail comparison uses two different five-year definitions; like-for-like (Dec-25 to Jun-26) the years-3-5 bucket grew 56.2% against 36.7% for the book, so the tail is lengthening inside the window Pillar 3 does not examine. And the footnote is XBRL-tagged and has printed seven times, improving fastest in precisely the two quarters the stock fell 20% — the market has read this and is discounting services revisions, the Wind H2 swing and the unpriced SRA pool instead.

The salvageable observation is real but small, and it is a different pitch: the one-year dollar bucket and the contracted-CY-next series have risen every single quarter through a 20% drawdown on the lowest volume in 14 months. That is a sentiment-dislocation argument worth perhaps $66/share, with a catalyst landing Oct 28 — four days after the finals. It is not a 25% LONG and the team should not carry it as one.
- **level**: high

The ratio was stable when Product RPO grew ~5%/yr and 44-47% sat inside twelve months; Product RPO has since doubled while that percentage collapsed to 36%. The backtest is arithmetically right and predictively dead.

(5) THE "PREMISE CORRECTION" ON THE PEAK PRICE IS ITSELF WRONG. The case states the intraday high was $1,178.20 on 2026-06-30. The prices table shows 2026-07-06 high = $1,195.94. The brief's $1,196 was correct as an intraday high; the analyst "corrected" a correct number. Drawdown from the true intraday peak = -21.4%, as the brief said.

(6) SHARE COUNT. 266,333,581 is unsourced and conflicts with the filed Q2'26 diluted count of 270.0M (gev_quarterly.csv, SharesDiluted). Every per-share figure in the case is inflated 1.4%.

(7) METHOD 1 AND METHOD 2 ARE NOT TWO ESTIMATES OF ONE QUANTITY. $39.74 (contracted book at mature EBITDA) and $143 (a perpetual quarter of the gas franchise) differ 3.6x and measure different things. Calling that "bracketing the answer" and then quoting the LOW end in the headline claim is the oldest tell in a pitch.
- **evidence_holds**: False
- **evidence_problems**: THE FLAGSHIP CITATION IS SELECTIVELY QUOTED, AND THE OMITTED SENTENCE IS THE MOST DAMAGING ONE IN THE CORPUS. Chunk 251590 is quoted from "For our total gigawatts under contract, demand remains diverse..." The sentence immediately BEFORE it, in the same chunk, reads: "half of the gigawatts that are now under contract are for our largest, most efficient HA turbines, units expected to run base load." More than 58 of the 116 GW are base-load HA machines. Base load at high capacity factor is the data-center signature; utility reserve-margin and peaking replacement is not base load. Management's own words, one sentence above the quote the case leans on, undercut the load-mix reading of the 80/20. Quoting past it is the single thing a PM will find fastest, because it is in the same paragraph.

THE "STRONG FORM" GEOGRAPHIC EVIDENCE IS A CATEGORY ERROR. FY2025 revenue by geography (45.6% US) measures revenue RECOGNIZED on contracts signed 2021-2024, across ALL THREE SEGMENTS — including Wind, which is Europe-heavy and lost $598M in FY25, and Electrification. It is a backward-looking consolidated revenue split. The claim is about the forward mix of a 2026 gas order book. These are different measurements of different things in different years. It is not independent corroboration; it is a different number that happens to point the same way. The case calls it "the strong form" precisely because the weak form is weak, but the strong form does not measure the claim.

PILLAR 4 IS GOOD RESEARCH THAT PROVES THE WRONG PROPOSITION. I verified the underlying disclosures and they are real and well found: Southern's ~13 GW with minimum bills, termination payments and posted collateral; FPL's 70% take-or-pay floor; the Meta parent guaranty behind Entergy Louisiana's Evest agreement; Texas SB 6 financial commitments at 75 MW. This is the most original work in the case. But every one of those provisions makes the UTILITY whole when a hyperscaler walks. None of them obliges the utility to place or keep a turbine order. The case concedes this in its own weakest-link and then still counts pillar 4 as repairing pillar 1. It does not.

CONVERSELY, THE CASE OMITS THE ONE FILING FACT THAT DECIDES IT, AND IT IS IN THE FILES IT ALREADY PULLED. H1'26 cash from operations was $10,680M (Q1 $5,188M + Q2 $5,492M). Contract liabilities rose from $25,950M at Dec-25 to $40,037M at Jun-26, a build of $14,087M. Operating cash flow EXCLUDING the customer-deposit build was therefore MINUS $3,407M. FY25 is the same story: CFO $4,987M against a deposit build of $8,350M = minus $3,363M. GE Vernova's entire reported free cash flow, in both periods, IS the customer deposit float. The business consumes cash before deposits. The case cites contract liabilities four times — as a kill condition, as "the hardest available evidence that customers are actually committing cash" — and never once nets them against operating cash flow. That is the whole ballgame and it is one subtraction away in a CSV the case already opened.
- **already_priced_or_known**: True
- **where**: Every input to pillars 1, 2 and 3 is a primary disclosure that has been public for two to eight months and is covered by 37 analysts. The 80/20 split was in PREPARED REMARKS on the Q1 call (2026-04-22) and repeated in prepared remarks on the Q2 call (2026-07-22) — and chunk 217366 shows a free consumer-facing web article reproducing Strazik's exact words in April 2026. The 54.4% non-US geography is a labelled table in the FY25 10-K (chunk 29936, filed 2026-01-29). RPO-due-within-twelve-months is a standard XBRL tag (RevenueRemainingPerformanceObligationPercentage) that every screen scrapes automatically. The 116 GW, the 20 GW/yr output ramp and the >=125 GW target were in the Q2 press release and repeated by wire services within hours (chunks 218632, 218633, 468550). There is no derivation anywhere in pillars 1-3 that a first-year associate would not have in the model by Jul 23.

The self-indicting proof: the case's implied target is $1,050 against a street average of ~$1,236. It is a LONG whose price target sits 15% BELOW consensus, built entirely from consensus's own source documents. That is not a variant perception — it is consensus, discounted. If the team pitches this, the PM's first observation is that they are less bullish than the sell side while claiming the sell side has mispriced the name.

The only genuinely under-modelled material is pillar 4's utility large-load contract terms (Southern's 13 GW of termination/collateral provisions, FPL's 70% take-or-pay, the Meta guaranty). That is real edge — and it argues about counterparty credit, which nobody is worried about, rather than order continuation, which is what the drawdown is pricing.

And the drawdown itself is already explained without any mispricing: the case's own data gaps establish that GEV fell 20.0% while Vertiv fell 30.3%. GEV underperformed the equal-weight basket by 7.5 points, not 20. A 7.5-point idiosyncratic move on the lowest volume in 14 months, into a Sell initiation at $470 and a cautious Bernstein note, is an ordinary de-rating of an AI-levered multiple from 48x to 38x forward. There is nothing left over to arbitrage.
- **killer_question**: "Your case is that contracted revenue is safe. Fine — I'll grant you all four pillars. Now: H1'26 cash from operations was $10.7 billion, and customer deposits rose $14.1 billion over the same period, so the business burned $3.4 billion of cash before deposits — exactly as it did in FY25. Free cash flow IS the float. So tell me what FY27 free cash flow prints if not one gigawatt is ever cancelled, the 80/20 holds exactly, and new signings merely FLATTEN at 20 GW a quarter instead of compounding — and then tell me why a stock at 40x EBITDA and 21x free cash flow deserves any multiple at all on cash that is a customer's deposit rather than GE Vernova's profit."

The case cannot answer it, because every pillar it built defends the REVENUE line and the CANCELLATION channel, while the stock is priced on the CASH line and the SIGNING-RATE channel. A hyperscaler capex pause does not need to cancel anything to break GEV inside the horizon; it only needs to slow the rate at which new deposits arrive. The case's four kill conditions all require cancellation, restatement or a guidance cut. None of them fires in the scenario that actually kills the stock.
- **revised_dollars_per_share**: I REPRICE BOTH SIDES OF THE LEDGER.

WHAT THE LONG GOT TOO LOW — the contracted data-center book.
Step 1. DC GW under contract = 116 x 20% = 23.2 GW (I accept management's split for this calc).
Step 2. Equipment price $700/kW, not $500/kW. Derivation: Q2'26 gross deposits collected = net contract-liability build ($40,037M - $31,949M = $8,088M) + deposits recognized as revenue ($3,511M) = $11,599M in one quarter. Attributing ~70% to Power against 30 GW of gas contracting activity (20 signed + 10 converted) = ~$271/kW of cash collected; at the 43% equipment-deposit-to-equipment-RPO ratio that implies ~$630/kW. The RPO residual method implies $850-950/kW. $700/kW is the conservative middle.
Step 3. Equipment revenue at risk = 23.2 GW x $700/kW = $16.24B over ~5 years = $3.25B/yr.
Step 4. x 12% equipment EBITDA margin = $390M/yr.
Step 5. Services 23.2 GW x $25M/GW-yr = $580M x 25% = $145M/yr.
Step 6. Mature DC EBITDA = $535M/yr.
Step 7. x 35x (haircut from GEV's own ~40x EV/EBITDA for 2029-33 arrival, NOT the case's arbitrary 25x) = $18.7B.
Step 8. / 270,000,000 filed diluted shares = $69.3/share = 7.4% of $940.33.
So the LONG understated its own ceiling by 74%. Directionally it is still right that this alone is smaller than the $234.53 drawdown. I concede that.

WHAT THE LONG LEFT OUT ENTIRELY — the signing-rate / free-cash-flow channel. This is the number.
Step 1. FY26 FCF guidance $11.5-12.5B, midpoint $12.0B. H1'26 delivered ~$9.9B.
Step 2. The deposit build required to produce it: H1'26 contract liabilities +$14,087M against CFO of $10,680M, so CFO ex-deposits = -$3,407M. Annualized, the ex-deposit business consumes ~$6.8B and the deposit build must run ~$19B to hit the guide.
Step 3. Kill condition: new signings slow 30% — from ~80 GW/yr annualized (20-21 GW in each of Q1 and Q2'26) to ~55 GW/yr. No cancellations. No restatement of the 80/20. No revenue miss. Deposit build falls ~30% = -$5.7B/yr.
Step 4. FY27 FCF then prints ~$6.3B against a ~$12B base.
Step 5. Multiple. The market pays $253.9B / $12.0B = 21.2x FCF today. I refuse to capitalize float at 21x. At 12x — appropriate for working-capital cash rather than earnings — the shortfall is $5.7B x 12 = $68.4B.
Step 6. / 270,000,000 shares = $253/share = 26.9% of $940.33.

That single line is larger than the entire drawdown taken to date, requires no cancellation, and fires none of the case's six kill conditions.

THE EXPECTED-VALUE TEST, ON THE CASE'S OWN NUMBERS.
Upside to its $1,050 target = +$109.67/share.
Downside on my signing-rate channel = -$253/share. On the case's OWN halved-sensitivity ("~$342/share... that is far more than the $234.53 already taken, so this scenario is NOT priced and it is the real bear case") = -$342/share.
Breakeven probability of the bear: 109.67 / (109.67 + 253) = 30.2%. Against the case's own -$342: 24.3%.
At a 30% bear probability and 70% upside: 0.70 x 109.67 - 0.30 x 253 = +$0.9/share. Zero.

So the LONG is only positive expected value if the probability of an AI-capex-driven signing slowdown over the next 3-12 months is below roughly 25-30%. The case never estimates that probability. The 20% drawdown on thin volume IS the market marking it to somewhere in that neighbourhood. There is no edge left — and the case wrote its own bear scenario, valued it at -$342, labelled it unpriced, and recommended LONG anyway.

REVISED FAIR VALUE: ~$900-950, i.e. spot. Not a long, not a short on this analysis — a pass. If the team must have a position, the asymmetry runs the other way: the correctly-specified downside (-$253) is 2.3x the case's own upside (+$110).
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. Not because the facts are wrong — most of them are right, and I verified them line by line — but because the case answers a question nobody is asking.

WHAT I CONCEDE, AND THE TEAM SHOULD KEEP: The in-horizon revenue line genuinely is locked. $45.8B of RPO due within twelve months, equipment recognized over time on cost-to-cost, a 53 GW firm backlog against 20 GW/yr of output — no data-center cancellation touches FY26 revenue, and the 5x-oversubscription point is robust across a 20%-to-60% data-center range. That is real and correctly derived. Pillar 4's utility-contract research (Southern's 13 GW with termination payments and posted collateral, FPL's 70% take-or-pay, the Meta parent guaranty behind Entergy Louisiana) is the best original work in the package. The peer-basket correction is right and honest: Vertiv fell 30.3% versus GEV's 20.0%, so the idiosyncratic piece is ~7.5 points, not 20 — the analyst volunteered the fact that most damages their own framing, which is the mark of someone worth listening to.

WHY IT DIES ANYWAY, IN ORDER OF LETHALITY:

1. IT DEFENDS THE WRONG FINANCIAL STATEMENT. GEV's H1'26 operating cash flow of $10,680M contains a $14,087M increase in customer deposits. Ex-deposits: minus $3,407M. FY25: CFO $4,987M against an $8,350M deposit build, minus $3,363M. The free cash flow is the float. The stock trades at ~40x EV/EBITDA and 21x FCF on cash that belongs, economically, to customers until GEV performs. The case treats contract liabilities purely as proof of commitment and never nets them against CFO. A signing slowdown — not a cancellation — flattens that build and takes ~$253/share, inside the horizon, without tripping a single one of the six stated kill conditions.

2. ITS OWN SENSITIVITY SECTION CONTAINS THE REFUTATION. The case computes a -$342/share bear scenario, states in writing that it is larger than the drawdown and "NOT priced," and recommends LONG. Against a +$110 target that requires P(bear) below 24.3%. No such probability is offered.

3. IT HAS NO VARIANT PERCEPTION. Every pillar-1-through-3 input is a five-month-old prepared remark, a 10-K table, or a standard XBRL tag, across a 37-analyst name — and the resulting target is 15% BELOW the street average. A long thesis less bullish than consensus, built from consensus's own documents, is arithmetic, not an idea.

4. THE FLAGSHIP QUOTE IS TRIMMED AT THE WRONG PLACE. One sentence above the 80/20 line, in the same chunk, Strazik says more than half the gigawatts under contract are base-load HA machines. Base load is the data-center signature. A PM who opens the transcript finds that in ten seconds, and from that moment the analyst's judgment, not just the case, is on trial.

5. THE CENTRAL VALUATION INPUT IS SOFT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. $500/kW derived by dividing one period's POC revenue by one period's shipments, in a quarter that was 16 aeroderivatives and 3 HA, on a book whose RPO doubled in eighteen months — then applied at 25x while the stock itself trades at ~40x. Correcting both gives $69/share, not $39.74, and the "5.9x the entire franchise" headline collapses to 3.4x.

WHAT I WOULD TELL THE TEAM TO DO WITH IT: do not pitch this as the long. Harvest two things from it. First, pillar 4 is a genuine asset in the room — it is the one piece the judges will not have seen, and it cleanly kills the lazy "hyperscaler walks and the utility eats it" bear argument. Second, the deposit-versus-FCF subtraction this case walked past is, in my view, the strongest single piece of work available on GEV in either direction, and it belongs in the pitch whichever side you end up taking. Whoever presents must be ready for the question in item 1, because on this evidence the stock is fairly priced and the asymmetry, properly specified, runs 2.3-to-1 against the long.

ERROR 1 - THE FLOOR-BREAK IS WRONG. This kills the $61.73/share de-rating leg (48% of the target).

Top of the two positive bands with Wind at guide: 4,507 + 3,000 - 400 - 480 = $6,627M = 14.4%. Bottom: 3,965 + 2,610 - 400 - 480 = $5,695M = 12.4%. The band's own width is ~$930M - roughly DOUBLE the $500M Wind miss being modeled.

(b) Double-counted with Leg B: marking down the forward earnings path IS the mechanism by which a multiple compresses. (c) Fatal: it capitalizes the gap to a COMPANY SLIDE, not to consensus. You can only harvest a hole if the market is paying for the number you remove. - **evidence_holds**: False

This is the best-sourced case I have seen on this name, and its failure is not sloppiness. Every citation checks out. LEG 3 — multiple, conditional on a failed inversion on 28 Oct: THIS SURVIVES, SMALL.
  One turn of 2028 EBITDA = $11.20B / 266,333,581 = $42.05 in 2028 = $34.75 PV = 3.7% of price.
  Reservation pool fundamental value, recomputed from the case's own pillar 4 inputs (63 GW x $300M/GW x 18% / 3 delivery years + 63 GW x $25M/GW-yr x 30%) x 25 = $150.80/share = 16.0%.
  A failed inversion justifies roughly one turn of de-rate plus a 30% haircut to the pool's ascribed value: $34.75 + $45.24 = $79.99 = 8.5%.
  Conditional target $860.34.

PROBABILITY WEIGHT. This is a dated binary on 28 Oct. Feasibility grid says the inversion is reachable at C=10-12 with signings down 22-33%, and GEV is selling 2031 slots — a sold-out manufacturer signing fewer reservations is not deterioration. Call it a coin flip. The case's own sensitivity puts the upside at +15-25% if it inverts. At 50/50 against +20%: EV = 0.5(-8.5%) + 0.5(+20%) = +5.7% for the stock, i.e. the short loses money in expectation.

I remove 72% of the claimed downside ($290 -> $80) and the remainder does not clear its own event risk. The one number I would want firmer before finalizing: consensus 2027 adjusted EPS. At $940.33 the implied forward P/E on $24-25 is 37.6-39.2x, not the ~35x in the brief. That makes the multiple leg somewhat better than I have sized it — but it is a multiple view, not a conversion finding, and it is available to anyone with a screen.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. This is a well-built flow model attached to a valuation bridge that does not follow from it.

What is genuinely good: the gas GW reconciliation is real work. I rebuilt it independently from gev_operational.csv and every quarter closes against disclosed signings (Q2-26 predicts S_end 64 vs 63, rounding). The analyst found the Q1-26 vs Q2-26 management contradiction (chunks 468325 and 468437 — Strazik guiding reservations to keep outgrowing orders in April, then promising the inversion in July, with the causal mechanism unchanged). That contradiction is a legitimate, dated, testable observation. It is worth one turn of multiple, not thirty-one points.

Why it fails, in order of damage:

1. HALF THE DOWNSIDE HAS NO MECHANISM. The $150.19/share 2028 cut assumes the conversion rate gates the shipment ramp. It does not. 53 GW firm backlog versus 54 GW of guided shipments through end-2028 means the ramp is already underwritten by orders GEV holds today. The case never checked its own bridge against the company's own shipment guide, which sits in the chunk (217505) it cites for something else.

2. THE CENTRAL FINDING IS A DENOMINATOR ARTIFACT, AND THE CASE MAKES THE SAME ERROR TWICE. Conversions went 3, 7, 8, 6, 10 — the numerator more than tripled while the pool grew 167%. The ratio fell because the funnel widened. The identical error sits in the brief's contract-liability stat, which I checked in xbrl: absolute liquidation ROSE 6.2% ($7,074M to $7,512M) while the percentage "deteriorated" from 40.2% to 29.1%. Two pillars, one mistake. The FIFO test settles it: 34 GW converted against 28 GW reserved through Q2-25 means realized dwell is ~3 quarters, inside Siemens' own stated 6-12 months.

3. THE PEER BENCHMARK IS UNSOURCED AND CIRCULAR. Zero corpus hits for a stated 26 GW Siemens reservation pool. It was inferred from 12-in-12-out, which assumes Siemens is at steady state — and the whole result is that a steady-state ratio beats a non-steady-state one. That is not a finding, it is the definition of C/S.

4. THE PILLARS CANNOT ALL PAY. Pillar 2 needs conversions low; pillar 3 needs signings to stop. These are different worlds and the bridge adds them.

5. THE "PINCER" IS FEASIBLE. My grid finds a valid window at the actual Q2-26 conversion number with signings down a third — which is what you expect from a company selling 2031 slots.

6. IT IS PRICED. The float point traded -8.69% on 22 Jul in management's own words; the 53/63 framing and the exact Oct 28 test are already published in the trade press (chunk 217437); GLJ has a $470 Sell in the market and the stock has not gone there.

7. IT HIDES ITS OWN BEST ANSWER. Step 0 says -3.8%. That route is dropped from the "three routes converge" claim.

To the team's credit, weakest_link #1 (non-refundable deposits plus a lapse-and-resell option in a sold-out market) and #2 (GEV -20.0% vs VRT -25.5%, which I verified) are honestly stated and both are correct. The analyst already knows what beats this case. What should follow is the narrower, defensible version: the April-versus-July management contradiction is a real credibility event on a confirmed date, worth roughly one turn. That is a trade with a 50/50 payoff against +20% upside — which is not a pitch. If the team wants SHORT, this is not the argument; if they want the event, they should size it as an event and say so.

- **revised_dollars_per_share**: Same anchor, same disclosure, three corrections: a realistic 2028 EBITDA, a defensible multiple, and a discount rate.

STEP 1 — 2028E ADJUSTED EBITDA, BUILT UP RATHER THAN ASSUMED.
Revenue is the easy half; I accept $56B. Margin is the whole argument, and the target's published composition is Power 22%, Electrification 22%, Wind +6%.
- Power: ~$28.4B 2028 revenue at 21% (vs 22% target; H1'26 actual 17.67%) = $5.96B
- Electrification: ~$19.8B at 21% (vs 22%; H1'26 actual 18.2%) = $4.16B
- Wind: ~$8.0B at 0% (vs +6%; H1'26 was -$657M against a full-year guide of -$400M) = $0
- Corporate: ~-$0.7B
2028E adjusted EBITDA = $9.4B, or 84% of management's $11.2B. I am granting 350bps of Power margin expansion and 280bps of Electrification expansion over two years and only docking the plan where it is furthest from reality.

STEP 2 — MULTIPLE. 25x on a terminal-year EBITDA with zero growth after is not a "default," it is the most aggressive point on the published ladder ($1,050 = 24x = "clearly pricing in sustained high growth beyond 2028"). STEP 3 — VALUE AND DISCOUNT.
21.44 x $9.4B = $201.5B EV. Add net cash $13.120B - $2.849B = $10.271B -> $211.8B equity / 266,333,581 = $795 as a late-2028 value.
PV over 2.28 years at 10%: $795/1.10^2.28 = $640, or -31.9% from $940.33.

BASE CASE $760 (-19%). I round up from $640 because a 21.44x exit on a franchise still compounding into 2029-2032 is harsh and because the $87.8B equipment RPO gives the revenue line genuine visibility; call it 24x on $9.4B PV'd, which lands near $720-790. I will publish $760.
BULL $960 (+2%): the full $11.2B lands AND 25x holds, discounted at 10% = $877; add a year of buyback and you get to ~$960. Note that the bull case, properly present-valued, is roughly flat.
BEAR $600 (-36%): $9.24B (16.5% margin) at 18x = $663 as a 2028 value, PV ~$535; or simply the published $650-700 "normalisation" band.

SKEW: +$220 against -$340 from $940.33. That is 0.65:1, negative expected value, against a crowded consensus long with a confirmed catalyst (Oct 28) that lands AFTER the competition finals. The case's own honest admission that risk/reward is "roughly 1:1 — which is honestly poor for a pitch" is, once the discounting is fixed, optimistic.

For the team: the decomposition work in Pillar 1 is genuinely good and worth keeping — it just points at the short, or at no position, rather than at the long. If you want to be long the AI-power complex, GEV is the leg that fell least (-20.0% vs VRT -25.5%), trades at 40.2x FY26E EBITDA, and has the only idiosyncratic 2027 margin-vintage problem in the group.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. Kill it.

Three independent reasons, any one of which is sufficient.

FIRST, THE CASE HAS NO RETURN ONCE THE ARITHMETIC IS COMPLETED. The $1,090 target is 25x a 2028 EBITDA figure, undiscounted, dressed as a 3-12 month price. Present-valued at 10%, it is $877 — below the $940.33 entry. The pitch's headline upside is entirely the discount rate it omitted.

SECOND, THE CASE DISPROVES ITSELF IN ITS OWN STRONGEST PILLAR. Pillar 1 establishes with a clean regression that 78% of the drawdown is the AI-power complex and that GEV's residual is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5). That is a finding of NO idiosyncratic mispricing. The case then capitalises the entire 5.58-turn compression — $234.63/share — as recoverable GEV-specific value. On its own numbers the recoverable idiosyncratic piece is roughly $26-34/share after the Jul 23 retrace. The pitch is a sector beta trade wearing a stock-selection costume, and it is long the leg of that sector that fell the least.

THIRD, THE LOAD-BEARING FACT IS INCOMPLETE IN A WAY THAT FLIPS ITS SIGN. "The market sold a guidance raise" is the emotional core of the pitch. The same sentence the case quotes ends "adjusted EBITDA margin* guidance remains 12%-14%" — earnings guidance was held while revenue rose $1.0B, a 13% incremental margin against a bridge that needs ~35%. And the raised FY FCF guide of $11.5-12.5B was already 82% banked at H1's $9,897M, implying H2 FCF of $1.6-2.6B, a 74-84% sequential collapse. A market that fell 8.7% on that release was not being irrational; it read the whole document. The case read half of it.

Supporting: the 2028 20% margin target requires Power AND Electrification at 22% and Wind at +6%; the case cites Power 17.67%, Electrification 18.2% and Wind -$657M as evidence the plan is on track. The sensitivity analysis holds the multiple constant in the bear and expands it in the bull, converting a real -30% downside into a fictional -3.6%. The two "independent" valuation routes share an input, disagree on share count, and justify the exit multiple with the entry multiple. And the whole framework — including the unusual 266.3M share count — appears in a free published note that uses it to argue the stock LACKS a margin of safety at 21x.

WHAT IS SALVAGEABLE. The factor decomposition, the Jul 22 quote work, the contract-liability-versus-cash gap ($40.0B owed, $13.1B held, $26.9B already spent), and the buyback timing ($2.4B at an average $1,020.67 in Q2'26) are all solid research. Every one of them supports the short or a pass. If the team is choosing a side by Friday, this analyst has just built the bear file and mislabelled it.

Finally, a competition point the case gets right and should not lose: the real catalyst (Q3 earnings, Oct 28) lands AFTER the Oct 22-24 finals. Whichever side the team picks, the pitch must stand on evidence available today, and on today's evidence this long is a consensus position with a target below consensus, negative present-valued expected return, and no variant perception.

The research is genuinely good — the Prolec purchase-accounting decomposition, the contract-liability series, the Section 232 dating are all real work, and the author's honesty in weakest_link is better than most sell-side. But the case has a load-bearing contradiction at its centre and the two halves of the $191.72 cancel each other.

The fatal flaw: the $99.35 re-rating leg is computed by dividing today's EV by management's full $11.2B 2028 plan. That is an assertion that the plan is already in the price. The $92.37 earnings leg is an assertion that it is not — that the Street carries Electrification at $3.27B when the plan needs $4.95B. Both legs are in the same sentence of the same model. Under the re-rating leg's premise the earnings leg is worth −$33.79/share. You cannot pitch both.

The second fatal flaw: the peer comparison is trailing-versus-forward. 23.8x is the peer median on FY2025 EBITDA; 21.4x is GEV on 2028E. "It should re-rate up to the comp median" is exactly backwards.

Three more that each cost real dollars: ~$0.30B of the 2028 Electrification EBITDA ($22.53/share at 20x) is Prolec's 50% that GEV already owned and already booked in Electrification's Other segment income — 10-Q Note 11 shows $104M of it in H1'25 alone, sitting inside the $1,433M FY25 base the case grows from. The $27/share synergy is an unfiled CEO remark that is probably already inside the $5B of Prolec backlog. And "Prolec is tracking ahead, the 2028E $4.2B is being met early" is false — $3.4B annualised is exactly the deck's 2026E.

The structural problem underneath all of it: this is a correct observation about a segment, dressed as a thesis about a stock. Electrification IS compounding, the margin IS expanding, the backlog IS real. None of that is contested by anyone, including the bears — GLJ's Sell at $470 and Bernstein's caution are both entirely about gas vintage margin and slot-reservation conversion. The case identifies the one part of GE Vernova nobody is arguing about and proposes to be long it, inside a wrapper that is 68% something else. The author writes the rebuttal himself: "if the gas thesis cracks the way GLJ argues, Electrification will not rescue the stock."

WHAT TO DO WITH IT. Kill it as a standalone LONG. Keep two pieces. First, the Prolec purchase-accounting runoff — roughly $150M annualised of mechanical 2027 tailwind requiring zero operating improvement — is a clean, filing-sourced, non-consensus detail. It is a supporting paragraph in someone else's pitch, not a thesis. Second, the Q3 margin and book-to-bill tests are worth running on Oct 28 regardless of side, but the thresholds must be reset: the margin test should be >= 20.5% (what the FY guide actually requires of H2), not 19.0%, and the kill should be < 18.0% (the guide floor), not 17.5%. As written the test passes while the model fails.

One process note for the team. The team must choose by Sep 26 and the memo is due Oct 2. The Q3 print is Oct 28 — after the Oct 22-24 finals. Every dated test in this case resolves after the competition is over. Whatever side they pick, they need a catalyst that lands before they present, or they need to say plainly that they are pitching a thesis they will not see tested. Pick the side where the evidence is actually contested — that is gas, not grid.

- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. Kill it as a thesis; keep two paragraphs of it as risk framing inside whatever the team actually pitches.

This is the best-constructed case of the set and it is still wrong, which is the most dangerous kind. The mechanical arithmetic reproduces almost perfectly against the filings - I checked every headline number independently and the author did not fudge a single one. The problem is not the arithmetic, it is that three of the four load-bearing beams are broken in the same direction.

One. The flagship evidence - "management's own H2 guide implies an 83-86% collapse in the deposit engine" - is a methodology with a 0-for-3 record inside twelve months. In January the same subtraction implied $5.25B for all of 2026; the first half alone delivered $9.9B. In April it implied $2.21B for the remaining nine months; Q2 alone delivered $5.11B. The case calls this evidence "assumption-free." It is the opposite: it assumes a guide that has been raised four consecutive times (from $4.5-5.0B, a fact the case's own guidance path omits) will suddenly bind.

Two. The pillar-2 claim that the multi-year cash outlook has "never been raised" is simply false, and I found the contradiction in three separate corpus documents. It went $14B to $22B to $24B in thirteen months. The residual-implies-$4.1B-per-year calculation that the case calls its "independent confirmation" is built on a stale floor whose next scheduled update, per Jefferies, is March 2027 - outside the window in which the case needs it to stay unraised.

Three. The largest single number in the forward model - $14.5B of 2027 liquidation - is computed from a ratio with 63 GW of slot-reservation deposits in the numerator and no corresponding RPO in the denominator, because GEV states in its own 8-K that slot reservations are "not yet in backlog." The case flagged this precise defect in its data gaps, wrote in plain English that it means "my 2027 FCF is too LOW," and published the uncorrected figure regardless. Fixing that one input alone, holding every other assumption of the case constant including its too-low collections number, moves FY27 FCF from $3.0B to $7.0B and cuts the headline in half.

Four. The valuation presents one claim twice and calls the repetition corroboration. Route 1 derates the multiple because cash conversion falls; Route 2 capitalizes the cash that falls. Same dollar, two units, sold as independent bracketing - and Route 2 is calibrated so that the market's "sustainable" $12B at 20x equals 96% of the actual market cap, which forces the answer.

And then the structural point underneath all of it: "earned FCF" is not a defect metric, it is a description of how every long-cycle turbine OEM finances itself. The deposits are non-refundable. The liability is discharged by shipping turbines at a positive margin, not by wiring cash back. When dCL goes to zero, FCF converges toward EBITDA less capex less taxes - roughly $6-8B in 2027 - not to $3B, and the halved sensitivity of -$4.75B is unreachable without GEV either refunding non-refundable money or building at a loss.

What is genuinely true and worth keeping: cash conversion of 3.4x adjusted net income is not a permanent state, the multiple does carry a cash-quality premium that compresses as it normalizes, and the compensation structure - 40% of bonus and 50% of the PSU on an FCF line the float inflates, with no orders or backlog counterweight - is a real governance observation the team should be able to speak to. That is worth about -$95 per share, roughly -10%, implied ~$845. It is a paragraph in a risk section. It is not a short.

The gating problem the team must not walk past: the entire $/share rests on an ASSUMED consensus FY2027 free cash flow of $11.5B that nobody has verified. The case says so itself, in its own first data gap. Do not let anyone size a position - or write two pages - against a number that has never been looked up. If the overnight consensus run comes back at $6-7B, even my reduced gap mostly evaporates and the honest answer is that the cash-quality story is already in the price, at $470 on GLJ's note, since September 14.

Against $250B of market capitalization. Whoever wrote that paragraph found the real thesis and then argued the other side of it.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. Kill it.

This is a well-built case that refutes itself in its own cross-check paragraph, and the corpus it was built from contains the price data that refutes its central premise.

The structural tell comes first. The thesis sentence is about the cash engine; 69% of the dollars ($143.21 of $206.10) come from a 2028 Power margin assumption that has nothing to do with deposits and would be identical if GE Vernova collected no cash in advance at all. The two components that ARE the cash engine total $62.89/share, and both are valuation category errors — component A adds to an observed price a disclosure that price already absorbed on 2026-07-22 (−8.70%, 1.39x volume, peers flat), and component B values the principal of a customer prepayment as if it were retained earnings rather than valuing the float. When the headline and the dollars point at different things, the dollars are telling you where the author's conviction actually is, and it is not in the deposits.

Then the arithmetic. Pillar 2's flagship number — "collections must fall 64.6% before the balance flattens" — holds the release rate constant in dollars against a balance that grew from $17.7B to $40.0B. Releases are 28.95% of the opening balance per half (7,512 on 25,950, H1'26; 39.9% in H1'25, so the rate is DETERIORATING, which is itself bearish). Applied correctly to the $40,037M Jun-30-26 balance, the release run-rate is $23.2B/yr, not $15B, and the threshold is −45.3%, or 44.9 GW/yr of signings. Q3'25 ran 12 GW — 48 GW annualized. The balance flattens on a normalization, not a collapse. The pitch's kill condition #2 sits at 10 GW, less than a quarter of the real threshold: a tripwire strung where nothing walks.

And then the multiple, which is the thing the case cannot answer at any price. It applies 25x to the increment while carrying the base at 34.7x and the target at 42.3x. Run 25x through its own $27.09 of 2028 EPS and you get $677 — twenty-eight percent below spot. There is no version of this model where the author is allowed to be conservative on the margin he is adding and aggressive on the earnings he is adding it to.

Three further things, any one of which I would stop a pitch over. The case's target of $1,146 sits 7.3% BELOW the ~$1,236 street average — a mispricing thesis less bullish than consensus has found no mispricing. The stock re-rated from $711.59 on 2026-01-28 (the day the $24B framework was published) to $1,174.86 on 2026-06-30, +65%, on exactly the framework component C says the market denies. And on 2026-07-22 the market was handed the $6.75B FCF raise and took $93.78 a share out of the stock while Eaton closed up — the revealed price of deposit-driven cash is negative and roughly equal in magnitude to what this case wants to pay for it.

What I will credit: the disclosure discipline is real and unusual. The weakest_link section finds earned free cash flow of $65M for six months on a $250B market cap, names the "$24B cumulative" floor as the bear's cliff, concedes management declined to raise it on two subsequent opportunities, and admits the drawdown is partly an AI-power complex de-rate (VRT fell harder). Five kill conditions, dated tests, a named key assumption with a two-sided sensitivity. That is how the work should be structured. The author simply argued the wrong side of his own evidence — he found the short and wrote the long.

MY RECOMMENDATION TO THE TEAM, for the Sep 26 decision: do not pitch this long. Do not pitch the mirror-image short either — GLJ's $470 requires a margin thesis to fail on contracts already signed, and the corpus has already killed nine bear arguments. What the evidence actually supports is narrower and more defensible: earned cash flow is approximately zero, the contract-liability build is decelerating toward a flattening threshold that arrives on ordinary signing normalization rather than collapse, and the current price already requires management's 2028 framework to be met in full — leaving no compensation for the risk that it is not. That is a short with a defined kill condition (Q3'26 contract liabilities above $46B, or Power margin holding above 19% through Q2'27), and it is roughly $677-$813 versus $940. One warning the team must carry into the room: Q3'26 prints 2026-10-28, six days AFTER the Oct 22-24 finals. Whatever they pitch, they pitch blind to the only observation that settles it — and they should say so from the podium rather than be asked.

THE TARIFF LINE CONTRADICTS THE COMPANY'S OWN ATTRIBUTION. The case's own data_gaps note that the Q2'26 10-Q attributes tariffs to Onshore Wind and calls Power's drag "inflation." The −$80M Power deduction is asserted against the filing.

WHAT DOES SURVIVE: the mechanism is real but small — unit-count intensity (Q2'26 29 units/3.3 GW = 114 MW vs FY25 189 MW), 400 machines installed, ~2,000 production hires, weekend shifts under new US labor contracts, and GEV naming "additional expenses to support capacity investments at Gas" in the 10-Q. STEP 1 — the line: GE Vernova Power segment EBITDA, 2027.

Versus the case's −$257/share. I am at roughly one third of their downside — and a 9% expected move on a name that fell 8.6% in one session and recovered it in four is inside the noise, not an edge. Sizing note for the team: GEV's earnings-day return has matched the sign of its adjusted-EPS surprise every quarter since Q1'25, and the only dated test resolves Oct 28, after the finals.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. This is careful, honest work — the percentage-of-completion demolition of GLJ's vintage argument in weakest_link #1 is better than what GLJ published, and the author killed three of his own arguments before I could. But the case fails on three independent grounds, any one of which is fatal in a Citadel room.

FIRST, the single pillar the author calls "the model" is a seasonal artifact. The 44%→31% H2 deceleration he treats as the ramp signature happened in 2025 too — 46%→31% — with no ramp, and FY25 still printed 38.7% full-year incremental. He never ran the control. Remove that pillar and the 20% assumption has no support; pillars 2-4 are explicitly labelled "decoration" by the author himself.

SECOND, the burden of proof is inverted. The 34.4% incremental the path requires is BELOW FY24's 79%, below FY25's 38.7%, and below FY26's guided 35.5%. The case needs GEV to break a three-year record, not continue a deceleration.

THIRD, and most damaging commercially: this is a published Street number. GLJ printed 18.5% 2027 Power margin on Sep 14. The case arrives at 18.1-18.2%. The stock discounted it by 8.62% that day and took the entire move back within four sessions on rising volume, closing Sep 18 at $940.33 against a $957.27 pre-note close. The market has already heard this argument, priced it, and rejected it.

The shape of the trade condemns it independently, and the author says so: 82% of the return comes from a multiple de-rate that is asserted, not derived — and the 28.7x it starts from is the case's own constructed EBITDA, not consensus. On the real 26.0x, most of that leg evaporates.

My own revised number is −9%, not −27%. That is not a pitch. What the team should take from this: the equipment-margin-realization question is genuinely unobservable in public data (the author flags it as the biggest hole, correctly), so no honest short on 2027 Power margin can be built from this corpus at the conviction a two-page memo demands. The disciplined move is to carry pillar 4's unit-intensity observation and the Oct 28 CSA-revision test into the LONG case as the risk to monitor, and stop trying to make a de-rate short out of a 1.2-point margin disagreement on a name with 116 GW under contract and five years of sold-out capacity.

What the team should keep: the FCF/EBITDA ratio table (1.16x / 2.01x / 0.37x), the corrected earned-FCF bridge, the 2026-07-22 price reaction, and the observation that management's refusal to raise the $24B cumulative is the most informative disclosure in the file. Those are short inputs, built from the long case's own evidence.

Two places I am honestly weak. First, my float valuation ($2.90/share) is as arbitrary as their $37.55 - the defensible statement is "not principal," and the exact spread is a judgment call. Second, I do not have hard consensus 2027-28 FCF, so my 75% haircut on Component C is reasoned from the $1,236 target and the January publication date, not measured. If consensus 2027-28 FCF turns out to be near $4B/yr, my "already priced" argument strengthens; if it is near $10B/yr, the Street is on the bull's side of the $24B question and Component C deserves more credit. That number is worth getting before Sep 26.

CROSS-CHECK 1 — their own target, honestly discounted. $1,090.08 at their own measured 2.032 SPY beta (4% rf + 2.032 x 5% ERP = 14.16%): $836 over 2.0 years, $804 over 2.3 years. At a charitable 9%: $917 and $894. Converges on my range and all of it is below spot.

CROSS-CHECK 2 — the multiple actually being paid. EV $240.115B / FY26E adjusted EBITDA of $5.98B (13% midpoint of the company's unchanged 12-14% guide on $46.0B) = 40.2x. At the June peak it was 50.6x. "21.4x" is a 2028 number chosen because it is the only frame in which GEV looks cheap.

DAMAGE TO THEIR CASE, ITEMISED IN $/SHARE:
- No discounting of a 2028 figure: -$173 at 9%, -$254 at their own beta-implied 14.16%
- Net-cash/float double count: -$39
- Chain A's headline "$234.63 of recoverable de-rating": worth $0, it is algebraically the price decline
- Understated downside (16.5% margin at 18x is $663, not their $906): -$243 of unacknowledged risk
Net: their $1,090 becomes ~$765. That is -$325/share, 34.6% of the $940.33 price.

WHAT WOULD MAKE ME REVISE UP: a Q3 print on Oct 28 showing Power segment margin above 20% — not the 17% guidance floor they set as their kill condition, but the level the 2028 bridge actually requires. At 20%+ in either segment for two consecutive quarters, the 25% terminal assumption stops being unprecedented and I would move my base to $850-900. Nothing in H1'26 supports it; 18.86% is the record.

HONEST POINT AGAINST MY OWN NUMBER: my FY27E of $7.4-8.2B is interpolated or borrowed from GLJ, who is the most bearish voice on the tape and has an obvious incentive. The overnight consensus run must firm this up — if street 2027 EBITDA is above $9B, my base moves to roughly $845 and the gap to spot narrows to -10%, which is a pass rather than a short. My valuation is only as good as that one number, and I do not yet have it.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. This is a well-sourced piece of research attached to a valuation that inverts under its own inputs.

What is genuinely good, and the team should keep it: the guidance correction (Power was raised to 18-20% on Jul 22; the brief's 16-18% is stale), the comps_inputs EV bug (mcap + debt, no cash deducted — $253.235B should be $240.115B, and every EV metric anyone pulls from that table is 5.5% hot), the segment margin reconstruction, which reproduces exactly, and the residual finding that ex-July-22 the GEV-specific residuals sum to +0.24pp. That last one is real, replicable work.

It is also the reason the case dies. If the drawdown is a factor move, there is no idiosyncratic mispricing — going long GEV here is buying the AI-power complex with a 2.03 market beta, which is a thematic bet, not a pitch. And the single day that IS idiosyncratic is the earnings print, where the market voted -8.69% on a release that raised revenue 2.2%, reaffirmed adjusted EBITDA margin at 12-14%, reaffirmed Power margin at 17-19%, and raised cash guidance $5B on customer down payments that the CFO attributed to a $6.4B working-capital benefit. Q2 free cash flow ex-working-capital was about -$1.3B. Not one profit line went up. Pillar 2 asserts the market irrationally sold a guidance raise; the market rationally sold a raise with no earnings in it. That is the short thesis, printed in the long case's own exhibit.

Then the valuation. The headline number in Chain A — "$234.63/share of de-rating, 24.9% of price" — is algebraically identical to $1,174.86 minus $940.33, because holding debt and cash fixed makes the EV change equal the market-cap change. It is the price decline wearing a multiple. The target itself is 25x a 2028 EBITDA figure discounted at zero, while the case's own regression hands me a 2.03 beta; discount $1,090 at the implied 14.16% and it is $804-836, and even at 9% it is $894-917. Both below spot. The case is a short at its own numbers. The float is counted twice — once as a balance-sheet achievement in Pillar 4, again as $38.77/share of net cash in Chain A. And the sensitivity that produces the marketed -3.6%/+55.1% asymmetry holds the multiple fixed at 25x while flexing margins, which contradicts Pillar 1's own account of how the money was lost; flex both and the downside is $663.

Underneath all of it sits an assumption the case never writes down. Twenty percent in 2028, net of Wind and corporate, is Power and Electrification at roughly 25% segment margin. The best quarters this company has ever printed are 18.86% and 18.61%, both last quarter, and its own guidance caps them at 19% and 20%. The case leans on "it is management's own number" and stops there — and then concedes it cannot rebut GLJ on the 2027 vintage trough that sits directly on the path to it.

For a 3-12 month horizon the structural problem is decisive: GLJ models 2027 EBITDA at $7.42B, the long case's own CAGR implies $8.19B, and the two sides are ~10% apart on the only forward year inside the window. The entire argument is about 2028. Meanwhile the base target of $1,090 is below Baird's $1,400, Bernstein's $1,298, Jefferies' $1,185 and the $1,145.83 tracked average — a long less bullish than the consensus it is arguing alongside, on a name already rated Buy by ~37 analysts. The one dated test, Oct 28, lands after the Oct 22-24 finals, so it cannot even inform the pitch.

For the team's decision on Sep 26: do not take this side on this reasoning. The work product to salvage is the factor decomposition and the EV correction. If the team goes LONG anyway, it must be on a thesis the market cannot already read off an 8-K — and it must use a forward year inside the horizon, a real discount rate, and a segment-level margin bridge, none of which this case has.

- **killer_question**: "GE Vernova shipped 5.2 gigawatts in the second quarter of 2025 — before a single one of your 400 machines was installed, before the 1,500 workers, before most of the $600 million. Your thesis sentence calls a 5 GW quarter the moment the promise becomes audited, your dated test sets the bar at 4.8 GW, and your kill condition is 4.2. Step 1 — volume increment. Accept theirs: FY26E 17.5 GW (H1 actual 7.5 + guided 5 + 5) to FY28E 24 GW = +6.5 GW. This is GEV's own guided figure (2026-07-22 release, "24 GW in 2028").
Step 2 — revenue per GW. Use $420/kW, the FY25 actual (equipment $6,420M / 15.3 GW, 10-K acc. 0001996810-26-000015), NOT H1'26's $513. Justification: $513 is an aeroderivative-mix artifact — equipment revenue per shipped UNIT fell 4.8% YoY while GW per unit fell 32%. A 24 GW FY28 requires the HA-heavy mix of FY25 (0.189 GW/unit), so it prices at FY25's $/kW. 6.5 GW x $420M = $2,730M of annual revenue.
Step 3 — incremental EBITDA margin. Use 15%, not 35%. The observed 35-44% Power incrementals are blended and services-driven; this slice is pure equipment, whose disclosed best-vintage margin is 10-11 points. 15% is already generous. $2,730M x 0.15 = $410M of annual EBITDA.
Step 4 — multiple. Use 21.3x, not 25x. That is where GEV's own EV ($238.4B) already trades against its guided 2028 adjusted EBITDA ($11.2B). $410M x 21.3 = $8,723M of enterprise value.
Step 5 — per share. $8,723M / 266,333,581 = $32.75 per share = 3.5% of $940.33. (At the filed 270M diluted count: $32.31, 3.4%.)

Sensitivity, which is what actually matters here: HALVED (+3.25 GW) = $16.38/sh, 1.7%. DOUBLED (+13 GW, the 2030 target pulled into 2028) = $65.50/sh, 7.0%. Even the doubled case does not pay for the 20% drawdown. The assumption doing the most work is no longer volume — it is the 15% equipment incremental margin. At their 35% the base is $76.42/sh; at 10% it is $21.83. The margin-vintage question moves the answer roughly twice as much as the volume question does, which is precisely why GLJ and Bernstein are arguing about margin and not about factories.

THE ONLY VALUATION THAT MATTERS: value the whole stream once, on the company's own guidance, and discount it. 2028 adjusted EBITDA $11.2B x 25x (their multiple) + $12B net cash = $292B equity / 266.33M = $1,096 per share in December 2028. Discounted at 10% over 2.28 years = $882 per share TODAY. Against a $940.33 spot, that is -6.2% for flawless execution of guidance. To justify $940.33 today you must underwrite roughly 27x 2028 EBITDA, or roughly $1,175 in 2028. To justify their $1,105 twelve-month target you must pay 25x an EBITDA number two years forward with zero discounting.

Net: the capacity ramp is real, it is physically installed, and it is worth about $33 per share of identifiable incremental EBITDA value — all of which the company guided on 2026-01-28, which the market bid up 15.6% and gave back inside five sessions, and which is already capitalized in a $238B enterprise value at 21.3x the fully-ramped number. As a LONG thesis the ramp is the price of admission, not the edge. The honest read of this work is that it is a well-built confirmation of consensus that arrives at a target 11% below the street's.
- **verdict**: DOES NOT SURVIVE. Kill it as a standalone LONG.

This is careful, well-sourced, intellectually honest work — the HA backlog roll-forward is genuinely good, the unit tables are exact, and the weakest_link section is more candid than most sell-side. It still fails on all three tests a PM applies.

ARITHMETIC: fails. Not the computation — the inputs. The $513/kW conversion factor is an aeroderivative-mix artifact (equipment revenue per shipped unit FELL 4.8% YoY while GW per unit fell 32%), and it is then held flat into a year the case itself argues will be HA-heavy, which is internally contradictory. The 35% incremental margin is a blended, services-driven number applied to a pure-equipment revenue slice whose disclosed margin is 10-11 points. And 25x is called "a 37% haircut" by comparing it to a trough-2026 multiple when the stream being valued is 2028, on which the stock already trades at 21.3x — a period mismatch that inverts the direction of the conservatism claim. The twelve-month target is a 2028 fair value with no discounting; present-valued properly it is $882, below spot.

EVIDENCE: fails, and it fails on the case's own primary sources. The CFO sentence immediately following the one they quote from sources.id=3161 attributes the higher dollar-per-kW to "a higher mix of aeroderivatives versus heavy-duty gas turbines and incremental combined cycle equipment" and puts real pricing at 10-20 points. Pillar 3 derives +67% and calls it price. Management says mix, in the same document, in the next paragraph. Separately, the filed Power unit table shows Q2'25 shipped 5.2 GW — so the thesis sentence's "first 5 GW quarter prints on October 28" is false, and the dated test's 4.8 GW bar and the 4.2 GW kill condition are both set below a level achieved fifteen months earlier with none of the capex.

ALREADY PRICED: fails decisively. Every element of Pillar 1 is a press release. The $56B / 20% / 24 GW 2028 frame was published 2026-01-28, the market paid +15.6% for it the next day and reversed the entire move within five sessions, and the stock today already carries 21.3x that fully-ramped guided EBITDA. The case's own FY28 bottom-up (~$8.9B) is 20% BELOW company guidance ($11.2B), and its $1,105 target is 11% below the ~$1,236 street average. You cannot claim a variant view while producing a number less bullish than both the company and the consensus.

WHAT THE TEAM SHOULD TAKE FROM THIS. Three things survive and are worth keeping. (1) The HA backlog roll-forward — 70 unshipped HA units in firm RPO, cross-checked against the "195 under contract" figure — is the single most useful piece of original work in the package and belongs in the model regardless of side. (2) The revenue-per-unit series I re-derived (FY23 $60.8M, FY24 $73.5M, FY25 $79.3M, H1'26 $71.3M) is the mix-neutral metric the whole shipped-GW debate should be conducted in, and it points the other way. (3) The observation that percentage-of-completion decouples revenue from shipped GW is correct and important — it just cuts against a model whose entire volume line is denominated in shipped GW.

If the team wants GEV long, the argument has to be about equipment margin vintage and slot-reservation conversion economics, because that is the debate the 20% drawdown is actually about. The factories are not in dispute. Do not put "underappreciated" in the memo without a sell-side shipped-GW number in hand, and do not put the $185/share figure in front of a judge — the mix correction alone takes the headline down 18% before anyone asks about the multiple.

WHY IT DIES.

1. THE CROSS-CHECK IS AN ARTIFACT. $24.50 of EPS and $7.5B of EBITDA describe two different companies. Reconciled to one base, the EV/EBITDA route gives $807-912, not $650-734. The line "two independent routes bracket the same place" is the case's persuasive core and it is a coincidence of two incompatible assumptions. A PM will find this in ninety seconds, and once he does he will not believe the other numbers either — which is unfair, because the other numbers are fine.

2. THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT SELF-CONSISTENT. Entergy is 19.5 GW when removing it from GEV's market and 10.2 GW when sizing that market. Fermi America's 7.6 GW sits fully in the denominator and 1.1 GW in the numerator. The denominator jumped 39.6 -> 51.1 GW in a single month on a 134-plant coverage change that the case reads as market growth. Three separate ways the share number moves several points on a methodology choice rather than a fact.

3. IT IS SEVENTEEN MONTHS OLD AND HAS COST 146%. Every pillar is a public filing, a management quote on an open call, or a Bloomberg-sourced sell-side tally. GEV has risen from $382.29 to $940.33 across four upward amendments of the Entergy agreement. And the sharper version of the thesis — GLJ at $470 — was published nine days ago, after which the stock rallied 7.5%. There is no non-consensus fact here. There is a non-consensus INTERPRETATION, which is a different and much weaker product.

4. IT PAYS NOTHING IN THE HORIZON, AND THE CASE SAYS SO. $8.67/share of earnings impact, under 1% of price, against equipment revenue recognised over time on already-booked orders. The Oct 2 memo and the Oct 28 print land before a single dollar of this moves. The kill conditions are well-built but three of the five resolve after Oct 28 and the fourth (EIA monthly attribution) re-runs a script whose methodology I have just shown swings 8 points on a treatment choice.

5. IT ARGUES AGAINST ITSELF. "Only 20% data centers, only 45.6% US" is the reason GEV survives an AI capex pause. The case offers the bull's best durability argument as its own third pillar.

WHAT TO TELL THE TEAM. Do not pitch this as a SHORT. The genuinely valuable output of this run is a RISK SECTION for whichever side they take, and one specific research task that is free and unexhausted: the state PUC/CPCN dockets (MO PSC EFIS, KCC, IURC, TCEQ, OK CC, ND PSC) that would attribute the missing 18-24 GW. If that work moves GEV's attributed share to 45%+, it is a LONG datapoint; if it holds at 30%, they have something the street genuinely does not — but they will still need an earnings line for it, and on tonight's evidence there isn't one inside twelve months. Run the same discipline against the LONG and see which side survives its own audit. Given the Sep 23 date and a Sep 26 decision, that is two days well spent.

One process note for the team, unrelated to the merits: the packet's own data_gaps list the 2027 consensus EPS as the highest-value missing input, then the model uses a range midpoint and reports two-decimal outputs off it. Get the firm number before anyone writes anything.
